jobs.title: Director, Product Development
jobs.description:
The Director, Product Development leads Domino's innovation agenda from consumer insight through commercialization. This role oversees Product Marketing and Research & Development to build a robust pipeline of menu innovation, product optimization, and strategic growth platforms that drive sales, profitability, and brand differentiation. The position combines consumer-centric marketing and culinary innovation, using research, data, and cross-functional collaboration to identify opportunities, develop business cases, and launch products that are consumer-relevant, operationally executable, and financially sound. The role also leads the Domino's Global Product Innovation Council to connect international innovation efforts, accelerate learning, and identify scalable opportunities.

What You'll Do

• Innovation strategy and pipeline leadership: Develop and execute the innovation roadmap; maintain a multi-year pipeline aligned with enterprise growth objectives that delivers at least three product innovations and at least one renovation each year; identify consumer, food, technology, and cultural trends; set priorities and resource allocation; shape menu strategy, portfolio architecture, and product lifecycle management with executive leadership; maintain supplier relationships; and optimize innovation processes from consumer-driven ideas through commercialization.
• Product Marketing leadership: Lead Product Marketing strategy for innovation, renovation, and optimization; develop customer value propositions for products, platforms, and promotions; align initiatives with brand, sales, and marketing objectives; oversee business cases, forecasting assumptions, launch recommendations, and post-launch evaluations with Decision Science; lead portfolio and menu management, including additions, renovations, simplification, and SKU optimization; and partner with Operations and the OpAC franchisee council to build system buy-in and support system launches.
• Research & Development leadership: Lead the R&D function in designing, developing, testing, and commercializing products and menu platforms; ensure innovation meets standards for quality, profitability, scalability, and operational simplicity; improve core menu items through renovation and optimization; partner with Quality Assurance, Operations, Supply Chain, and Procurement; champion a disciplined stage-gate process; and oversee product testing, operational readiness, and national launch execution.
• Global Product Innovation Council leadership: Establish strategic priorities and governance for product innovation across international markets; chair council meetings; connect global marketing, culinary, operations, and innovation leaders; evaluate global concepts for scalability and commercialization; formalize sharing of best practices, consumer learnings, and product performance; build a globally informed pipeline; assess standardization, regional adaptation, and local innovation opportunities; establish scorecards and reporting; and serve as the liaison between U.S. innovation teams and international markets.
• Consumer insights and learning: Partner with Analytics & Insights on research agendas and consumer learning plans; use quantitative and qualitative research, sales data, behavioral trends, and market intelligence to guide innovation and portfolio strategy; translate consumer, category, and competitive insights into product opportunities; document successes and failures to strengthen organizational learning; and manage internal sensory capabilities for development and consumer qualification.
• Cross-functional leadership and execution: Serve as executive sponsor for major innovation programs and national launches; lead cross-functional teams through concept development, testing, readiness, and commercialization; align Marketing, Operations, Technology, Supply Chain, Finance, Franchisees, Decision Science, and International teams; balance consumer appeal, operational feasibility, and franchisee economics; and drive execution and business outcomes.
• Talent leadership and organizational development: Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing Product Marketing and R&D team, including Senior Managers; foster innovation, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement; create development and succession plans; build capabilities in consumer-led innovation, commercialization, product strategy, and portfolio management; and promote cross-functional learning and knowledge sharing.

What You’ll Bring

In addition to the technical and functional requirements of this role, successful candidates demonstrate Domino's Hungry for MORE Ways of Working:

Be Curious

• Seeks clarity, asks thoughtful questions, and uncovers root causes to solve problems effectively.
• Actively pursues learning opportunities, applies feedback, and continuously develops new skills.

Connect the Dots

• Uses information and insights to identify opportunities and drive informed decisions.
• Builds strong partnerships across teams and considers the broader organizational impact of decisions.

Aim High

• Sets ambitious goals, challenges the status quo, and focuses on work that drives meaningful business results.
• Uses feedback and data to continuously improve performance and outcomes.

Shift Fast

• Adapts quickly to changing priorities and business needs while maintaining focus on results.
• Demonstrates resilience, sound judgment, and the ability to learn from setbacks.

Deliver More

• Takes ownership, executes with discipline, and consistently produces measurable results.
• Identifies opportunities to create additional value for customers, team members, and the business.

Leadership Expectations

• Builds and develops high-performing teams aligned to Domino's Ways of Working.
• Creates accountability, fosters collaboration, and delivers results through others.
• Leads confidently through change while maintaining team engagement and performance.
• Demonstrates enterprise thinking and drives cross-functional alignment to achieve business goals.

• Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Business, Food Science, Product Development, or related field.
• 12+ years of progressive experience in Product Marketing, Innovation, R&D, Brand Management, Product Development, or related disciplines.
• Minimum 7 years of leadership experience managing high-performing teams.
• Experience leading cross-functional innovation programs from concept through commercialization.
• Strong analytical capability with demonstrated use of consumer research and business analytics.
• Proven ability to influence stakeholders across multiple functions and organizational levels.
• Excellent communication, storytelling, and executive presentation skills.

Preferred Qualifications

• MBA or advanced degree in Business, Marketing, Food Science, or related field.
• QSR, restaurant, foodservice, or consumer packaged goods experience.
• Experience scaling innovation across franchise or multi-unit operating systems.
• Deep understanding of consumer behavior, menu economics, portfolio strategy, and product commercialization.
• Experience working with stage-gate innovation and product development processes.

Benefits:

• Paid Holidays and Vacation
• Medical, Dental & Vision benefits that start on the first day of employment
• No-cost mental health support for employee and dependents
• Childcare tuition discounts
• No-cost fitness, nutrition, and wellness programs
• Fertility benefits
• Adoption assistance
• 401k matching contributions
• 15% off the purchase price of stock
• Company bonus

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

jobs.title: Senior Cloud Infrastructure Engineer
jobs.description:
CHAOS Industries is redefining modern defense with omniscient systems purpose-built for today’s realities. Designed and built by top U.S. military veterans and Silicon Valley innovators, CHAOS Industries’ products are powered by Coherent Distributed Networks (CDN™), empowering warfighters, commercial air operators, and border protection teams to act faster, adapt rapidly, and stay ahead of evolving threats. In a world where technological threats move at unprecedented speed, CHAOS Industries delivers advanced sensing and detection solutions that give the ultimate advantage: time.

CHAOS Industries was founded in 2022 and has raised $1B in total funding from leading investors including 8VC, Accel, and NEA. The company is headquartered in Los Angeles, with offices in Washington, D.C., San Francisco, and London. For more information, please visit www.chaosinc.com.

The Role

You'll join a small, highly collaborative team in San Francisco building the cloud platform behind some of the world's most advanced radar systems. You'll design, build, and operate both the infrastructure and the backend services that move mission-critical sensor data from radars in the field to the operators who depend on it. The platform is in production and growing fast, and your job is to scale it as our fleet of sensors, customers, and deployments grows.

What You'll Build

• Cloud Infrastructure - design and operate our Azure infrastructure as code with Terraform: networking, Azure Container Apps, managed databases, and the CI/CD pipelines that deploy to them.
• Backend Platform Services - build and own high-throughput Python (FastAPI) services and the data layer behind them (PostgreSQL/TimescaleDB, Redis, Cosmos DB) that ingest and stream real-time sensor data.
• Platform Architecture - work with engineering teams across the company to define the architecture of the next generation of the platform.
• Operations - own security, reliability, and observability across the platform: identity and access, secrets management, network isolation, monitoring and alerting (Datadog), and incident response.

What We're Looking For

• Have built and operated production infrastructure in at least one major cloud - Azure, AWS, or GCP - defined in code with Terraform, Pulumi, Bicep, or CloudFormation.
• Have run containerized production workloads (Docker) on a managed platform such as Azure Container Apps, AWS ECS or Fargate, Google Cloud Run, or Kubernetes.
• Have strong cloud networking fundamentals: virtual networks, subnets, routing, DNS, load balancers, private endpoints, and firewalls.
• Have built and operated production backend services in Python, Go, or a similar language, and understand what happens under load - concurrency, async I/O, connection pooling, and resource limits.
• Are fluent in distributed systems: consistency and replication, partitioning, caching, back-pressure, idempotency, and how systems fail - and how to design so that they degrade gracefully.
• Have scaled a production system well beyond its original design, and fixed what broke on the way.
• Build securely by default - least-privilege access, secrets kept out of code, and patched, hardened systems - and can explain the trade-offs behind those choices.

Experience in any of the following is a plus:

• Azure Government, AWS GovCloud, or other regulated environments (FedRAMP, CMMC, NIST 800-171 or 800-53).
• Real-time and streaming data systems: WebSockets, server-sent events, pub/sub, and message queues.
• Identity and cloud security: Entra ID, OAuth 2.0 / OIDC, managed identities, service-to-service authentication, and policy as code.

The Medical Director I performs comprehensive in-person assessments and coordinates with the IDT to develop an individualized care plan for each participant. At the direction of the Medical Director II, this role oversees all participant care in nursing homes and hospitals, including admits and discharges for acute, short-term, and long-term placement, and the use of medical specialists to ensure effective care coordination. The Medical Director I also provides direction and support to Nurse Practitioners and other members of the IDT.

This role is different because the Medical Director I at WelbeHealth:

• Has the unique opportunity to lead in a PACE center in a mission-driven organization, shaping the culture and building the clinical team

• Spends ample time engaging with, forming long-term relationships with, and truly caring for participants in a value-based model

• Growth opportunities

On the day-to-day, you will:

• Provide assessments, planning, primary care, and continuous medical coverage to participants

• Collaborate with community-based physicians and the IDT in discharge planning from acute or long-term settings

As a Buyer II, you will independently manage procurement execution across assigned suppliers and commodities while ensuring material availability to support engineering builds and production. You will serve as the primary point of contact for supplier execution activities and proactively manage delivery performance, shortages, and supply continuity.

This role will primarily support electronics commodities including custom printed circuit board assemblies (PCBAs), cable harnesses, sensors, connectors, and related electronic assemblies. You will work closely with Global Supply Managers (GSMs), Planning, Engineering, Manufacturing, and Finance to ensure procurement activities are executed effectively and supplier commitments align with business needs.

jobs.title: Brand Partnerships Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.




ABOUT THE ROLE 

Ramp is hiring a Brand Partnerships Manager to shape and accelerate our growth through strategic partnerships and collaborations.

You’ll build our brand partnerships strategy from the ground up: sourcing high-potential partners, developing relationships, structuring creative collaborations, and turning them into campaigns that drive awareness, engagement, and business growth.

Success in this role looks like building real, high-impact partnerships with tangible value for Ramp, our partners, and the audiences we reach together. The ideal candidate is a marketer who can also run a deal: you come up with the partnership, you know why it matters for the business, and you execute relentlessly to get it out the door. You should have an instinct for great ideas, a strong creative point of view, and a close read on what’s happening across media, sports, and culture. Most importantly, you’ve turned those ideas into campaigns that break through culture, get attention, and drive business outcomes.

Ramp is a place for people who move fast, take ownership, and are looking to do the best work of their careers. We want someone who can build this function out, bet on partners that matter, and create collaborations that move the needle and are unmistakably Ramp.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own Ramp’s brand partnerships program end to end: partner strategy, sourcing, negotiation, and execution.

 - Find high-value partners across finance, sports, business, and media who can put Ramp in front of new audiences.

 - Build a system for spotting and tracking emerging talent so we can place smart bets early. We sponsored Neal Shipley while he was still an amateur golfer, and TBPN in the very early days. We like spotting emerging brands and talent before everyone else does.

 - Develop bold partnership concepts that tie into Ramp’s brand, product priorities, launches, and broader marketing campaigns.

 - Lead deal strategy and negotiation, including pricing, asset packages, usage rights, exclusivity, deliverables, timelines, and contract terms.

 - Work with teams across Ramp to run and test campaigns across paid, owned, and earned channels, so every partnership delivers both creative impact and business results.

 - Manage active partnerships day to day. Keep deliverables on track, and keep finding new ways to work with existing partners so Ramp gets the most out of every relationship.

 - Work closely with Ramp’s sales team to spot deals where a partner could help, and find timely, relevant ways to bring them in.

WHAT YOU NEED

 - A track record of developing, negotiating, and executing high-profile brand, media, or strategic partnerships, ideally within a fast moving in-house team or at an agency. The ideal candidate has a builder mindset and is willing to challenge conventional approaches and take a first principles approach.

 - Strong creative judgment, with the ability to spot culturally relevant ideas and turn them into partnerships and campaigns that earn attention.

 - The ability to thrive in ambiguity, take initiative, and launch new programs quickly from scratch You can move from strategy to execution quickly, manage complexity, and drive work across teams.

 - Excel at balancing brand authenticity with performance metrics. Strong business acumen and judgment to balance efficiency with bold bets.

 - Ability to switch between strategy and in-the-weeds execution. In one meeting, you’re zooming out to set the vision and framework, the next you’re diving into day-to-day execution and delivery.

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Extensibility Platform
jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About our organization

The Developer Experience & Product Platform (DEeP) organization empowers all of Stripe's products with a shared product platform that delivers high-quality, consistent, cross-product experiences across our UI and API surfaces. DEeP focuses on providing a scalable developer experience that any developer can leverage to accelerate a customer's ability to create value from Stripe.

Within DEeP, the Extensibility program is how Stripe expands its total addressable market, and increases customer retention. With extensibility, Stripe becomes programmable — customers and product teams can adapt Stripe to their needs on a common platform.

Stripe has three interconnected extensibility primitives:

• Scripts — Secure, isolated TypeScript runtime allowing merchants and developers to customize Stripe product behavior (e.g., discount calculations, invoice logic, proration).

• Custom Objects — User-defined data models (e.g., Shipments, Locations, Warranties, Entitlements) with first-class APIs, SDKs, and Dashboard experiences.

• Workflows — A programmable orchestration layer (graduating to GA at Sessions) enabling no-code and pro-code business logic across Stripe, including custom actions, delays, smart retries, and 3P integrations.

These primitives are deeply interdependent, involve 10+ cross-functional teams and culminate in a flagship product launch.

What you’ll do

We are seeking a product-focused Technical Program Manager to drive the Extensibility program across the Workflows, Custom Objects, and Scripts workstreams. This is a newly created, high-impact role at the intersection of platform engineering, product management, and cross-organizational program ownership.

In this role, you will own one of the most strategically consequential programs in DEeP — driving the direction, health, and outcomes of Stripe's Extensibility platform across Scripts, Custom Objects, and Workflows. You will set the program strategy in partnership with DEeP leadership, holding organizations accountable to the success of the program.

• Drive cross-org decisions across DRIs in Script Platform, Custom Objects, Apps, SDK, Observability, DevEx, and Versioning — actively resolving the hard, ambiguous integration and ownership questions that fall between team boundaries.

• Own the critical path to major launches — proactively shaping scope, driving descope decisions, and negotiating trade-offs across teams so that launches reflect deliberate strategic choices.

• Influence and shape product and engineering roadmaps — bringing a program-level perspective to team planning cycles, pushing back where individual team roadmaps are misaligned with broader extensibility strategy, and advocating for cross-cutting investments that no single team will prioritize on their own.

• Support ProServ and Partnerships — Ensure ProServ and Partnerships requirements are surfaced into the roadmap with the same rigor as product requirements, and hold the bridge between what the platform delivers and what those teams need to close and serve complex customers.

Qualifications

Minimum requirements

• 5+ years of technical program management experience with demonstrated success in driving complex cross organizational programs.

• Strong product sense and ability to understand enterprise customer needs

• Demonstrated ability to communicate with precision and credibility across engineering, product, and executive audiences, translating complex technical trade-offs into strategic decisions, and driving alignment.

• Demonstrated ability to lead and align cross-functional teams — driving decisions, resolving conflict, and building consensus across organizations with competing priorities

• Proven track record of successful program delivery in complex technical environments

• Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience

Preferred Qualifications

• Background in product management or product operations Experience with developer platforms, API products, or payment systems

jobs.title: Legal Counsel
jobs.description:
ABOUT ANTITHESIS

We build a platform that finds the bugs other testing approaches never see. Antithesis runs your entire system inside a deterministic simulation, breaks it in every way we can think of, and hands you a root cause with a perfect reproduction — no flaky tests, no false positives, no "works on my machine." Engineering teams debug faster and ship with far more confidence.

AI-generated code has made this work more urgent than ever. Agents write code faster than any human can, but faster code isn’t better code if it’s buggy, stuck in review, or quietly failing in production. The verification bottleneck is real, and it’s growing. That is precisely the problem Antithesis exists to solve. We’ve spent years quietly rethinking how the world approaches software reliability, and we’re just getting started.

We’re well-funded, deeply technical, and headquartered in Northern Virginia with satellite offices in London, San Francisco, and Singapore. Our team is in the office daily, which is how we take on hard problems together. If that sounds like fun to you, keep reading.



ABOUT THE ROLE

Antithesis is looking for a Legal Counsel to serve as a key legal partner to the business as we grow. In this role, you will support vendor and customer contracting, lead the company’s privacy work, support our international subsidiaries, and build the internal policies that help the company scale responsibly.

This role is well suited for someone who enjoys working at the intersection of law, product, and business strategy, and who likes covering a broad range of matters. You should be comfortable handling commercial and privacy issues, partnering with senior stakeholders, and balancing speed, judgment, and rigor in a fast-moving environment.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Vendor contracting: Review and negotiate vendor and procurement agreements, including software, cloud infrastructure, and professional services contracts, partnering with finance to build processes to keep purchasing moving

 - Customer contracts: Draft, review, and negotiate customer agreements, including SaaS agreements, order forms and related amendments, and advise sales and finance on deal structure, risk allocation, and negotiation strategy

 - Regulatory and Compliance: Lead the company’s privacy work including policies and review of vendor terms; advise on regulatory and compliance matters impacting the company

 - International subsidiaries: Support the company’s international subsidiaries on commercial, corporate, and local compliance matters, coordinating with outside counsel in the relevant jurisdictions

 - Internal policies: Draft, maintain, and roll out internal policies, and help employees understand and apply them in their day-to-day work

 - Create and refine templates, playbooks, and approval paths that bring consistency and speed to recurring contract and privacy issues

 - Provide business-focused legal advice on general corporate matters that enables thoughtful decision-making across the company



WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Customer deals move at the pace the business needs, without the company taking on risk it didn’t understand or intend

 - Vendor contracts are turned around promptly, with privacy, security, and liability terms that protect the company

 - International subsidiaries stay in good standing and get responsive, practical legal support

 - Employees have clear, practical internal policies that they understand and follow

 - Stakeholders across the company treat Legal as a partner that helps them get to yes in a manner that protects the company, not a checkpoint to route around




WHAT YOU BRING

 - J.D. and active bar membership in good standing in at least one U.S. jurisdiction (see Virginia requirement below)

 - 5-10 combined years of experience at a top tier law firm or in-house.

 - Significant experience handling commercial transactions, with a strong mix of vendor-side and customer-facing contracting

 - Hands-on experience with privacy matters, such as privacy policies, data processing agreements, and vendor privacy review, along with working knowledge of frameworks like GDPR, UK GDPR, and U.S. state privacy laws

 - Experience supporting international subsidiaries or cross-border matters, including managing outside counsel abroad, is a plus

 - Experience drafting and implementing internal company policies

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills

 - Ability to work independently while collaborating closely with cross-functional partners

 - Strong attention to detail without losing sight of the broader business context



YOU MAY BE A GREAT FIT IF

 - You’re willing to roll up your sleeves, take on new challenges and pitch in where needed

 - You can distinguish between theoretical risk and real business risk

 - You enjoy being a close partner to sales, finance, and operational teams

 - You are comfortable moving between a customer negotiation, a privacy question, and a subsidiary matter in the same day

 - You like designing repeatable legal processes, not just handling one-off matters

 - You thrive in roles that require both sound legal analysis and strong commercial instincts




LICENSING REQUIREMENT

Candidates should be barred in Virginia or able to qualify as a Part I Corporate Counsel in Virginia.

jobs.title: Medical Learning Designer
jobs.description:
MISSION

Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear. 

In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives.



Neko Health is changing how clinicians and operators learn, and we are hiring a designer to lead it. You will turn deep clinical expertise into learning that works, from curriculum design to virtual practice environments built with Engineering.

Reports to: Head of Medical Education and Training | Team: Medex, Medical Education | Role type: Individual contributor

About the role

Today, learning content is built in the gaps between other jobs, and the same material often exists in several versions. This role changes that. You will be the single production engine for Neko's clinical and operator learning: deciding how things are best learned, building them, and making each new asset faster to make than the last. The curriculum, the asset library and the production process are still to be created, so this is a builder role.

What you will do

 - Design curriculum and programs for every Neko clinical population, writing learning objectives in observable performance terms.

 - Build learning assets across e-learning, video, job aids and facilitator guides, modular so a protocol change updates a component rather than triggering a rebuild.

 - Own the asset library, including its taxonomy and when assets are retired.

 - Write the learning requirement for virtual practice environments and validate that what Engineering builds teaches what it should.

 - Design assessments, including rubrics, checklists and observation tools, that two assessors can apply consistently.

 - Draw expertise out of clinicians and operators, and shadow clinical teams so your designs reflect real practice.

 - Evaluate whether learning changed practice, using assessment and quality data rather than completion figures, and improve or retire what is not working.

 - Administer our learning systems and maintain an auditable training record for every clinician and operator, including the protocol version they are trained to.

Requirements

 - 6+ years in instructional or learning design, with ownership of design decisions rather than production alone, and a portfolio of products you built.

 - 4+ years applying adult learning and competency-based design, and explaining why a design choice serves the objective.

 - 4+ years authoring e-learning, video and written materials with current industry tools.

 - 3+ years designing assessment, including rubrics and observation instruments, not only knowledge checks.

 - 3+ years working with subject matter experts to turn their knowledge into accurate, learnable content.

 - 2+ years writing requirements for a technical team and seeing them through to a working product.

 - 2+ years working with learning platforms and how content is packaged, delivered and tracked.

 - Practical, curious and quick to prototype: you would rather put a rough version in front of ten learners next week than a polished one in three months, and you build things others can maintain.

Nice to have

 - Experience in healthcare, medical device or another regulated environment where content is reviewed before release.

 - Experience designing simulation or scenario-based learning, including the debrief around it.

 - Experience designing for localization and accessibility in digital learning.

 - A qualification in instructional design, learning technology or education.

jobs.title: Assistant City Solicitor or Deputy City Solicitor – Health and Adult Services Unit
jobs.description:
The attorney will play a critical role in representing City social and health-related city entities that serve the adult residents of Philadelphia. The attorney will be responsible for independently managing a large caseload of affirmative litigation in mental health civil commitment hearings, as well as a smaller number of lead code violation complaints. The attorney will also defend the City in administrative appeals arising from agency decisions. Attorneys in the HAS Unit handle their cases from inception through disposition. The successful candidate will possess superior oral advocacy skills, excellent legal research and writing skills, and a demonstrated commitment to seeking input, clarifying uncertainties, and sharing knowledge with other members of the team. Additional responsibilities for this position include reviewing, responding to, and potentially litigating subpoenas; interviewing witnesses; meeting with clients; drafting pleadings and motions; and conducting legal research.

Essential Functions

The functions listed below are intended to describe the general nature and level of work performed in this role. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or essential functions. Duties may be modified, assigned, or reassigned as operational needs evolve, consistent with applicable law.

Advise and represent the City of Philadelphia before government agencies and ,judicial forums.

Autonomously litigate fast-paced, high-volume cases from inception to resolution which will include researching cases, preparing witness testimony, orchestrating client meetings, developing case theories, and crafting closing arguments.

Cultivate familiarity with Pennsylvania Mental Health Procedures Act of 1976, Disease Prevention and Control Law of 1955, Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966, Drug and Alcohol Abuse Control Act, Confidentiality of HIV-related Information Act of 1990, The Philadelphia City Code, Philadelphia Home Rule Charter as well as various applicable regulations and caselaw.

Flag, analyze and interpret changes in case law, statutes and regulations that impact the Unit’s practice.

Draft motions, briefs, pleadings, and responses for filing.

Negotiate settlements.

Track cases, maintain case files and perform other administrative and case management functions related to the practice of law.

Communicate timely and professionally with the judges, colleagues, and opposing parties.

Develop and nurture values of diversity equity and inclusion, ensuring equitable access to services, especially considering this Unit’s interaction with the City’s most vulnerable populations.

Fostering and maintaining a collegial, inclusive, and professional environment that recognizes and values all forms of diversity.

Regularly communicate with and seek advice from supervisor, mentors and unit members.

Participate in efforts to raise the profile of the Unit and the Law Department.

Competencies, Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

Knowledge of laws, legal codes, court procedures, precedents, government regulations, agency rules and processes which govern our unit’s clients with a particular focus on the confidentiality of the documents produced by each client.

Ability to analyze large amounts of information, determine relevant facts, propose viable solutions, and employ diplomacy in challenging situations.

Ability to find what applicable laws and regulations apply to a specific matter.

Ability to foster and maintain a collegial, inclusive, and professional work environment.

Ability to communicate information and ideas in writing so others will understand. Must be able to clearly present and explain their case to arbitrators, mediators, opposing parties, judges, or juries and listen, answer questions, present to large groups and high-level officials

Ability to educate clients on applicable legal requirements and policy positions.

Excellent judgment and critical thinking

Demonstrate a commitment to diversity in the office that values all individuals and respects differences.

Strong interpersonal skills, including the ability to work in teams and collaborate with colleagues and clients.

Excellent research and writing skills

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a demonstrated ability to identify and analyze legal issues within complex fact patterns.

Ability to work independently.

Ability to ask thoughtful questions, seek input from colleagues, and contribute to a team-oriented environment

Ability to organize and maintain a high-volume caseload.

• Assistant City Solicitor applicants must have at least one (1) year of relevant litigation experience.

• Deputy City Solicitor applicants should have a minimum of four (4) years of relevant litigation experience. Legal experience should ideally include some or most of those described under Essential Functions.

• Candidates must have a law degree from an ABA accredited law school and must either be a member in good standing of the Pennsylvania Bar, or currently eligible to be admitted by reciprocity to practice in Pennsylvania (Pa.B.A.R. 204). Continued employment of attorneys not admitted to the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania within six (6) months of hire is at the discretion of the Law Department.

TO APPLY: Interested candidates must submit a cover letter and resume.

Salary Range -

Assistant: $83,945 to $94,686;

Deputy: $97,299 to $117,022;

Commensurate with education and experience.

Discover the Perks of Being a City of Philadelphia Employee:

Experience savings of 10% to 40% on your educational expenses, extending not only to City employees but in some cases, spouse and dependents too!

Work Location & Onsite Expectations

This position is designated as fully onsite, and employees are expected to report in person five (5) days per week, in accordance with the City Policy. Regular on-site presence is an operational requirement of this role.

Who Thrives in This Role

This position is well-suited for candidates who are adaptable, collaborative, comfortable making real-time decisions, and able to manage competing priorities while maintaining a high standard of professionalism in a fast-paced, in-person environment.

You’ll work alongside executives to shape role strategy, design a high-touch candidate experience, leverage AI to improve our recruiting operations, and close exceptional talent for a fast-growing commercial team. You know what great looks like in a candidate, whether from building GTM teams at high-growth companies or from consistently exceeding hiring goals. jobs.title: Desktop Operations Lead
jobs.description:
Datavant is the data collaboration platform trusted for healthcare. Guided by our mission to make the world’s health data secure, accessible and actionable, we provide critical data solutions for organizations across the healthcare ecosystem - including providers, health plans, researchers, and life sciences companies. From fulfilling a single patient’s request for their medical records to powering the AI revolution in healthcare, Datavanters are building the future of how data is connected and used to improve health.

By joining Datavant today, you’re stepping onto a driven and highly collaborative team that is passionate about creating transformative change in healthcare.

About the Role

The Desktop Operations (DTO) Lead is a senior, hands-on leader who runs the daily operations of our Desktop Operations team. As the main escalation point for urgent and high-impact issues, you will own the quality and consistency of the team's work, help drive process improvement, and represent the team in specific meetings and projects. Our team includes both fully remote staff and members based in our physical offices, so you will also coordinate onsite project work and office-related improvements alongside the team's remote work.

This is a working-lead role rather than a formal people-management position. You will coach team members, triage and direct work, and propose operational and business decisions. Formal people-management responsibilities such as 1:1s, performance reviews, compensation, and hiring or termination decisions stay with the Desktop Operations Manager, who you will advise and support.

We hold this team to a higher standard than a typical L1 support team. Our technicians are autonomous, proactive, and accountable for their own work, which includes raising capacity concerns early and partnering with each other to redistribute work when someone needs help. As Lead, you will help hold that bar by monitoring team performance and surfacing where it is or isn't being met.

What You'll Do

Most of this role is oversight and stepping in on the exceptions, not doing everything yourself. The team owns the day-to-day work; you keep it running well, catch what needs attention, and drive improvements over time. Expect to ramp into it, getting a handle on escalations and quality first, then building out the proactive work.

Escalation and incident triage (primary focus)

• Be the main point of contact for escalations from other leaders, teams, and stakeholders.

• Step in on the situations that go beyond a single technician's scope. Technicians own and prioritize their own queues, so you focus on the exceptions, and jump in when a ticket is clearly being neglected or mishandled.

• Do a couple of quick queue sweeps a day as a safety net, watching for major or whole-office incidents, executive impact, and tickets that are aging, reopened, or near SLA. (Tickets are auto-assigned through round-robin.)

• Own coordination of major desktop and endpoint incidents through resolution.

• Handle what you can at the team level, and bring only business-critical or sign-off items to the Manager, with the context to decide.

• Spot recurring escalation themes and feed them into longer-term fixes.

Quality, standards, and metrics

• Spot-check completed tickets for quality and consistency with team standards.

• Keep an eye on documentation. Each technician updates or creates one doc a week; you make sure it is happening and that the quality holds up.

• Track team KPIs and SLAs such as resolution time, reopen rate, CSAT, backlog, and ticket aging.

• Watch performance against our higher-than-L1 bar of autonomy, proactivity, and accountability, and flag where people are excelling or slipping.

• Give the Manager a regular metrics summary that calls out trends and root causes.

Process and continuous improvement

• We are not a typical L2 team; we think of ourselves as business enablers. When we see an issue, we look for a way to handle it better next time and cut ticket volume, rather than just closing the ticket. You will help drive this alongside the team.

• Turn recurring problems into permanent fixes instead of solving the same thing repeatedly.

• With the team, propose automation and workflow improvements that reduce ticket volume and manual effort.

• Lead a project to build a proper ticket priority and impact framework: an ITIL-aligned model with end-user impact and urgency inputs, working with the Jira team to implement it.

Onsite and physical office operations

• Be the advisory and oversight point for office-related escalations and improvements. Office managers can come to you when onsite work is not being handled well.

• Coordinate office project work the Manager delegates. Day-to-day onsite work stays with the onsite technicians, who prioritize it and keep stakeholders informed.

• Stay looped in on AV and vendor activity. Onsite members coordinate directly with the AV vendor; you keep tabs and flag anything that needs attention.

• Keep an eye on office hardware and asset needs. The remote IT Asset Management team owns shipping and onsite members handle orders; you flag gaps or recurring problems.

• Keep the Manager informed of anything affecting a whole office, and bring office process changes for approval before rolling them out.

Coaching and team development

• Offer technical mentorship and coaching in the moment.

• Notice skill gaps, training needs, and workload imbalances, and advise the Manager to inform 1:1s and reviews. (Formal 1:1s, reviews, and personnel decisions stay with the Manager.)

Stakeholder and cross-team representation

• Represent Desktop Operations in specific projects or cross-team meetings the Manager delegates, bringing sign-off items back with the context to decide.

• Be a day-to-day point of contact for partner teams on the work you are handling.

How the Role Works

You will decide independently on:

• Escalation routing and triage decisions

• In-the-moment coaching and quality feedback to team members

• Day-to-day operational direction within established standards

• Office-manager escalations about onsite work, and coordination of office project work the Manager has delegated

You will recommend, with the Manager approving:

• Process, workflow, and SOP changes

• Office-related process changes and improvements, for a single site or across locations

• Tooling purchases or changes that involve spend

• Policy changes or anything that affects other teams

• Input into hiring, development plans, and performance discussions

The Manager retains:

• Formal 1:1s, performance reviews, and personnel decisions

• Compensation, hiring, and termination decisions

• Final sign-off on business decisions and budget

What You'll Bring

• At least 5 years of progressive, hands-on desktop support or desktop engineering experience.

• A track record of informal leadership, such as mentoring peers, owning incidents from start to finish, and being a trusted go-to for escalations. Formal lead or management experience is a plus but not required; this role suits a strong individual contributor ready to step into leadership.

• Strong incident management and troubleshooting skills under pressure.

• A solid grounding in desktop engineering: device management, configuration, provisioning and imaging, OS deployment, and patching.

• Familiarity with IAM principles and SSO. Our environment uses Microsoft Entra.

• Hands-on experience with endpoint and MDM tooling across Windows and Mac. We use Microsoft Intune for Windows and Mosyle for Mac, and experience with comparable platforms such as Jamf for Mac or Configuration Manager/SCCM for Windows carries over well.

• Working knowledge of ITSM and ITIL processes and tooling. We use Jira for ticketing and issue tracking and incident.io for managing major business-impacting incidents.

• Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain technical detail to non-technical people.

• Good organizational skills and sound judgment about what to handle and what to escalate.

• Experience supporting a distributed workforce across both remote and physical office environments.

Nice to Have

• ITIL foundation or familiarity with incident, problem, and change management.

• Experience building or maintaining SOPs, runbooks, and operational documentation.

• Familiarity with reporting and metrics tooling and dashboards.

What Success Looks Like

• Escalations are handled quickly and consistently, with only the right items reaching the Manager.

• Team metrics and quality are visible and trending in the right direction.

• Recurring issues steadily decline as permanent fixes take hold.

• The team's work stays consistent and in line with standards.

• Onsite and remote members work to the same standards, and office issues are caught early.

• The team keeps moving toward a more proactive, business-enabling state.

jobs.title: Director of Growth Marketing
jobs.description:
COMPANY DESCRIPTION

Today, when you go to your doctor and get referred to a specialist, your doctor sends out a referral and tells you, "They'll be in touch soon." So you wait. And wait. Sometimes days, weeks, or even months. Why? Because too often providers are overwhelmed with the painstakingly tedious work required to get paid by insurance companies. Powered by proprietary models, Tennr handles the complex paperwork that gets patients through the door and providers paid, helping operators get patients the right care, at the right time, in the right setting.




ROLE DESCRIPTION

As Director of Growth, you'll own the plan for how Tennr generates pipeline: where we invest, what we stop doing, and how we know it's working. Our buyers run DME suppliers, infusion centers, specialty pharmacies, and other provider organizations. They're operators, not software buyers. They search for specific problems, not product categories, and more of them now ask AI assistants which vendors to consider. We sell several products into each of them, including referral intake, prior auth, AI voice, and patient onboarding, and every new vertical, product, and channel multiplies the ways we could spend the next dollar. Your job is to pick the few that matter most and make sure the team executes on them.

You'll lead Growth Marketing and work closely with Sales, Product, and Finance. You'll set the targets, work backwards from them to operating milestones, and run the cadence that keeps the team accountable to the number. This role suits someone who thinks like a general manager: you'll act as strategist, analyst, systems builder, and partner to Sales in the same week. The scope will grow to cover new problems as Tennr grows.

You'll know you're right for this if you've been the person leadership hands its hardest growth problem, you're as comfortable building the model as running the review, and you want to build a team around this work.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Goals & Metrics: Own Tennr's marketing-sourced pipeline target and set the channel goals that roll up into it. Break it into its drivers: CPL, CPQL, conversion to opportunity, and pipeline contribution by segment and channel. Own the model that explains what moves each one, and make sure progress is measured the same way every week.

 - Roadmap: Diagnose the biggest opportunities and constraints across verticals, products, and channels. Form a clear point of view on where Growth should invest and what it should deprioritize, and defend that call with data.

 - Planning: Turn the roadmap into a short list of initiatives with owners, success metrics, budget, and headcount. Run annual and quarterly planning for Growth, allocate budget across channels, including direct programs, and partner with Finance on spend and payback.

 - Operating System: Design the cadences, dashboards, and decision forums that surface performance gaps early and turn them into action. Partner with Sales on pipeline reviews, keep conversion signal clean from first touch to closed deal, and make changes in our systems of record yourself rather than filing a ticket.

 - Strategic Projects: Lead the high-stakes growth questions as they come up, such as how to enter a new vertical, how to take a new product to market, or how to position against a competitor, and bring the analysis that settles them.

 - Direct Programs: Own the programs that put Tennr in front of buyers and customers directly. Decide which ones earn investment, run them against a fixed budget and date, and hold them to the same pipeline standard as every other channel.

 - Experimentation: Set the bar for which experiments get run, funded, and scaled across new channels, AI tools, and Clay workflows, and cut the ones that don't earn their spend.

 - Team: Lead Growth Marketing across paid, search, AEO, and direct programs. Hire and develop the team as it scales, while staying hands-on in the work yourself.

 - Cross-Functional Leadership: Work with Sales on target segments and pipeline, Content Marketing on offers, Brand and Design on creative, Product on launches, and Finance on budget. Create clarity and drive decisions across teams you don't manage directly.
   
   


QUALIFICATIONS

 - 7+ years of experience, mixing strategy work (management consulting at MBB or similar, investment banking, or private equity) with at least 3 years at a high-growth startup in strategy, business operations, growth, or revenue operations. At least 1 year personally owning a business outcome, such as a P&L, quota, pipeline, or retention number.

 - First-principles thinking. You can take an ambiguous problem, identify the outcome that matters, break it into its drivers, and design a practical path forward.

 - Quantitative fluency. You build your own models, write your own SQL. and can use imperfect data to find performance gaps, make tradeoffs, and tell whether a strategy is working.

 - Operator instincts. You move between setting direction and getting into the details required to make something work, and you keep multiple workstreams moving without losing the important details.

 - Program execution. You've delivered high-stakes programs with hard dates, outside partners, and fixed budgets, and you know what has to be true weeks before the day.

 - Presence. You can represent Tennr with senior operators and customers, and earn their trust quickly.

 - Cross-functional leadership. You create clarity, establish accountability, and drive decisions across teams you don't manage.

 - Ownership. You own the outcome, not just the inputs, and you follow up until the work is done. You've rebuilt a playbook from first principles before and want to do it again.

 - Clear writing. You can put a recommendation, the reasoning, and the tradeoffs on one page and get a room to a decision.

 - Judgment you can show. You can walk us through growth plans you've built, the bets you made, and what happened to pipeline.

 - An informed view on AI, backed by real examples of how you've applied it to your own workflows or a team's, and a clear sense of where it helps and where it doesn't.

 - Experience managing people, or a track record that shows you're ready to build and lead a team.
   
   


A PLUS IF YOU…

 - Have healthcare or healthtech experience, especially selling to provider organizations.

 - Have worked at a vertical SaaS company that sells to operators rather than software buyers.

 - Have built a customer community or advisory board.

 - Have taken a new product or a new vertical to market.

 - Have built go-to-market workflows in Clay, Salesforce, or similar tools yourself.
   
   


WHY TENNR?

 - Drive Impact: one of our company values is Cowboy, meaning you set the pace. You won’t just talk about things, you’ll get them done. And feel the impact.

 - Develop Operational Expertise: learn the inner workings of scaling systems, tools, and infrastructure.

 - Innovate with Purpose: we’re not just doing this for fun (although we do have a lot of fun). At Tennr, you’ll join a high-caliber team maniacally focused on reducing patient delays across the U.S. healthcare system.

 - Build Relationships: collaborate and connect with like-minded, driven individuals in our Hudson Square office 4 days/week.

 - Free lunch! Plus a pantry full of snacks.

 


BENEFITS

 - Beautiful new office at 345 Hudson Street

 - Unlimited PTO

 - 100% paid employee health benefit options

 - Employer funded 401(k) match

 - Competitive parental leave

jobs.description:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.




ABOUT THE ROLE 

We are looking for an Analyst, Deal Operations to help drive Ramp’s next phase of growth! Reporting to the Senior Manager, Deal Desk, you’ll be a key partner in taking our Sales organization to the next level, responsible for quoting, pricing structure, and contracting for our Sales team. You'll be an integral part of the Deal Operations team with a focus on offering guidance to drive deal execution while complying with company policies and procedures and ensuring consistency to manage risk. You’ll work directly with our Sales, Legal, Accounting, and cross-functional leadership to better streamline efficient workflows and enhance sales productivity.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

jobs.title: Mediation Specialist
jobs.description:
About Lucid

At Lucid, we are creating exceptional mobility experiences through innovation to drive the world forward. Built on Lucid’s proprietary technology and software-defined vehicle architecture, our award-winning vehicles bring our “Compromise Nothing™” approach to the global automotive market. That means refusing to choose between performance and sustainability, design and engineering, ambition and integrity. In Lucid Air and Lucid Gravity, we have designed and built vehicles that have redefined their segments, combining exceptional range, performance, design, and expansive space in a single experience.

We achieve this through deep vertical integration, with design, engineering, and production happening in-house across our global offices and manufacturing facilities. Our teams come from industries around the world, united by a shared commitment to excellence. By refusing to settle, you can help redefine what’s possible and shape the future of mobility.

The ideal candidate for the Mediation Specialist will be expected to demonstrate excellence and possess the ability to learn quickly and to strive for perfection within a fast-paced environment. The Mediation Specialist will be responsible for providing a superior level of customer service and attention to customers who encounter unsatisfactory experiences with their vehicle. This position will need to acknowledge notice of complaints, perform root-cause analysis. This role will negotiate basic or moderately complex situations. The ideal candidate will deliver communications that are always timely, detailed, and compassionate to ensure customer satisfaction. This candidate will work independently or collaboratively and be able prioritize and manage their own workloads. This individual will also ensure each resolution will be optimized for each situation, in accordance with established processes and requirements.

Key Responsibilities:

• Research product inquiries and provides consistent and efficient follow-through on all customer concerns requiring further investigation.

• Respond to customer communications, concerns, or issues in relation to their concern, with a focus on prevention and early intervention for customer retention and interception of any repurchase or replacement vehicle requests.

• Gather required documents for thorough case assessment with relevant stakeholders

• Negotiate settlements with customers in the interest of customer retention and Lifetime Owner Loyalty as an alternative to a vehicle buyback

• Extensive interaction with field service teams to ensure accuracy of information Advocate for customer expectations throughout the entire investigative process.

• Review case in detail to evaluate and investigate information from documentation such as sales documents, loan contracts, Work Orders, customer lifecycle, receipts, or other pertinent details or documents.

• Make and maintain a connection with the customer by understanding needs, managing expectations, and serving the customer with empathy.

• Facilitate expeditious outcomes of investigations.

• Assist in settling procedural matters.

• Capture issues, concerns, needs, and interests of all parties involved through case management tool or other resources.

• Contribute to business objectives, performance metrics, and effectively use tools & technology to meet existing or new goals.

• Provide real time input and consultation around trends with vehicles, parts or Voice of Customer around recurring issues.

Role Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s Degree and/or 4+ years in litigation, customer service, or related work experience, at least one of which is in an automotive, or adjustment fields.

• Experience working under pressure in a fast-paced environment while consistently meeting standards for productivity and quality.

• Highly analytical while remaining empathetic, as to accurately evaluate information and provide an appropriate determination.

• Experienced communication skills such as, but not limited to, active listening and negotiation skills.

• Ability to decipher highly nuanced documentation, while utilizing knowledge of automotive repair information, services, techniques and/or litigation trends.

• Strong knowledge of various computer operating systems and Microsoft Office Suite products.

jobs.title: Sr. Director, Assays & Platform Technologies
jobs.description:
Who We Are:

Cell Signaling Technology (CST) is a different kind of life sciences company, one founded, owned, and run by active research scientists, with the highest standards of product and service quality, technological innovation, and scientific rigor for over 20 years. We consistently provide fellow scientists around the globe with best-in-class products and services to fuel their quests for discovery.

Helping researchers find new solutions is our main mission every day, but it's not our only mission. We're also dedicated to helping identify solutions to other problems facing our world. We believe that all businesses must be responsible and work in partnership with local communities, while seeking to minimize their environmental impact. That's why we joined 1% for the Planet as its first life science member, and have committed to achieving net-zero emissions by 2029.

The Role:

As the Sr. Director for Assay and Platform Technologies, you will define and execute the company’s collective immunoassay platform strategy, and support  critical commercial and business development partnerships. Operating at the intersection of research, product development, and commercial execution, you will oversee portfolio leadership, guide cross-functional collaborations, and lead four immunoassay platform sub-teams to drive innovation from concept through commercial success.

Essential duties and responsibilities (with ESTIMATED percentage allocation)

Platform Strategy & Portfolio Leadership (35%)

• Responsible for strategic and operational objectives, work plans, budgets, and portfolio health metrics across the four sub-teams

• Responsible for the development of innovative products and solutions configured for use in established and emerging immunoassay platforms.

• Develop and implement the product development platform strategy across traditional and emerging immunoassays, single-cell analysis, spatial biology, and mass spectrometry-based proteomics; translate CST's strategy into platform-specific roadmaps.

• Product pipeline governance: accountable for the integrity and strategic coherence of the immunoassays product portfolio.

• Responsible for go/no-go recommendations on platform onboarding and resource allocation decisions.

• Collaborates with product development groups (antibody & protein technologies, antibody discovery, application & validation groups, and the Custom Solutions team on strategic and operational objectives, work plans, and portfolio health metrics.

• Resource and budget management: makes decisions on resourcing trade-offs across sub-teams and between R&D platform development and pre/post-sales scientific support activities.

• Drives adoption of new assays and platforms to support pre/post-sales, publishing, and customer engagement in alignment with company’s R&D objectives, with priority focus in biotech, pharma, and CRO customer segments.

Scientific Research & Translational Leadership (25%)

• Maintains deep scientific expertise across priority immunoassay platform areas.

• Responsible for the conceptualization or design of products designed to meet the specific needs of biotech, pharma, and CRO customer workflows in drug discovery, biomarker development, and clinical/translational research.

• Informs platform development priorities through active engagement with the Custom Solutions Group; ensures biopharma customer intelligence from custom engagements feeds back into platform roadmap decisions.

• Ensures broad technical enablement through external scientific publications, white papers, application notes, and conference presentations that establish CST platform leadership and credibility in the translational research market

• Attends relevant industry conferences to gather intelligence and engage with scientists and KOLs.

• Hires and develops scientific expertise within the immunoassay platforms core, with an emphasis on biopharma workflow support; ensures sub-team leaders have the necessary skills required to support pre/post-sales engagement.

Commercial & BD Partnership (25%)

• Operates as the primary R&D interface for the Platform Commercial segment; works in close collaboration and shares accountability with the biopharma commercial team and Product Marketing Managers (PMMs) to align platform development priorities with commercial pipeline and customer needs. Collaborates with Biopharma Marketing, Business Development (BD), and Sales leaders to define business and revenue objectives.

• Partners with Field Application Scientists (FAS) to ensure pre/post-sales technical support capability keeps pace with platform complexity; defines FAS capability requirements and provides scientific direction for FAS training.

• Works tightly with BD in partnership identification, designing deal objectives, and scientific due diligence for platform-adjacent opportunities — spatial, IVD, single-cell, proximity, and proteomics partnerships.

• Engages directly with key pharma accounts and KOLs to understand workflow needs, validate platform positioning, and identify unmet needs that translate into product development priorities.

• Partners closely with the Custom Solutions Group to ​receive biopharma workflow intelligence and​ transition bespoke client innovations into broad-market catalog platform products provides scientific direction that enables effective product launch, market positioning, and lifecycle management.

Talent Management (15%)

• Directly manages four platform sub-team leaders; sets performance expectations, provides coaching, and conducts meaningful performance reviews. Holds sub-team leaders accountable for milestone delivery and laboratory informatics data integrity.

• Builds and executes a talent strategy: succession planning, IC development, and the hiring of new biopharma workflow and platform expertise.

• Develops individual development plans for sub-team leaders with particular emphasis on commercial partnership skills, external scientific representation, and platform-specific domain depth.

Who You Are & What You Bring To The Team:

• Ph.D. in a relevant life science discipline with a strong record of peer-reviewed publications

• Minimum of 10 years related experience with 8+ years of direct people management experience

• Scientific Deep Dive: Expertise in 2+ platform areas: Immunoassays, single-cell technologies, or spatial biology.

• Translational/Biopharma: Preclinical R&D, drug discovery, biomarker development, or clinical research applications.

• Product Lifecycle: Proven track record leading platform product development from concept through commercial launch.

• Experience at the R&D / Commercial interface (tools, diagnostics, or biopharma services).

• Demonstrated experience incorporating AI-enabled scientific tools into research, translational, or development workflows to improve the quality, speed, or effectiveness of scientific decision-making.

• Capable of innovating applications to drive product development and solve customer needs and problems

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills

• Exceptional organization skills, and the ability to manage multiple projects and prioritize efforts appropriately

• Effective communication skills (verbal and written)

• Demonstrated ability to generate novel scientific hypotheses and design complex experiments to test them.

Ideally, You'll Have:

• Demonstrated leadership experience in academic institutions and biotechnology or pharmaceutical industry settings.

• Demonstrated ability to build and manage BD partnerships.

• Experience with complex solution development.

• Pre/post-sales scientific engagement expertise.

Physical Conditions / Physical Requirements:

• Office work environment is typically quiet with some background noise

• Ability to work at a desk and computer for extended periods

• Dexterity to operate computer equipment and handle documents.

• Ability to read and interpret detailed documents and reports.

• Occasional standing and walking will be required to move around the office or facility.

• Infrequent lifting of light objects, such as files or equipment, up to 15 pounds, may also be necessary.

• Requires occasional travel as needed to attend industry conferences, partner sites, and/or meet with key external partners.

This position has a starting base salary range of $249,000 - $300,000 per year, which the company, in good faith, reasonably expects to pay for this role at the time of posting. Actual compensation within this range will be determined based on factors including, but not limited to, relevant skills, qualifications, experience, and internal equity.

What We Offer:

At Cell Signaling Technology (CST), we recognize that people will always be our most important asset. Providing a safe, inclusive, and stimulating working environment that understands the importance of diversity, human dignity, and meaningful work is as important as establishing company policies that incorporate excellent health insurance and pay benefits. We recognize that the  development of people is the key to their happiness and thus ensure every employee has impactful discussions with their manager and develops actionable performance and professional development plans. Lastly, we are committed to engaging and supporting our employees in committees and philanthropy that benefit their local communities and environment through community investment programs.

jobs.title: Director, Revenue Readiness
jobs.description:
What We Do:

Cybercrime is growing, and more businesses are getting hit by threats that used to target only the biggest organizations. That pushes defenders like us to operate at the highest level, and it deepens our need for good people who want to make a meaningful impact.

Founded in 2015 by former NSA cyber operators, Huntress is a remote-first team working to make enterprise-grade cybersecurity accessible to businesses of all sizes. We work closely with security teams and service providers protecting complex environments, often without the time or headcount to handle it all. That’s why we build our technology in-house and back it with a 24/7 human-led Security Operations Center (SOC). As a result, our platform is never disconnected from the experts who manage it, ensuring our customers' protection.

Huntress now secures more than 5M endpoints and 16M identities worldwide. Those numbers keep growing because more businesses rely on us to help carry the load and operate with more confidence. Every day, you can see that commitment in how we stand with our customers and how we show up for each other.

Reports to: VP, Revenue Operations

Location: Remote US

Compensation Range: $190,000 to $210,000 base plus bonus and equity

What You’ll Do:

Revenue Readiness owns how Huntress prepares revenue teams to perform. As Director of Revenue Readiness, you will set the vision and build the function that turns company priorities, process changes, product launches, and evolving selling expectations into a coordinated readiness strategy.

You will lead across the revenue organization to establish the governance, operating standards, learning systems, and program discipline needed to prepare sellers and frontline managers consistently across roles, segments, motions, and geographies. You will shape priorities with senior GTM leaders, make clear investment and sequencing decisions, and lead your team and cross-functional partners through execution.

Perfect Imperfection guides how you work. You create enough structure to scale while continuing to learn and improve the model. You Give a $h*t about whether people are genuinely prepared to perform. You bring Candor when ownership or expectations are unclear, build trust by giving more than we take, and demonstrate Warrior Spirit as you lead meaningful organizational change. You are Outcome-Obsessed about building organizational readiness that helps Huntress execute its growth priorities.

Responsibilities:

• Set and lead the global Revenue Readiness vision, strategy, operating model, and multi-year roadmap, aligned with Huntress's growth priorities and the capabilities revenue teams need to execute them.

• Serve as the senior functional leader for Revenue Readiness, advising GTM executives on organizational preparedness, capability needs, investment priorities, and the risks associated with major business changes.

• Own the Revenue Readiness portfolio and make decisions about priorities, sequencing, capacity, and resource allocation based on business impact and the organization's ability to absorb change.

• Build the foundational readiness infrastructure for Huntress, including program intake and prioritization, learning governance, delivery standards, reinforcement expectations, content lifecycle management, platform administration, and measurement.

• Establish a consistent readiness architecture across new hire onboarding, role-based ramp, frontline manager readiness, major business changes, and ongoing development.

• Create a scalable process for translating identified business needs, performance gaps, product launches, system changes, and new go-to-market expectations into structured readiness programs.

• Partner with Sales Ops Business Partners to understand prioritized business needs and define the capabilities, behaviors, and measures of preparedness required to address them.

• Establish clear ownership across Revenue Readiness, Sales Ops Business Partners, Sales Leaders, Product Marketing, GTM Systems, Technical Sales, and other subject matter experts. Revenue Readiness owns program architecture and operationalization, domain experts own subject matter accuracy, and Sales Leaders own coaching, reinforcement, and team execution.

• Lead the planning and orchestration of company-level readiness initiatives, aligning senior stakeholders on objectives, ownership, timing, reinforcement, and measures of success.

• Set direction and accountability for the operational health of the learning ecosystem, including the LMS, learning calendars, program records, learner communications, reporting, and content standards.

• Develop scalable readiness programs for Huntress selling practices and workflows, including MEDDPICC, Digital Sales Rooms, Mutual Action Plans, and AI-supported ways of working.

• Define how Huntress measures readiness across participation, preparedness, competency, adoption, and behavior change. Use those insights to improve programs and guide future investment while maintaining Sales Leader accountability for business performance.

• Build, lead, and develop the Revenue Readiness team. Establish the organizational structure, capabilities, role clarity, operating rhythms, and performance expectations needed to support a growing global revenue organization.

• Represent Revenue Readiness in senior GTM planning and decision-making, ensuring major initiatives account for the time, support, and reinforcement teams need to adopt change successfully.

What You Bring To The Team:

• You have 10+ years of experience across revenue readiness, sales enablement, learning operations, sales effectiveness, or related go-to-market functions, including 5+ years leading teams or major functional programs.

• You have led a revenue readiness, enablement, or sales effectiveness function in a scaling B2B SaaS organization and have built or significantly evolved its strategy, team, infrastructure, and operating model.

• You have influenced senior executives, shaped cross-functional priorities, and made investment and resource tradeoffs across a portfolio of competing business needs.

• You understand how to build organizational readiness and assess whether teams are prepared to execute, reinforce new expectations, and sustain change.

• You have designed scalable systems for program intake, prioritization, learning operations, onboarding, reinforcement, content governance, and readiness measurement.

• You are an effective cross-functional operator who can bring together business leaders, operational partners, systems teams, and subject matter experts while maintaining clear ownership.

• You can establish clear roles and decision rights across Revenue Readiness, Sales Ops Business Partners, Sales Leaders, Product Marketing, GTM Systems, Technical Sales, and other contributors.

• You understand B2B SaaS selling across multiple roles, segments, motions, and levels of complexity, including the critical role frontline managers play in coaching, reinforcement, inspection, and accountability.

• You can lead a team and senior stakeholders through meaningful organizational change, creating clarity, building alignment, and establishing the priorities, governance, and operating practices needed for a scalable Revenue Readiness function.

• You use data and judgment to evaluate preparedness, identify readiness risks, improve programs, and communicate investment tradeoffs to senior leaders.

• You can orchestrate multi-step AI workflows and reusable systems that improve analysis, program development, learning operations, prioritization, and decision quality while applying sound judgment to the outputs.

What We Offer:

• 100% remote work environment - since our founding in 2015

• Generous paid time off policy, including vacation, sick time, and paid holidays

• 12 weeks of paid parental leave

• Highly competitive and comprehensive medical, dental, and vision benefits plans

• 401(k) with a 5% contribution regardless of employee contribution

• Life and Disability insurance plans

• One-time $500 reimbursement for building/upgrading home office

• Annual allowance for education and professional development assistance

• Access to the BetterUp platform for coaching, personal, and professional growth

USA Employment Lawyers is a plaintiff-side boutique class and collective action litigation firm based in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, with an active nationwide docket. The firm represents workers in wage-and-hour matters, including overtime, off-the-clock work, unpaid wages, and related employment claims. The role of the Intake Specialist at USA Employment Lawyers is fundamental to our mission of advocating for employees nationwide. As the first point of contact for potential clients, the Intake Specialist will conduct initial screenings, gather facts, and ensure prompt triage of cases, supporting our goal of holding employers accountable for wage violations. This position directly impacts our ability to deliver justice to employees, contributing significantly to the firm's reputation and success.
