jobs.title: Principal Software Engineer, Anti-Abuse
jobs.description:
At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset — who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.



We are hiring a Principal Software Engineer for our Anti-Abuse team. The Anti-Abuse team sits at the core of protecting Snowflake and our customers from abuse on the Snowflake Platform. We strive to see the complete picture, leading platform-wide abuse and fraud detection while designing and deploying proactive controls for Snowflake's highest-risk capabilities: Snowpark, Data Sharing, Cortex AI, and the next generation of cloud engineering challenges as Snowflake rapidly scales. In this role, you will be the lead technical architect responsible for defining and driving our technical strategy for abuse prevention, detection, and response across the entire Snowflake ecosystem.




AS A PRINCIPAL SOFTWARE ENGINEER, ANTI-ABUSE AT SNOWFLAKE, YOU WILL:

 - Define and drive the long-term technical vision for abuse and fraud detection across the Snowflake platform, serving as the chief architect for platform-wide anti-abuse strategy

 - Partner directly with product and engineering teams building Snowflake's newest and highest-risk surfaces (Snowpark user code execution runtimes, Data Sharing and Marketplace, AI/LLM services) to design and deploy robust anti-abuse controls from day one

 - Architect and scale high-throughput, low-latency telemetry pipelines and risk-scoring engines capable of analyzing millions of queries, sessions, and data transactions across multi-cloud environments (AWS, Azure, GCP)

 - Continuously model emerging abuse techniques, including trial compute abuse, cryptocurrency mining, bot-driven account creation, credential stuffing, and illicit network traffic routing

 - Design intelligent mitigation systems that automatically throttle, challenge, or isolate abusive workloads and malicious actors with near-zero false-positive impact on legitimate enterprise workloads

 - Raise the technical bar across the engineering organization through mentorship of staff and senior engineers, and influence architectural standards across adjacent platform teams




OUR IDEAL PRINCIPAL SOFTWARE ENGINEER, ANTI-ABUSE WILL HAVE:

 - 12+ years of software engineering experience in distributed systems, cloud platform infrastructure, or security engineering, with significant time dedicated to anti-abuse, fraud detection, platform trust, or threat mitigation

 - Proven track record architecting mission-critical, large-scale distributed services in Java, C++, or Python

 - Deep experience designing controls for code-execution runtimes, multi-tenant compute environments, cloud APIs, or data platforms (e.g., mitigating compute hijacking, sandbox escapes, abuse of serverless functions, or network egress abuse)

 - Demonstrated ability to build streaming event processing, anomaly detection, behavioral heuristic engines, or graph-based syndicate detection systems at enterprise scale

 - Strong intuition for attacker economics and mechanics, with experience modeling threat vectors across account lifecycles (signup, trial, payment, execution, sharing)

 - Exceptional ability to partner with product managers, infrastructure teams, and security researchers to embed safety controls into high-velocity product roadmaps

 - B.S., M.S., or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Cybersecurity, or equivalent practical experience




BONUS POINTS FOR THE FOLLOWING:

 - Experience building anti-abuse systems for multi-tenant cloud platforms or SaaS-at-scale environments

 - Familiarity with AI/LLM abuse vectors (prompt injection, model extraction, automated content generation for fraud)

 - Track record of designing zero-trust or defense-in-depth architectures for compute runtimes

 - Published research or industry contributions in fraud detection, adversarial ML, or platform trust and safety

 - Experience operating detection and response systems across multiple cloud providers simultaneously




WHY JOIN OUR ANTI-ABUSE TEAM AT SNOWFLAKE?

The Anti-Abuse team works at the intersection of platform security, distributed systems, and adversarial thinking. You will own the technical strategy for protecting one of the world's fastest-growing cloud platforms from novel and evolving threats. This is not a compliance checkbox role: you will architect real-time detection systems, embed native guardrails into new product primitives before they reach production, and partner directly with engineering leaders across the organization to anticipate threats no one else is seeing yet. If you want to build the immune system for the agentic enterprise, this is the role.



Snowflake is growing fast, and we’re scaling our team to help enable and accelerate our growth. We are looking for people who share our values, challenge ordinary thinking, and push the pace of innovation while building a future for themselves and Snowflake.

How do you want to make your impact?

For jobs located in the United States, please visit the job posting on the Snowflake Careers Site for salary and benefits information: careers.snowflake.com http://careers.snowflake.com

jobs.title: Commissioning Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT MARIANA MINERALS

Mariana Minerals is a software-first, vertically integrated minerals company on a mission to supply the critical minerals powering modern energy, AI, and defense technologies. We’re reimagining the minerals supply chain by combining deep industry expertise with advanced software, automation, and data-driven decision-making.

We’re building a core commissioning team of talented, versatile engineers who know how to take a plant from mechanical completion to running. As a Commissioning Engineer, you’ll own electrical and mechanical commissioning scopes: energizing power systems, bringing up equipment and utilities, and getting new systems online safely.

You’ll work alongside local commissioning teams, own your commissioning assignments, and make sure we’re building and using our systems throughout commissioning.

Your first year will likely be focused on Copper One, our operating copper mine and refinery in Utah, or Lithium One, our new lithium facility in Texas. After that, you’ll go wherever we’re bringing new capacity online, anywhere in the world. Between commissioning pushes, you’ll support design teams and projects at other sites. There’s always something being built.

This is a hands-on role for scrappy, collaborative engineers who thrive during startup. You’ll solve problems in the field, do some of your own design work when needed, bring new systems online for the first time, and do it safely, every time.

Responsibilities

 - Lead commissioning teams at various locations. The candidate must be willing to travel to sites during commissioning.

 - Develop detailed commissioning plans in advance of commissioning activities.

 - Ensure documentation is complete, including LOTO procedures, work instructions, maintenance procedures, detailed plans, schedules, budgets, etc.

 - Own scopes relative to engineering expertise.

 - Lead safe startup practices so everyone gets home safe.

 - Confirm proper installation and functionality of equipment. Lead specific activities on site during dry and wet commissioning.

 - Lead ramping activities for assigned commissioning area(s).

 - Ensure equipment is functional, including controls functionality.

 - Train and hand over equipment to onsite operators and maintenance personnel.

 - Serve as a technical expert to assist in process engineering after handover to operations as needed.

 - Simplify commissioning procedures, then assist in building tools in MarianaOS to automate and scale.

 - Document and share lessons learned so every site starts from a stronger playbook.

 - Support design teams and projects at other sites between commissioning cycles.

 - Contribute to design reviews and HazOps during the design phase.

 - Travel up to 80%, including extended site assignments during onsite commissioning. Short-notice trips are possible. Between projects, work from a Mariana office or, preferably, an operating asset when needed.

Requirements

 - Bachelor’s degree or higher in chemical, mechanical, electrical, or a related engineering field preferred, or proven hands-on experience commissioning industrial systems.

 - Hands-on commissioning experience on greenfield or new-plant startups, with deep expertise in electrical or mechanical systems and working knowledge of the other.

 - Background in battery/EV, semiconductor, data centers, advanced manufacturing, or similar fast-paced industrial environments strongly preferred.

 - Working knowledge of equipment common in mining and/or refining and plant utilities.

 - Ability to read and mark up single-lines, P&IDs, schematics, and mechanical drawings.

 - Desire to help build a smart P&ID system.

 - Preferred: PLC/controls and instrumentation startup experience, experience at a company that designs, installs, and commissions its own equipment, and comfort using AI tools to speed up your work.

 - Collaborative by default. You share knowledge openly and make the team around you better.

 - Strong safety mindset, with experience leading safe energization, LOTO, and startup practices (NFPA 70E).

 - Valid driver’s license.

Safety

Safety comes first on every project. You’ll model our site safety policies every day and help lead safe startup practices on site.

 - Lead JHAs and LOTO for your commissioning scope, follow permit-to-work procedures, and participate in safety meetings, audits, and incident investigations.

 - Participate in HazOps.

 - Always wear proper PPE and complete all site safety training.

Physical Demands & Work Conditions

 - Expect heavy on-site work, and extended or irregular hours during commissioning, followed by stretches of remote or office-based work.

 - Active industrial and construction environments that involve standing, walking, climbing, and working in tight spaces for extended periods, and lifting up to 50 lbs.

 - Noise, dust, outdoor work in varying weather, and remote site locations.




OUR CULTURE IS BUILT ON FOUR PRINCIPLES:



Everyone Gets Home Safe. We never put speed or cost ahead of people.

Extreme Ownership. We take full responsibility for outcomes, relentlessly driving toward solutions.

Engineer Out Requirements, then Automate. We simplify, optimize, and then automate for scale.

Share Your Legos. We collaborate openly, share knowledge, and empower each other to build bigger, better solutions.



Join us as we build the future of responsible mineral sourcing and supply!

jobs.title: Sanctions Operations Associate
jobs.description:
About Rippling

Rippling gives businesses one place to run HR, IT, and Finance. It brings together all of the workforce systems that are normally scattered across a company, like payroll, expenses, benefits, and computers. For the first time ever, you can manage and automate every part of the employee lifecycle in a single system.

Take onboarding, for example. With Rippling, you can hire a new employee anywhere in the world and set up their payroll, corporate card, computer, benefits, and even third-party apps like Slack and Microsoft 365—all within 90 seconds.

Based in San Francisco, CA, Rippling has raised $1.4B+ from the world’s top investors—including Kleiner Perkins, Founders Fund, Sequoia, Greenoaks, and Bedrock—and was named one of America's best startup employers by Forbes.

We prioritize candidate safety. Please be aware that all official communication will only be sent from @Rippling.com addresses.

About the role

Rippling is seeking a Sanctions Operations Associate to join our growing Financial Crime Compliance Team. A core part of this role is the review and disposition of sanctions screening alerts. You will evaluate matches generated by Rippling’s automated screening program, applying sound analytical judgment to distinguish true matches from false positives, escalate confirmed hits, and maintain clear documentation throughout the alert lifecycle. This includes assessing name, geography, and ownership-based hits across OFAC and international sanctions lists, and ensuring disposition rationales meet audit and regulatory standards. You will also support sanctions due diligence reviews of existing customers, prospects, and third-party partners, helping ensure alignment with Rippling’s risk appetite and applicable sanctions regulations.

Due diligence reviews involve research using open-source, proprietary, and third-party tools, reviewing sanctions-related adverse media, and drafting targeted outreach and escalation questions. You will contribute to risk analyses across a broad spectrum of sanctions exposure and work closely with teams across the organization, including the Compliance FCC Team, KYC, Sales, Implementation, Legal, and Product.

What You Will Do

• Review and disposition sanctions screening alerts generated through Rippling’s screening program; evaluating potential matches against OFAC and international sanctions lists, assessing name, geography, and ownership-based hits, applying risk-based judgment to distinguish true positives from false positives, and escalating confirmed or high-risk matches with clear, well-documented rationales
• Support end-to-end sanctions due diligence reviews of customers, prospects, and third-party partners, from initial screening through risk determination and resolution
• Conduct research across open-source, proprietary, and third-party tools, including adverse media analysis and sanctions nexus assessments for complex entities and ownership structures
• Participate in customer-facing due diligence calls and help develop targeted outreach and escalation questions that surface meaningful risk
• Contribute to the policies, procedures, and operational frameworks that support Rippling’s sanctions due diligence program

jobs.title: Senior Safety Analysis Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT RADIANT

Radiant is an El Segundo, CA-based startup building the world’s first mass-produced, portable nuclear microreactors. The company’s first reactor, Kaleidos, is a 1-megawatt, fail-safe microreactor that can be transported anywhere power is needed and run for up to 5 years without refueling. Portable nuclear power with rapid-deploy capability can replace similar-sized diesel generators and provide critical asset support for hospitals, data centers, remote sites, and military bases. Radiant’s unique, practical approach to nuclear development leverages modern software engineering to rapidly deliver safe, factory-built microreactors that use existing, well-qualified materials. Founded in 2020, Radiant is on track to test its first reactor at the Idaho National Laboratory this summer, with initial customer deliveries beginning in 2028.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Radiant is seeking a Senior Safety Analysis Engineer to lead reactor safety analyses supporting the design, testing, and deployment of Kaleidos. You will evaluate reactor behavior during normal, transient, and accident conditions, assess safety margins, and develop technically defensible analyses that inform reactor design decisions and regulatory evaluations.

This role combines reactor systems and thermal-hydraulic analysis with fuel performance, source term development, and radiological consequence assessments. You will own complex analytical work from methodology development and model execution through uncertainty evaluation, technical review, and documentation, working closely with nuclear design, thermal, mechanical, materials, testing, and regulatory teams.

The ideal candidate brings strong reactor safety fundamentals, hands-on modeling experience, and sound engineering judgment. You should be comfortable identifying dominant physical phenomena, evaluating analytical uncertainties, and translating complex results into practical design and safety decisions.




RESPONSIBILITIES & DUTIES

 - Lead deterministic reactor safety analyses covering anticipated operational occurrences, transients, and postulated accident scenarios.

 - Develop and apply system-level thermal-hydraulic and transient models to evaluate reactor response, operating limits, and safety margins.

 - Perform source term and radiological consequence analyses, including fuel performance, fission product release and transport, and dose evaluations.

 - Evaluate uncertainties in reactor physics, power distributions, fuel behavior, and thermal-hydraulic models and their impact on safety conclusions.

 - Apply sensitivity studies, bounding assumptions, and phenomena-ranking methods to develop technically defensible analysis approaches.

 - Collaborate with nuclear, mechanical, thermal, materials, and controls teams to establish analysis inputs, evaluate design alternatives, and resolve safety-related technical challenges.

 - Partner with testing and materials teams to identify data gaps, establish validation requirements, and correlate analytical predictions with experimental results.

 - Develop and improve safety analysis methods, models, and tools, including verification and validation, configuration control, and uncertainty quantification.

 - Prepare and technically review calculation packages, safety analysis reports, and regulatory documentation supporting reactor design and licensing activities.

 - Work with regulatory and safety teams to establish safety requirements, support technical submissions, and resolve technical issues through closure.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS & SKILLS

 - Bachelor's degree in nuclear engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related technical discipline from an accredited institution.

 - 5+ years of relevant experience in reactor safety analysis, thermal-hydraulics, nuclear systems modeling, or related engineering disciplines.

 - Experience developing and applying reactor systems or safety analysis codes such as RELAP5-3D, TRACE, SAM, MELCOR, or equivalent tools.

 - Strong understanding of reactor thermal-hydraulics, transient behavior, heat transfer, and deterministic safety analysis.

 - Knowledge of reactor physics, fuel performance, fission product behavior, and radiological safety principles.

 - Experience developing or evaluating source terms, radiological consequences, or other safety-related performance calculations.

 - Experience evaluating modeling assumptions, uncertainty, sensitivity, and conservatism in engineering analyses.

 - Demonstrated ability to independently own complex analytical projects and translate results into design requirements, safety conclusions, and technical documentation.

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience preparing rigorous calculation packages, technical reports, or safety-related engineering documentation.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS & SKILLS

 - Master's degree or Ph.D. in nuclear engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related technical discipline.

 - Experience with high-temperature gas-cooled reactors, microreactors, advanced reactors, or first-of-a-kind nuclear systems.

 - Experience with TRISO fuel performance, irradiation behavior, fuel failure mechanisms, and fission product release and transport.

 - Familiarity with source term, dose consequence, or fuel performance tools such as ORIGEN, MACCS, PARFUME, or BISON.

 - Experience with reactor physics and neutronics tools such as MCNP, OpenMC, Serpent, or SCALE.

 - Familiarity with probabilistic risk assessment (PRA), licensing basis event selection, and risk-informed safety methodologies.

 - Experience with safety analysis code verification and validation, uncertainty quantification, and nuclear quality assurance practices.

 - Familiarity with DOE authorization processes, NRC licensing frameworks, nuclear industry codes and standards, or regulatory safety analysis.

 - Experience supporting reactor testing, safety basis development, regulatory submissions, or technical engagement with regulators.


ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

 - Must be mission driven and willing to support extended hours when needed.

 - Must work 100% onsite at Radiant's El Segundo headquarters.


BENEFITS AND PERKS

 - Stock: Substantial incentive stock plan for all full-time employees.

 - Medical: 100% up to base silver level plan for employee + 50% dependents, offers up to Platinum plans.

 - One Medical: Sponsored memberships for employees and their dependents.

 - Vision: 100% top tier plan coverage + 50% for dependents.

 - Dental: 100% top tier plan coverage, orthodontia extra, 50% for dependents.

 - Voluntary life, accident, hospital, critical illness, commuter and FSA/HSA are offered as employee contributed benefits.

 - 8-weeks of paid parental leave for all parents. Additional paid pregnancy leave for CA employees.

 - Daily catered lunch. Free snacks and drinks.

 - Flexible PTO policy. Remote workday allocation.

 - Company and team-bonding events, happy hours and in-person camaraderie.

 - Beautiful El Segundo headquarters close to the Pacific Ocean.



Total Compensation and Benefits
Radiant compensates people for impact and invests in those who continue to raise the bar. Radiant’s new hire compensation package includes base salary, substantial equity grants, and comprehensive health benefits. Total compensation and level are determined through a rigorous evaluation of interview performance, experience, education, and qualifications, and are designed to support continued growth as scope, responsibility, and impact expand at Radiant.

We are an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, pregnancy, age, national origin, disability status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Portable nuclear power with rapid-deploy capability can replace similar-sized diesel generators and provide critical asset support for hospitals, data centers, remote sites, and military bases. RESPONSIBILITIES & DUTIES

 - Own test activities from requirements definition and planning through execution, data analysis, and documentation.

THE OPPORTUNITY:


As a Staff Product Manager, you’ll set the standard for how every AI-powered feature in Abby’s platform reaches a caregiver or a clinician. You’ll operate across Abby’s core products (caregiver and clinician) making sure the signal a caregiver captures contributes to the judgement a clinician acts on.

Part of your responsibility is to ensure AI features are ready to leave shadow mode and to ensure that the AI portfolio is trustworthy, coherent, and shipped with rigor. At the Staff level, you are expected to be a force multiplier: operating with high autonomy,, closely partnering closely with our founder, clinical, and engineering leadership to redefine what is possible in home-based care, and influencing how the entire product organization thinks about AI.

 - Define the Evaluation Standard: Own the gate clinical or caregiver-facing AI features have to clear. Decide what “ready” means and raise the bar for features to get there.

 - Own Cross-Surface AI Consistency: A patient’s baseline, care plan, and chart notes are read and written by both the caregiver and clinician products. Ensure that those systems reason about the same patient the same way, so a signal captured on one surface is reflected in the other.

 - Set the Bar for AI Product Development: : Partner closely with the PMs on other product areas to raise the standard of their AI-feature specs, their evaluation criteria, and their partnership with Applied AI.

 - Partner Directly with Applied AI Leadership: Work at the architecture level on how caregiver AI and clinician AI are evaluated, monitored, and iterated post-launch.

 - Build for Regulated, Clinically Critical Ground Truth: Ensure that evaluation frameworks hold up against clinical scrutiny and payer/compliance review. Partner with clinical leadership and compliance to make sure that products measured against clinician dispositions are rigorous enough to trust.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE:

 - Clinical or caregiver-facing AI features that reach production clear a documented shadow-mode evaluation against real dispositions.

 - Caregiver-side and clinician-side AI systems can be proven to reason consistently about the same patient with no contradicting baselines or signals that are dropped at the handoff between surfaces.

 - Other AI PMs at Abby Care treat your evaluation standard as the bar.


WHAT YOU’LL HAVE:

 - Experience: 8+ years of product management experience, with a proven track record of leading complex, high-impact AI or ML product initiatives at a Staff or Lead PM level in a high-growth tech environment.

 - AI Product Depth: Direct experience designing evaluation frameworks for AI systems in production and deciding how AI features’ real-world performance is measured, monitored, and gated before and after launch.

 - Technical Fluency: Strong technical acumen, particularly in working with engineering and Applied ML and AI teams to build data-intensive or AI-driven platforms. You don't need to write code, but you must be able to deeply evaluate technical trade-offs.

 - Customer Obsession: Deep empathy for users (in our case, family caregivers and care recipients) and a rigorous approach to qualitative and quantitative research in a regulated environment.

 - Relentless Resourcefulness: You thrive in fast-paced startup environments. You adapt quickly, solve challenges with creativity, and deliver results without unnecessary complexity.

 - Exceptional Communication: The ability to distill complex healthcare and technical concepts into clear, actionable product requirements and compelling strategic narratives for executive stakeholders.


BONUS / NICE TO HAVE:

 - Experience in HealthTech, Medicaid waivers, or highly regulated industries where AI decisions carry compliance or clinical-safety weight.

 - A strong background working with LLMs, machine learning, or AI-native consumer products.

 - Previous experience navigating a marketplace or labor-supply business model (e.g., gig economy, digital health).


BENEFITS:

 - Competitive compensation packages that reflect the value you bring. We reward our team for the impact of their work.

 - Comprehensive health coverage that works for you. Choose from high-quality medical dental and vision options, including a $0 deductible PPO and a company-funded HSA, alongside employer-paid life and disability insurance.

 - Generous paid time off. We provide policies that allow you to recharge along with 10 paid company holidays.

 - Financial savings benefits to support your future. We support your financial well-being with HSA contributions, optional FSA and commuter benefits, and full coverage of all 401(k) account fees (employer match not currently offered).

 - Paid parental leave to support your growing family. We provide up to 10 weeks of paid parental leave based on tenure, so you can focus on bonding and adjusting to life as your family grows.




OUR VALUES

    Redefining healthcare starts with how we treat the parents and children we serve. We go above and beyond for every family, building strong, lasting relationships. We continually ask ourselves, “Would we want this for our own families?”

 2. Urgency with Precision
    Millions of families are waiting for care, and they cannot wait, therefore this is not your typical 9 to 5 job. We match their urgency with our own, delivering exceptional care without compromise. Here, speed and excellence go hand in hand.

    As an ambitious startup, we adapt quickly and make the most of limited time and resources. We solve challenges with creativity to deliver results without unnecessary complexity.

jobs.title: Account Director, Crypto
jobs.description:
BUILD A SAFER WORLD.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

TRM is on a mission to build a safer financial system for billions of people. We deliver a blockchain intelligence data platform to financial institutions, crypto companies, and governments to fight cryptocurrency fraud and financial crime. We consider our business — and our profit — as a way to move towards our mission sustainably and at scale. 

The Sales Account Director for crypto-first businesses will lead the go-to-market strategy to increase and strengthen our foothold in the space. We're looking for a customer-obsessed, consultative salesperson to own the entire sales process with new customers. This person will be knowledgeable about the cryptocurrency ecosystem and feel comfortable navigating both complex six-figure deals and fast-moving transactional deals. 

Responsibilities:

 - Own the end-to-end sales process with new customers -- from researching opportunities to tailoring their sales approach to prospects' needs to closing deals -- across crypto-first businesses.

 - Write client proposals (sometimes, from scratch) and negotiate contracts / SOWs.

 - Develop and leverage an in-depth understanding of client needs and key initiatives, tailor sales approach to specific business needs, and map these to TRM products.

 - Generate, maintain, and report against an ongoing pipeline of strategic opportunities to meet and exceed sales targets.

 - Actively seek to understand industry trends to help position against competitors.

 - Gather and distribute product feedback from clients and prospects to the sales and product teams to help us continually enhance our product offerings.

What we’re looking for

 - 5+ years of B2B SaaS sales experience with a demonstrated ability to consistently deliver against net new sales targets.

 - Strong customer-facing presentation/listening skills with the aptitude to establish credibility with senior financial and compliance executives.

 - Natural storyteller with the capacity to understand customer needs and convey compelling value propositions.

 - Exceptional communication and problem-solving skills.

 - Strong knowledge of cryptocurrencies, digital assets, and/or blockchains.

 - Familiarity with regulatory initiatives and changes related to cryptocurrency; understanding of Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Know Your Customer (KYC) regulatory frameworks.

 - Previous experience working in a fast-paced, growing startup environment.

 - Additionally, this role may be eligible to participate in TRM’s equity plan.

 - Please note – we factor in the different costs for geographies outside the United States.

About the team:

 - The Private Sector Business Development team is made of independent sales leaders who take ownership and initiative of their territory and responsibilities. Because we’re a global team, each team member is a master of their own territory.

 - We work asynchronously to share intel, win strategies, and support one another when prospects cross time zones.

 - Knowing the impact that our work has on the future of TRM, we’re scrappy and find ways to get things done and overcome any challenges that come our way.

 - Each team member works according to typical business hours in their territory. At times, it’s necessary for the team to meet together a few hours earlier or later than an individual’s local business hours, but those occasions are planned in advance.

Learn about TRM Speed in this position:

 - Returning prospect and customer communications within 24 hours at most, typically faster.

 - Raising any customer concerns to the relevant internal teams promptly and ensuring

 - Responding to internal requests (asks re: customer, prospect, and market information that can range from small to large projects) as quickly as possible.


APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.




INTERVIEWING WITH TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

 - Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

 - Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

 - First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

 - Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

 - References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.

 - Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.

 - Welcome to TRM: We're excited to build a safer world with you!

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.




AI FLUENCY AT TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

 - Accelerate repeatable workflows

 - Structure and solve problems

 - Improve output quality

 - Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.




LIFE AT TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

 - Priorities and targets to change quickly

 - Operating with a high degree of ambiguity

 - A high level of personal ownership and accountability

 - Close collaboration across teams and functions

 - Frequent, high-touch communication

 - Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

 - A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute. 




LEADERSHIP PRINCIPLES

jobs.title: Manager, RF Manufacturing Test Engineering
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril’s Manufacturing team is seeking a Manager, RF Manufacturing Test Engineering to join our team. The EW Manufacturing Team is responsible for rapidly iterating and building cutting-edge defense hardware for Electromagnetic Warfare.

We aim to develop and deploy critically needed capabilities that address our customers’ most pressing national security requirements. As the Manager, RF Manufacturing Test Engineering, your role encompasses the strategic oversight and tactical management of production systems to support high-volume products across the portfolio. You are charged with ensuring rigorous testing protocols are in place, resulting in the consistent delivery of superior quality products to our customers. Furthermore, your leadership guarantees the fulfillment of manufacturing's test throughput requirements. This position demands an innovative approach to resolving complex testing challenges, advancing scalability, and enhancing our automation, throughput, user interfaces, and data analytics methodologies.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Direct the manufacturing test engineering team, set objectives, guide initiatives, and assess team outcomes.

• Oversee and consistently contribute improvements of the manufacturing test strategy for each product to ensure scalable operations across Anduril, transitioning from pre-production to full-scale output.

• Collaborate with product SEIT and development engineering for design testability, ensuring seamless production integration.

• Strategize and implement advancements in manufacturing testing, focusing on automation, uniformity, and operational streamlining.

• Maintain test capabilities of multiple products across their respective manufacturing value stream - from system level checkouts and acceptance testing to key component level in process validation.

• Evaluate test data, compile findings, and identify opportunities for product and process enhancements.

• Communicate strategic visions to key stakeholders, guiding the scaling of platforms from pre-production (LRIP) through to mass production (FRP).

• Lead the procurement and implementation of new test equipment, performing cost-benefit and ROI analyses as needed.

• Champion initiatives that enhance safety, reduce costs, improve quality, and increase productivity through testing.

• Cultivate a culture focused on innovation, collaboration, and accountability in the engineering department.

• Act as the go-to technical authority for manufacturing test matters, advising on and troubleshooting complex issues.

• Design proactive maintenance and calibration protocols for manufacturing test equipment.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• 8+ years of relevant industry experience with emphasis on manufacturing test and product sustainment.

• Bachelor’s degree in Electrical/Electronics, Computer, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field.

• Minimum of 2+ years as a people manager leading manufacturing test engineering or relevant adjacent fields.

• Experienced in Linux, C#, Python, NixOS, LabView, or other forms of test automation.

• Experience with computer hardware communication protocols: USB, Ethernet, RS232, RS485, PCIe, HDMI, CAN, etc.

• Solid experience with PCBA/electronic assembly testing and knowledge of testing standards including and not limited to: acceptance testing, EOL testing, and ESS testing.

• Proficiency in using electronic and RF test equipment.

• Strong analytical skills for root cause analysis of non-conforming electro-mechanical hardware

• Familiar with Test Execution Systems (TES), Product Life Cycle (PLM) systems, Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems.

• Experience in managing projects that integrate electrical, mechanical, and software/firmware systems.

• Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Demonstrated ability to lead the development of manufacturing test systems and teams.

• Proficiency in LabVIEW, MATLAB, and test automation.

• Knowledge of PCBA design and mechanical design

• Familiarity with various hardware communication protocols.

• Experience with designing HASS & ESS-related tests (Thermal, Vibration, etc.).

• Familiarity in using AI tools

US Salary Range

$146,000—$194,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

• No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

• Please always verify communications: Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address. Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

• Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

• What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.

By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

jobs.title: Senior Applied AI Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT ABBY CARE: POWERING THE FUTURE OF CARE AT HOME FOR ALL OF AMERICA.


Abby Care is building the leading AI-native platform for family-led care. America is facing a growing care crisis. Millions more people need care at home than ever. Over 50 million family caregivers support loved ones without the tools, training, or recognition they deserve.

We believe families are the largest untapped caregiving workforce in America, and that technology can help them deliver better care while driving stronger outcomes and greater transparency across the healthcare system.

Abby Care combines clinical oversight with an AI-powered platform to train, enable, and support family caregivers in delivering high-quality care at home. Our platform helps health plans and government partners better understand, verify, and improve care in the home. We expand access to care, reduce reliance on higher-cost settings, and help ensure public dollars are spent effectively.

We are proud to partner with leading health plans, providers, and community organizations and are backed by top VCs. We envision a future where family-led care is a core part of the healthcare system. Abby Care is building that future.

Join us in solving one of the most important challenges of our time.




THE OPPORTUNITY

Abby Care is building an AI-native operating system for home care—one that manages the full lifecycle from caregiver and patient intake through care delivery, billing, and compliance.

As we expand our capacity to support more family caregivers at scale, we’re looking for a Senior Applied AI Engineer to design and build production AI systems that automate complex, consequential healthcare workflows. Reporting to the Applied AI Leader, you will own major initiatives from initial problem definition through production deployment and measurable impact.

Depending on the problem, you may build an agent that collects clinical documentation, interprets evidence across multiple records, prepares a prior authorization packet, assists a nurse during a visit, identifies billing risk, or coordinates operational follow-up.

You will determine how workflows should be decomposed, what context and tools an AI system needs, how its behavior should be evaluated, where deterministic controls are required, and when a human must intervene. You will work closely with product engineers, product managers, designers, clinicians, operators, and analysts to ensure that the systems you build reflect real-world workflows and produce meaningful outcomes.

High-agency and pragmatic, you are comfortable operating in ambiguity, moving between experimentation and production engineering, and owning technically complex systems end to end. If you are excited to apply frontier AI capabilities to difficult, high-impact problems while transforming care in the home, we’d love to hear from you!

This is a full-time hybrid opportunity based in San Francisco, California, with four days per week in person.




WHAT YOU’LL WORK ON

 - Own high-impact AI systems end to end: Lead initiatives from workflow discovery and technical design through production deployment, iteration, and measurable business or care outcomes.

 - Build reliable agents and copilots: Develop systems that reason over structured and unstructured data, use internal tools, and execute multi-step workflows across intake, care delivery, billing, and operations.

 - Engineer for real-world complexity: Design systems that handle incomplete information, conflicting evidence, changing requirements, and operational edge cases by combining models, retrieval, rules, state machines, and human oversight.

 - Build rigorous evaluation and monitoring: Create representative datasets, evaluation harnesses, production tracing, confidence-based escalation, and systematic error-analysis processes.

 - Integrate AI into complete workflows: Partner with Product, Design, Clinical, Operations, Analytics, Platform, and System of Record engineers to ensure AI capabilities solve real problems rather than remain isolated prototypes.

 - Raise the technical bar: Contribute reusable platform capabilities, shape architectural decisions, mentor engineers, and improve how the team builds and operates Applied AI systems.



WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - You independently own and deliver complex Applied AI systems from discovery through sustained production operation.

 - The systems you build create measurable improvements in workflow completion, speed, quality, operational capacity, or family experience.

 - AI behavior is supported by representative evaluations, systematic error analysis, and clear production monitoring.

 - Your systems respond safely to uncertainty through confidence handling, escalation, and human approval where appropriate.

 - AI capabilities are integrated into end-to-end product and operational workflows rather than remaining isolated prototypes.

 - The components you build are reusable across use cases and improve the velocity of the broader engineering organization.

 - You help other engineers make better architectural and implementation decisions through technical leadership and mentorship.

 - You develop a deep understanding of Abby Care’s operational and clinical domains and use that understanding to improve the systems you build.


WHAT YOU’LL HAVE

 - 5+ years of professional software engineering, machine learning, or Applied AI experience.

 - Experience building and operating AI- or machine-learning-powered systems in production.

 - Strong hands-on experience with language models, retrieval systems, structured generation, model APIs, or agent architectures.

 - Strong software engineering fundamentals, including backend systems, APIs, data modeling, testing, and observability.

 - Experience designing evaluations and analyzing the behavior of probabilistic systems.

 - Demonstrated ability to take ownership of ambiguous, cross-functional problems and drive them through implementation and iteration.

 - Strong judgment about where AI is appropriate and where deterministic approaches or human review are required.

 - Ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly to technical and nontechnical partners.

 - Experience mentoring engineers, leading technically complex projects, or influencing architectural decisions.

 - Must reside in or be willing to permanently relocate to the San Francisco Bay Area.

 - Experience with model fine-tuning, post-training, reinforcement learning, synthetic data generation, multimodal models, document intelligence, knowledge graphs, ontologies, workflow engines, or state machines is preferred but not required.

 - Experience in healthcare, fintech, insurance, or another regulated and operations-intensive environment is preferred but not required.

Benefits

 - Competitive compensation packages that reflect the value you bring. We reward our team for the impact of their work.

 - Comprehensive health coverage that works for you. Choose from high-quality medical dental and vision options, including a $0 deductible PPO and a company-funded HSA, alongside employer-paid life and disability insurance.

 - Generous paid time off. We provide policies that allow you to recharge along with 10 paid company holidays.

 - Financial savings benefits to support your future. We support your financial well-being with HSA contributions, optional FSA and commuter benefits, and full coverage of all 401(k) account fees (employer match not currently offered).

 - Paid parental leave to support your growing family. We provide paid leave, so you can focus on bonding and adjusting to life as your family grows.




OUR VALUES

 1. Families First
    Redefining healthcare starts with how we treat the parents and children we serve. We go above and beyond for every family, building strong, lasting relationships. We continually ask ourselves, “Would we want this for our own families?”

 2. Urgency with Precision
    Millions of families are waiting for care, and they cannot wait, therefore this is not your typical 9 to 5 job. We match their urgency with our own, delivering exceptional care without compromise. Here, speed and excellence go hand in hand.

 3. Relentlessly Resourceful
    As an ambitious startup, we adapt quickly and make the most of limited time and resources. We solve challenges with creativity to deliver results without unnecessary complexity.

 4. Purpose with Positivity
    We take our mission seriously while never losing sight of the people behind the work. Respect, kindness, memes, and coffee make us stronger as a team and better for the families we serve.

 5. Driven to Redefine What’s Possible
    We are here to make healthcare better, which means asking hard questions, challenging outdated systems, and finding smarter, more compassionate ways to deliver care.



Equal Opportunity Employer

Abby Care is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, national origin, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis. If you have a disability and require reasonable accommodation during any portion of the application or hiring process, contact talent@abbycare.org.



Abby Care considers qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records for employment and conducts background checks consistent with applicable law, including the California, Los Angeles County, San Francisco, Philadelphia, and New York City Fair Chance laws. We are an E-Verify participating company.



Automated Decision Tools

Abby Care may use automated decision tools to help match and rank candidate work experience, education and skills found in online profiles, resumes and job applications against job requirements. We believe that these tools help ensure objective, data-based decisions during the hiring process, however, all Abby Care hiring decisions involve final human review and input. jobs.title: Hospice Clinical Director (Kansas City, KS)
jobs.description:
About Us

Ennoble Care is a mobile primary care, palliative care, and hospice service provider with patients in New York, New Jersey, Maryland, DC, Virginia, Oklahoma, Kansas, Pennsylvania, Texas, Florida, and Georgia. Ennoble Care’s clinicians go to the home of the patient, providing continuum of care for those with chronic conditions and limited mobility. Ennoble Care offers a variety of programs including, remote patient monitoring, behavioral health management, and chronic care management, to ensure that our patients receive the highest quality of care by a team they know and trust. We seek individuals who are driven to make a difference and embody our motto, “To Care is an Honor.” Join Ennoble Care today!

Job Summary:

The Hospice Clinical Director is responsible for ensuring the coordination and management of patient care. Assists the Director of Nursing in maintaining the quality of patient care in accordance with the Agency’s objectives and policies, through planning, coordination, implementation and evaluation of the hospice services provided.  This market services the Kansas City region in Kansas.

RESPONSIBILITES

• Coordinate and oversee direct and indirect patient services provided by clinical personnel.

• Provide supervision and guidance to clinical staff to ensure the quality of services and maintenance of standards.

• Perform chart audits.

• Gather data for QAPI and participates in QAPI activities.

• Appraise clinical staff performance during their probationary period and annually, provides the teaching and counseling necessary to enhance the delivery of services and the professional development of nursing and health aide staff.

• Identify and evaluate patient needs and appropriateness of home care by reviewing the initial intake screening form before assignment of direct care staff. Assist with the orientation of new staff. See patients in the home setting as needed. Maintains adequate and appropriate Medical Supplies.

• Assists with orientation of new personnel as well as in-services for current staff.

• Responsible for ensuring Medicare, State and ACHC regulations are followed by all clinical staff.

• Assists the Director of Nursing with responsibilities as requested.

• Assume responsibility for self-development by continually striving to improve his/her Nursing/management practice through formal education, attendance at workshops and conferences, active participation in professional and related organizational meetings, and/or individual research and reading.

JOB CONDITIONS

• Position may be stressful.

• Primarily a desk job which involves minimal and occasional lifting of medical supplies and charts.

• On occasion, one may be required to bend, stoop, reach and move patient weight up to 250 pounds lift and/or carry up to 30 pounds.

• Travel is required to and from patient's home when supervision of care is scheduled.

• The ability to access patients’ homes which may not be routinely wheelchair accessible is required.

• Hearing, eyesight and physical dexterity must be sufficient to perform a physical assessment of the patient's condition and to perform patient care.

jobs.title: Manager, National Accounts
jobs.description:
ABOUT MURAD

Founded by board-certified dermatologist and pharmacist Dr. Howard Murad, Murad is a dermatologist-developed skincare brand built on the belief that skincare is healthcare. Inspired by Dr. Murad's lifelong commitment to science-backed wellness, we create high-performance products and experiences designed to support healthier skin and happier lives.

At Murad, we bring together science, innovation and a holistic approach to wellness to help people look, feel and live better.

THE OPPORTUNITY

We are looking for a Manager, National Accounts to join our National Sales team. Reporting to the Director of Sales and Operations, this role will own our acquisition and liquidation channels end to end — secondary-market retailers (TJ Maxx, Ross) and subscription boxes (Ipsy, FabFitFun, Allure), where the bulk of this business sits, plus high-visibility placements like Good Morning America steals and deals — driving profitable growth that aligns with Murad's brand strategy and marketing calendar.

The ideal candidate will bring 4–6 years of headquarter selling or retailer account management with direct experience at these specific customers, advanced Excel and analytical skills, and the agency to navigate ambiguity and build processes in a small, fast-moving team — and will thrive in a collaborative, fast-paced environment.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Own the acquisition and liquidation channels end to end — sales process, timelines, forecasts, deliverables, internal approvals, cross-functional follow-up, and communication — for assigned National retail partners, including TJ Maxx, Ross, subscription boxes (Ipsy, FabFitFun, Allure), and broadcast retail placements.

• Think forward, not transactional: define the role each customer plays in the business, identify growth opportunities per partner, and secure placements that maximize brand relevance, consumer reach, and margins.

• Deliver SKU-level, bottoms-up sales forecasting and demand planning; partner with supply chain and operations on units, pricing, and inventory to hit sales targets and maintain target margins.

• Build and protect margins — develop margin models and deal parameters (lowest acceptable to highest offer), ensure every deal lands at margins finance will approve, and route discontinued or excess product to the right channels rather than high-visibility placements.

• Own the channel activation calendar and lead business reviews and post-program recaps that surface performance trends, key learnings, risks, and actionable recommendations.

• Navigate ambiguity and build the playbook — proactively hunt down answers across teams, codify learnings into SOPs and standardized processes, and help the team operate more nimbly.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

• Minimum 4–6 years in headquarter selling / retailer account management, with direct experience at TJ Maxx, Ross, or subscription-box programs (Ipsy, FabFitFun, Allure) — required.

• Advanced Excel proficiency (non-negotiable) with strong analytical skills — able to manage, analyze, and communicate data: forecasts, pricing, COGS, and margin analyses.

• True ownership and accountability — owns the business end to end, from deal negotiation through execution and recaps.

• Strategic thinking with strong business acumen and business writing skills; able to communicate, collaborate, and influence across cross-functional teams and external partners.

• Comfort navigating ambiguity — in a small but mighty team, proactively seeks out answers and builds SOPs and processes rather than waiting for direction.

• Clear, precise communication — independently develops clear, accurate, audience-appropriate materials and presentations for internal leadership and external partners.

• Detail-oriented with precise execution — validates forecasts, pricing, COGS, SKU, and inventory data against source documents; manages multiple concurrent projects and priorities in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.

NICE TO HAVE

• Beauty or skincare category experience — the ability to speak the language of beauty retail: category margins, product lifecycles, and how to pitch newness and core assortment while routing various products to the right channels, tying assortment decisions to brand strategy and the marketing calendar.

• Operations or supply chain experience —cross-functional flow between sales, supply chain, and finance (quantities, routings, inventory, demand planning). The ability to understand the ops side to anticipate constraints, keep deals, and manage a deal from start to finish.

• Oracle experience — the ability to pull and analyze data across SKU-level sales, forecasts, margin analyses to find opportunities

• Experience with logistics software or shipping platforms — attention to detail on numbers, margins, and routings is crucial in this channel, and a great candidate is comfortable in the logistics detail and the operational follow-through.

HOW WE WORK

At Murad, how we work matters just as much as what we deliver. Our values guide how we show up for our consumers, our customers and one another:

• Push for Extraordinary

• Respect. Connect. Appreciate.

• Dare to Take Risks

• Be a Voice, Not an Echo

• See the World Through Their Eyes

• Spread Wellness and Positive Vibes

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

jobs.title: Inventory Control Technician
jobs.description:
ABOUT FLUIDSTACK

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it. 


We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!




HOW WE OPERATE

 - Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

 - Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

 - Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

 - Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

 - Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.




ROLE SCOPE

 - Execute the daily cycle count reconciliation for five data center sites and warehouses from the WMS count export, following the documented method step for step: dedupe the scans, net shortages against recorded transactions, and publish each site's variance tracker before the morning deadline, seven days a week on a rotation.

 - Post the WMS corrections each variance calls for (quantity adjustments with reason codes, location transfers, part alias fixes) within the authority limits set by the Program Manager, Inventory Control, and log the site lead's root cause and resolution on every row until it closes.

 - Request same-day recounts and bin checks through the established site contacts, confirm the results land in the system, and verify on the next count that the correction held.

 - Triage every below-minimum and zero-on-hand alert the day it fires against the alert decision tree, enter and maintain min/max values and exception fixes as directed, and escalate anything the rules do not cover to the Program Manager the same day.

 - Prepare the system-pulled, cross-checked inputs for the daily customer count report and the weekly accuracy review, and work the record-integrity backlog (17,000+ serialized assets without a location, duplicate bin records, 3PL discrepancy lists) against the plan and dates the Program Manager sets.
   


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would. https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/fluidstack/05c2e69c-42f9-4fcb-9cf0-a467aaf98f1c

 - You've done cycle counts and variance reconciliation as a daily job in a WMS, and you can show a tracker or log you kept current for months.

 - You work a documented procedure the same way every day, and when a step does not fit the situation you flag it and take action.

 - You find the wrong row with lookups, pivots, dedupe and formula checks, and you've caught your own errors before anyone else saw them.

 - You've posted adjustments and transfers in an inventory system with reason codes, and you know which ones you're allowed to post yourself and which ones need a sign-off.

 - You've asked a warehouse team you don't work beside to recount a bin the same day, and you closed the loop when the result came back.

 - You've kept a seven-day cadence on a rotation, working remotely from the operation you support, and your Sunday output looks the same as your Tuesday output.

 - Bonus: WMS systems (SAP EWM, NetSuite, Manhattan, DCIM platforms). Data center hardware (optics, trays, network switches, GPU servers). Spreadsheet automation or query languages (Apps Script, SQL). Barcode or RFID scanning workflows.
   


SALARY & BENEFITS

 - Competitive total compensation package (salary + equity).

 - Retirement or pension plan, in line with local norms.

 - Health, dental, and vision insurance.
   
   - Generous PTO policy, in line with local norms.
     
     Total compensation may also include equity in the form of restricted stock units.



We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

About Us

Ennoble Care is a mobile primary care, palliative care, and hospice service provider with patients in New York, New Jersey, Maryland, DC, Virginia, Oklahoma, Kansas, Pennsylvania, Texas, Florida, and Georgia. Ennoble Care’s clinicians go to the home of the patient, providing continuum of care for those with chronic conditions and limited mobility. Ennoble Care offers a variety of programs including, remote patient monitoring, behavioral health management, and chronic care management, to ensure that our patients receive the highest quality of care by a team they know and trust. We seek individuals who are driven to make a difference and embody our motto, “To Care is an Honor.” Join Ennoble Care today!

Job Summary:

Ennoble Care is hiring for a Full-time Hospice Registered Nurse Case Manager to work within and around the Rockdale / Dekalb / Newton County, GA and surrounding areas. As a member of the interdisciplinary team, the RN Case Manager works under the general direction of the Director of Nursing, the attending physician and the interdisciplinary group in providing skilled nursing assessments, planning, and care in order to maximize the comfort and health of both patients and their loved ones/caregivers.

Responsibilities:

• Shall be assigned patient caseload by the Patient Care Coordinator or designee

• Assume primary responsibility for a patient caseload that includes the assessing, planning, implementing and evaluating phases of the nursing process

• Initiate communication with attending physicians, Hospice staff members and other agencies as needed to coordinate optimal care and use of resources for the patient and loved ones/caregivers

• Maintain regular communication with the attending physician concerning patient and loved ones/caregivers

• Seek input from other team members regarding the patient plan of care to obtain additional knowledge and support

• Provide accurate and timely documentation in electronic medical records.

• Participates in and contributes appropriate information for Interdisciplinary Group meetings

• Accept responsibility for coordinating physical care of the patient by teaching primary caregivers, volunteers, and employed caregivers or by providing direct care as appropriate

• Meet regularly with the Hospice nursing staff to review problems or unique issues from caseloads; share professional support; and exchange feedback aimed toward enhancing professional growth

• Attend patient care conferences and facilitate discussion of issues from caseload for full staff discussion, consultation and evaluation

• Supervise and document the NAC every two weeks or as assigned

• Inform the Patient Care Coordinator of unusual or potentially problematic patient/family issues

• Assume the role of associate nurse when responding to patient/loved ones/caregivers of other primary nurses during off-hour times or as requested by the Patient Care Coordinator to fill patient/family needs during the absence of other primary nurses

• Provide appropriate support at time of death and period of bereavement

• Participate in the Hospice orientation and in-service training programs for professional staff

• Participate in agency and community programs as required to promote professional growth and understanding of hospice care

• Maintain familiarity with policies of the agency and rules and regulations of State and Federal bodies which govern hospice

• Accept other assignments as appropriate

Qualifications:

• Must be a graduate from an accredited School of Nursing.

• Must be a Registered Nurse who is currently licensed to practice nursing under the provisions of Article 1 of Chapter 26 of Title 43 of the Official code of Georgia.

• One year of RN experience. Hospice experience preferred.

• CPR certified to care for patients without DNR’s

• Must have excellent assessment skills and problem solving skills.

• Should be skillful in organization and in the principles of time management and have knowledge of case management processes.

• Must be a licensed driver with an insured automobile in good working order.

• The ability to communicate well, both verbally and in writing.

• Must have no exceptions to RN license, and be able to administer pharmaceuticals, perform medication reconciliation, and any nursing procedures or special treatments needed within the scope of nursing practice for state. All skills to be competencied before actual hands on patient care, and when procedures or treatments are not usually performed.

jobs.title: Software Engineering Intern, Full Stack
jobs.description:
About Tessera Labs

Tessera Labs is redefining how enterprises adop and operationalize Artificial Intelligence. Backed by Foundation and with a recent $60M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), we build multi-agent AI Systems that automate complex business workflows across platforms like SAP, Salesforce, Workday, Snowflake, Databricks and more.

Our mission: bring real AI automation to the enterprise - with speed and precision and measurable impact. We move fast, operate with extreme ownership, and build at the frontier of applied AI.

About the role

We're hiring a Full Stack Software Engineering Intern to help build Tessera Mosaic, where AI agents work alongside people to transform how enterprises operate. You'll help drive product problems end to end, from interfaces for understanding and controlling agents to the data and backend systems that power them.

You'll work closely with product and design, with real ownership over what we build and how we build it. If you enjoy turning ambiguous problems into polished products, you can have an outsized impact on a platform that's still early. You can lean toward frontend or backend depending on your preference, or do both.

What you'll do

 - Build product features in React and TypeScript on the frontend and/or Python on the backend, including APIs, data models, and services.

 - Take problems from a rough starting point to shipped: figure out what's actually being asked, dig into the data and code, propose an approach, and build it.

 - Build the tools that make AI agents understandable and controllable for the people using them: seeing what an agent is doing, reviewing its work, and stepping in when needed.

 - Work with data from systems like SAP, Salesforce, and Oracle, including their complex data models and real-world edge cases.

 - Partner with product and design to question assumptions, shape solutions, get feedback early, and iterate.

What we're looking for

 - Strong product sense. You think about the people using what you build and have ideas about how to make it better, whether you're working on the frontend or the backend.

 - Experience building software, through class projects, side projects, or a previous internship. Any language is fine.

 - You learn quickly and can make progress on a problem without being told exactly what to do. We care far more about how fast you're growing than where you're starting.

 - Some comfort with data, like SQL and how tables relate to each other, and a willingness to learn whatever a feature needs, from the database to the UI.

 - You explain your thinking clearly and ask questions early.

 - Proactively ask for help when blocked and communicate openly about challenges.

Nice to have

 - You've built something with LLMs or agents.

 - Familiarity with React, TypeScript, or Python, which make up most of our stack.



Location: San Jose, CA, New York or Remote (U.S.)

Duration: 10–12 weeks

Hours: Up to 40 hours per week

Start Date: Fall 2026/Spring 2027/Summer 2027 (flexible)



Tessera Labs is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes candidates from all backgrounds and experiences.

 

No third party may recruit, solicit candidates, publish job opportunities, use Tessera Labs’ name or branding, or represent that they are acting on behalf of Tessera Labs without prior written authorization. Any such activity conducted without explicit written consent is strictly prohibited.
