jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Inference
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic’s Inference organization serves Claude to millions of users and enterprise customers, across our own products and the world’s largest cloud platforms, with the speed, reliability, and efficiency that frontier AI demands. The stack that makes this possible is deep and tightly coupled: accelerator kernels, an in-house inference engine that manages the entire token path for both production and research workloads, distributed routing, autoscaling, and capacity management. Every layer affects the others, often in ways that are hard to see in isolation. We build across GPUs, TPUs, and Trainium, and the complexity of building, testing, and shipping inference software grows with every platform we add.

We're looking for a Technical Program Manager to drive the programs that scale it. The work spans four closely coupled areas:

• Scaling and infrastructure. Routing, autoscaling, and capacity management for the serving fleet, and bringing new capacity online.

• Velocity. The toolchains, development environments, and CI/CD that let inference engineers build, test, and ship across every accelerator platform.

• Inference engine. The software between the accelerator kernels and the routing layer that serves every request.

• Performance. Improving throughput, latency, cost, and reliability across the stack, with correctness treated as part of performance.

This is not a status-tracking role. You'll own outcomes end to end, often where no single team is accountable for the whole picture. Much of your value comes from crossing boundaries into Research, Safeguards, Security, Compute, Infrastructure, API, and our cloud and silicon partners, and bringing back the requirements and dependencies that no team sees from inside its own space. There is little process to inherit, and we want to keep it that way: you'll build the minimum machinery the work needs and remove it when it stops helping. And because this is Anthropic, you'll have Claude as a collaborator. We expect TPMs on this team to push hard on what AI-assisted program management and fleet operations can look like.

Key responsibilities

• Own the programs that scale Claude’s serving fleet across accelerator and cloud platforms, from early direction through delivery.

• Drive new capacity online end to end, working across compute, infrastructure, security, networking, and inference teams so one person is accountable for the whole path.

• Build visibility into supply, demand, and utilization with capacity and finance partners, and drive trade-offs among utilization, cost, latency, and reliability to a clear decision.

• Lead reliability programs and large migrations without disrupting production traffic or research, and make sure incident follow-ups land in team roadmaps.

• Drive the programs that make inference engineers faster: define the productivity metrics that matter, find the bottlenecks, and improve how software is built, tested, and released across platforms, in step with Anthropic’s central Infrastructure org.

• Coordinate roadmaps and priorities across the production, research, and safeguards needs that depend on the same teams.

• Track performance and efficiency work from opportunity to measured impact in production, with correctness held as a release criterion.

• Own inference readiness for model launches alongside our launch TPMs.

Minimum qualifications

• 7+ years of experience as a TPM, or in an equivalent engineering or SRE lead role, owning large multi-team infrastructure programs end to end in production distributed systems, ML infrastructure, or cloud platforms. You can speak to the outcomes in detail, including where a program slipped and what you did about it.

• Technical fluency in large-scale serving infrastructure, including request routing and load balancing, autoscaling, capacity planning, cluster orchestration, deployment and rollout, and observability. You know enough to challenge a design, find the real risk, and add value beyond tracking.

• A working understanding of how LLM inference uses hardware (prefill and decode, batching, caching, compute versus memory bandwidth versus interconnect), or a track record of getting deep in an unfamiliar technical domain quickly.

• A track record of building program mechanisms from scratch on ambiguous, fast-moving efforts, and of retiring process that has stopped earning its keep.

• The ability to drive outcomes across organizations you don't manage, with competing priorities and unclear decision ownership. You read people and rooms well, know when to push and when to listen, and earn the trust of senior engineers and researchers.

• Strong written communication, including plans, reviews, and executive updates that many teams depend on.

• Low ego and high ownership. You do whatever the program needs, whether that is writing a script, running an incident bridge, or chasing a quota, and you care more about the outcome than about scope or credit.

• Care about Anthropic's mission and about serving frontier AI safely and reliably.

Preferred qualifications

• Direct experience with LLM or ML inference serving at scale, such as model servers, batching and scheduling, KV caching, quantization, speculative decoding, or multi-model routing.

• Experience with accelerator infrastructure (GPU, TPU, or Trainium), including cluster bring-up, hardware qualification, or running one workload across more than one accelerator platform.

• Experience managing capacity across multiple clouds or regions, including demand forecasting, headroom policy, cost modeling, or unit economics for compute-heavy services.

• Experience with developer productivity, release engineering, or CI/CD at scale, especially for hardware-dependent workloads, and with using engineering metrics to measurably raise velocity.

• Experience running performance or efficiency programs, with enough grounding in rooflines, kernels, ML compilers (XLA, Triton, Neuron), numerics, or collective communication to reason about trade-offs with the engineers doing the work.

• Familiarity with Kubernetes-based orchestration and job scheduling.

• Experience working with research teams and turning their needs into infrastructure requirements.

• Practical experience using AI tools in your own workflow, including building automations or agents, and clear ideas about where they help and where they don't.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:

$290,000—$435,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

jobs.title: Mid-level Software Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT SCHOOLHOUSE

Founded by Sal Khan, Schoolhouse http://schoolhouse.world/ is a peer-to-peer learning platform that delivers human connection and develops durable skills through online learning to best prepare students to thrive in the age of AI. So far, we’ve reached 200k+ learners from 180+ countries and we plan to grow to millions.


ABOUT THE VISION

Our vision is to provide an education safety net to ensure that no talent goes undiscovered and that every student feels empowered in our changing world. We do this by bringing high school students together around learning to create an environment where they can develop and showcase academic mastery and durable skills.

At Schoolhouse, learning is academic, civic, and global. Students join tutoring sessions where peers help them reach academic goals through personalized support. They participate in Dialogues to discuss challenging issues and empathize across divides. Above all, students belong to a global community centered around human connection.

We believe this vision is ambitious, so we need a team that can move quickly in the face of ambiguity. We value sincerity and empathy and believe deeply in the power of human connection. We step in to help each other out, we think big but start small, we uplift each other, and we’re all learners at heart.

Learn more about our vision and our values here:

 - Teen Helps 52-Year-Old Man Earn His High School Diploma https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZdIPGLgT8pk

 - The Power of Peer Tutoring https://schoolhouse.world/blog/the-power-of-peer-tutoring/

 - Schoolhouse’s Public Roadmap https://schoolhouse.world/roadmap

 - What are Schoolhouse's community values? https://schoolhouse.world/faq/en/article/what-are-schoolhouses-community-values-1b7nl3c/


ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for Mid-level Software Engineers who want to build stuff that’ll have an impact. You’ll join our 5-person engineering team and own full-stack features that hundreds of thousands of learners and tutors use worldwide.

Engineers at Schoolhouse have lots of ownership — you’ll work directly with our designer and other stakeholders to build out new experiments and streamline existing operations. We think the best way for engineers to build a quality product is to be involved early, drive progress, and stay close to our end users.

Scaling free quality interactions between students around the world comes with challenges that live at the intersection of UX, people ops, and technology. We need to both meet learner / tutor needs while ensuring that these interactions stay high quality and safe.

Some examples of what we’ve worked on include:

 - Building an AI simulation & coach to help tutors practice for their first tutoring session

 - Experimenting with new ways to connect tutors to learners wanting immediate homework help

 - Creating a moderation system to automatically recognize and act on safety issues so humans can focus their time on the most important issues

 

Responsibilities:

 - Work with users and teammates to understand problems, contribute product ideas, and take work from prototypes / experiments through deployment.

 - Scope work and make technical decisions with support from experienced teammates.

 - Write simple, readable code that’s easy to maintain and change.

 - Participate in code reviews and pairing sessions to help maintain codebase quality.


ABOUT YOU

If this sounds like you, we’d love for you to apply!

 - You’ve been a full-stack software engineer 3+ years and have a track record of building & shipping full-stack features.

 - You can explain the product and technical tradeoffs behind the approaches you’ve taken.

 - You have experience with Typescript, Node.js, React, Next.js, and Postgres (or can ramp up quickly).

 - You build for users & have a nose for understanding what would help them the most.

 - You move quickly while maintaining code quality. Perfect is the enemy of good.

 - You fill in the gaps — you ask for help, but still work independently to figure things out. If necessary you can put on another hat if it’ll help users the most.

 - You’re available to work in a US timezone.

Bonus points

 - You have deep technical experience with our stack Typescript, Node.js, React, Next.js, Postgres, AWS, and GCP.

 - You have experience building mobile apps.

 - You have experience working in education or on an ed-tech product.


LIFE AT SCHOOLHOUSE

 - Work with an amazing team. We’ve got folks with backgrounds in education, consulting, astrophysics, startups, and more.

 - Fully remote with flexible working hours. Meetings are in US Pacific Time mornings.

 - Take real time off. We have unlimited PTO & use it. Folks regularly take time off throughout the year.

 - Competitive salary and comprehensive benefits. Work-from-home stipend. Professional development budget. Health, dental, vision (for US employees).

 - Semesterly retreats and monthly regional meetups

 - Make an impact you can see. Check out our community stories page https://schoolhouse.world/stories. Watch students help each other learn. See tutors grow into leaders. Your code will help real people learn and grow.


ABOUT THE APPLICATION PROCESS

 - We might make some adjustments, but our expected interview process:

 - A 30-minute intro screen to learn more about you and understand whether this role is a mutual fit

 - A 45-minute screen where you'll read some code and brainstorm / prioritize product ideas

 - A 1-hour programming interview where you’ll fix bugs and implement features on a toy repo

 - A 1-hour systems design problem where you'll design a data model / api and handle challenges at scale

 - A 45-minute culture fit call with non-technical team members

 - Reference calls

 

We’re building an inclusive and equitable platform for learners across the world, and it’s important our core team reflects these principles too. Research shows people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we strongly encourage to you apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.

jobs.title: Industrial and Personnel Security Manager
jobs.description:
About Varda

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

About the Role

Varda is advancing pharmaceutical development in microgravity and flying government missions that involve hypersonic reentry and advanced flight testing. None of it happens without a security program that protects the people, facilities, information, and hardware behind these missions. You would be the one making that program real.

As the Industrial and Personnel Security Manager, you will own the day-to-day execution of Varda’s industrial security compliance and personnel security programs. This is a hands-on, builder’s role: you will develop practical processes, keep the program inspection-ready, and work side by side with HR, IT, Legal, Engineering, Mission Management, and Business Development, from early customer engagement through launch and recovery.

You will report to the Director of Security, who is also the Facility Security Officer (FSO). You will support industrial and personnel security activities as assigned by the FSO, and you may serve as Alternate FSO upon designation and completion of required training. The Director retains primary FSO authority, program oversight, and required certifications. Special program personnel security and COMSEC duties apply as customer requirements are established.

Physical security operations are outside the scope of this role. Varda plans to hire a dedicated Physical Security Manager after this position.

What You’ll Do

Industrial Security and Compliance

• Run the industrial security program in accordance with 32 CFR Part 117 (NISPOM), contract requirements, security classification guides, and applicable DoD and Intelligence Community requirements.

• Own facility clearance records and supporting documentation, and prepare updates and government correspondence for FSO review using NISS or the applicable government system.

• Lead annual self-inspections: plan them, maintain inspection evidence, draft reports for the Director’s review and certification, and track corrective actions through closure.

• Be the face of readiness for DCSA security reviews and customer assessments, coordinating deliverables with the FSO and external security advisory partners.

• Review DD Forms 254 and classification guides, and turn requirements into procedures. Work with Contracts and Business Development to build security requirements into prime contracts, subcontracts, and proposals.

• Control classified information and material from marking, receipt, storage, and dissemination through inventory, transfer, approved transmission, and destruction when authorized.

• Build the procedures, training materials, and records people actually use, and recommend practical improvements to the Director when you spot compliance gaps.

Personnel Security

• Manage clearance processing and records in DISS, NBIS, and applicable customer systems, including investigation requests, upgrades, transfers, reciprocity coordination, and Continuous Vetting actions.

• Coordinate SCI nominations, program access requests, and customer-required polygraph scheduling when applicable, and verify eligibility and need-to-know before access is granted.

• Partner with HR on cleared employee onboarding and offboarding, and maintain clearance rosters, access records, personnel security files, and briefing acknowledgments.

• Brief the team: initial, annual, refresher, foreign travel, and termination briefings, plus program indoctrinations and debriefings with authorized officials.

• Process incoming and outgoing visit authorizations and certifications, and verify visitor clearance and access requirements.

• Spot issues early by tracking foreign travel, foreign contacts, reportable changes, and adverse information. Prepare timely reports and elevate sensitive issues to the FSO in coordination with HR and Legal.

• Plan ahead by forecasting clearance needs with hiring and program teams, and track metrics on processing status, overdue reporting, training completion, and inspection findings.

Program Support and Incident Response

• Support insider threat administration under the Director’s ITPSO oversight, including training, referral documentation, and coordination with authorized stakeholders.

• Document security incidents, support inquiries and required reporting, and track mitigation and corrective actions under FSO direction.

• Step in as alternate COMSEC custodian when designated, trained, and authorized, supporting inventory, accountability, and handling requirements.

• Team up with IT and Information Assurance on CUI protection and classified infrastructure, and support program protection planning and security requirements without assuming ISSM or ISSO authority.

• Be the go-to advisor who gives employees and leaders clear security guidance, and recommend tools, resource needs, and future staffing as the program grows.

Minimum Qualifications

Experience and Technical Knowledge

• At least 5 years of relevant industrial security experience in a DoD or Intelligence Community contractor environment, including substantive hands-on personnel security responsibilities.

• A track record of ownership: demonstrated experience administering clearance actions, reporting, training, classified information controls, and inspection preparation, and independently owning recurring security processes.

• Strong working knowledge of 32 CFR Part 117 (NISPOM), DD Form 254 requirements, and security classification guides, with the ability to translate requirements into clear procedures.

• Hands-on proficiency with DISS and NBIS, and the ability to use NISS and customer-specific systems applicable to assigned responsibilities.

• Working knowledge of relevant ICD 704 personnel security requirements when supporting SCI personnel.

• Strong written communication, organization, discretion, and judgment, with the ability to brief employees, executives, and government representatives and to manage sensitive personnel information.

• The ability to work independently, coordinate across functions, prioritize competing deadlines, and build repeatable processes in a growing company.

Clearance and Conditions of Employment

• U.S. citizenship and an active Top Secret security clearance with SCI eligibility, plus the ability to maintain the clearance and obtain required customer program access.

• Ability to satisfy additional customer access requirements, including a CI polygraph if required by the assigned program. An existing polygraph is preferred but not universally mandatory.

• Ability to work on-site in El Segundo and support other Varda facilities, with occasional domestic travel and mission-driven schedule requirements as needed.

• Completion and maintenance of required role-specific government and customer training. FSO or COMSEC training is required before performing formally designated duties.

Education

• Bachelor’s degree in security management, criminal justice, business administration, or a related field, or equivalent relevant professional experience. A degree is not mandatory when your experience demonstrates the required capabilities.

Preferred Qualifications

• 7 or more years of relevant experience, including prior FSO, Alternate FSO, CPSO, CSSO, or security program leadership responsibilities.

• Direct experience supporting successful DCSA reviews and personnel security or industrial security compliance for SCI or SAP programs.

• COMSEC account experience, insider threat program administration, and experience partnering on CUI or classified information system requirements.

• Relevant CDSE FSO course completion or recognized security certifications such as SPeD or ISP.

• Experience building security processes in aerospace, space, advanced manufacturing, or a startup environment.

Pay Range

• Salary Range: $115,000 - $155,000

• Role is located in El Segundo, CA

• Leveling and base salary is determined by job-related skills, education level, experience level, and job performance

• You will be eligible for long-term incentives in the form of stock options or long-term cash awards

• Offer compensation also includes the ability to purchase company stock through the Employee Stock Purchase Plan

ITAR Requirements

Varda, like all employers, must ensure that its employees working in the United States are lawfully authorized to work in the U.S. Additionally, our employees are exposed to and have access to certain export-controlled items. Because our employees are provided access to export-controlled items, our policy is to only hire “U.S. persons” who are permitted to have access to our technology without an export license.

“US person” means: U.S. citizen, U.S. lawful permanent resident, or protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3) (i.e., individual admitted to the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum).

E-Verify Statement

Varda Space Industries, Inc. participates in the U.S. Department of Homeland Security E-Verify program. The E-Verify program is an Internet-based employment eligibility verification system operated by the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services. Learn more about the E-Verify program.

E-Verify Notice                                                               Right To Work Notice

Read more                                                                             Read more

Varda Space Industries is an Equal Opportunity Employer.  We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. Candidates and employees are always evaluated based on merit, qualifications, and performance. We will never discriminate on the basis of race, color, gender, national origin, ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, martial status, mental or physical disability, or any other legally protected status.

jobs.title: Lot Assistant - ADESA Salt Lake City
jobs.description:
Full Time (approximately 36 hours) Monday - Friday

Pay rate: $16/hour

About Us

ADESA, a Carvana-owned company, currently operates in over 50 locations throughout the US. Our auto auctions, some up to 200 acres, provide a wide array of vehicle services, including repair, reconditioning, and auction remarketing, and many of our sites serve as market hub distribution centers. Our inventory comprises hundreds of thousands of vehicles across North America, from retail to commercial, OEM & more.

We work in a service industry and embrace a “we” versus “I” culture – help others, and they will help you. Our industry is fun, fast-paced, and competitive – and filled with the best people who are passionate about what they do.

We’re excited about the future! As an industry leader, ADESA is poised for a multi-year expansion, including huge investments in facilities, massive sales growth, and an ever-increasing inventory of vehicles! We are looking for great people who want to take this journey with us! Get a sneak peek into life at ADESA!

Role and Team

• Reporting to the Lead Lot Operations or other designated manager, you will assist with outside functions to support lot movements and general operations before, during, and after sale day. In this role, you will assist on the lot, including driving the service truck, lot tow truck (non-DOT), and forklift, to ultimately maintain accurate inventory flow and ensure vehicle readiness.

Responsibilities

• Lot Operations Support: Support lot operations by preparing and staging vehicles for sale, including stickering (run and customer stickers), marking vehicles on the spot, moving vehicles using a lot tow truck or forklift, and operating the service truck to support the driver team.

• Inventory Accuracy: Scan the lot and use electronic devices to record the movement of vehicles on the property.

• Vehicle Readiness: Assist with vehicle readiness tasks such as jumping vehicles and adding fluids (gas, water, etc), adding air to tires, and verifying vehicle status while maintaining accurate lot organization.

• Property Management: Handle the removal of personal property from vehicles.

• Operational Flow: Communicate with shop and operations teams to ensure an efficient flow of inventory from vehicle check-in to the auction sale line.

• Customer & Admin Support: Provide customer service support and coordinate with administrative teams to ensure efficient execution of sale day activities.

• Vehicle Identification: Confirm vehicle mileage, make year, and VIN to ensure accurate record-keeping.

• Safety & Maintenance: Maintain work areas to ensure a safe environment and report any incidents or hazards to the designated manager.

• General Duties: Perform any other duties assigned by the designated manager.

Skills and Attributes

• Teamwork: A team player who can collaborate well with multiple departments, customers, and vendors.

• Customer Focus: Strong customer service skills.

• Detail-Oriented: Proven ability to multitask while maintaining strict attention to detail.

• Efficiency: Proven ability to manage deliverables and metrics against aggressive targets and timelines.

• Adaptability: Ability to work in a fast-paced environment and handle outside conditions.

• Communication: Effective interpersonal skills with excellent verbal and written communication.

Qualifications

• High School diploma or GED preferred

• Must be 18 years of age and have a valid driver’s license that meets the requirements

• Able to safely drive a variety of vehicle makes, models, and sizes, including tow trucks, forklifts, and the service truck

• Automotive or auction experience preferred

• Proficiency with computer systems and applications

• Obtain and maintain forklift certification

ADESA Values

• Our Next Customer May Be Your Mom: Every customer deserves the same level of care and respect one would give to their own mother.

• We’re All in This Together: The company is unified by the shared goal of providing fantastic customer experiences, achieved through mutual trust, respect, and understanding.

• There Are No Sidelines: Employees are encouraged to be proactive, work hard, and take ownership of what needs to be done in a fast-paced environment.

• Be Brave: Employees should not fear taking risks, pushing themselves outside their comfort zones, or being decisive, even if they stumble along the way.

• Zag Forward: The company empowers creative and passionate thinking to find meaningful ways to be different and deliver amazing experiences.

• Don’t Be a Richard: A simple guiding principle to act appropriately and professionally.

• Stay Scrappy: This value rejects mediocrity and "good enough," pushing employees to do more with less to pass savings on to customers.

ADESA Benefits and Perks

Competitive Pay | Quality Benefits | Holiday and Paid Time Off | Education and Equipment Reimbursement Programs | Matching 401(k) | Career Path Opportunities | And More!

Other Requirements

To be able to do your job at ADESA, there are some basic requirements we want to share with you. Of course, we’ll make any reasonable accommodations for those with disabilities to perform the essential functions of their jobs.

• The physical activity requirements of the position range from Light to Medium Physical Work.

• Constant - standing, watching, touching, listening, walking, talking

• Frequent - bending, stooping, kneeling, lifting, grasping, pushing, pulling

• Potential – running, jumping, yelling, or other rapid or forceful movement in emergencies

• Visual acuity requirements include color, depth perception, and field of vision comparable to definitions for Clerical, Administrative, and Machine Operators (including inspection) positions.

Physical Working Conditions

This position is subject to both inside and outside environmental working conditions, including temperature changes, outside weather conditions, slightly elevated ambient noise levels, and minor atmospheric conditions affecting skin or respiratory systems, such as fumes, odors, and dust associated with internal and external service station/convenience food and petroleum dispensing operations.

To be able to do your job at ADESA, you must be able to read, write, speak, and understand English. Of course, we’ll make any reasonable accommodations for those with disabilities to perform the essential functions of their jobs.

Legal Stuff

Hiring is contingent on passing a complete background check.  This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship.

ADESA is an equal employment opportunity employer.  All applicants receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, national origin, age, mental or physical disability, protected veteran status, or genetic information, or any other basis protected by applicable law.  ADESA also prohibits harassment of applicants or employees based on any of these protected categories.

jobs.title: Deputy General Counsel, Employment Law
jobs.location: New York, United States; San Jose, California, United States
jobs.description:
Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom. OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves. Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er.

About the Opportunity

As a Deputy General Counsel for Employment, you will be responsible for global employment matters reporting directly to the Global Head of Employment Legal, who is located in the US. You will work closely with other members of the Legal team and business leaders throughout the company, but especially with our global HR, finance, and compliance departments. The ideal candidate will be based out of our San Jose, California or New York office.

The right candidate will have an understanding of and enthusiastic belief in the cryptocurrency/digital asset space, 9+ years of experience working on employment matters for a top law firm as well as in-house at a fast-paced, brand-name business. We are looking for a teammate with strong academic credentials and excellent analytical skills. The ideal candidate will have strong expertise and experience in advising business leaders to produce quick analyses of issues related to employment law and HR, including recruiting, hiring, immigration, internal investigations, employee relations and employment litigation and arbitration.

We offer a competitive base salary and bonus structure as well as excellent benefits and an opportunity to work in a cutting-edge industry that will be the future of financial services.

What You’ll Be Doing

• Supporting the business by managing and handling legal HR, employment, and recruiting matters for the company and its global affiliated entities, with a primary focus on supporting OKX group operations in the US and across the globe.

• Supporting our HR, finance, compliance and recruiting departments on a daily basis by providing legal advice and guidance on all employment matters affecting the company;

• Driving the strategy and managing employment litigation and arbitration matters and retaining and supervising outside counsel;

• Supporting HR and compliance by advising on internal investigations and interviewing employees;

• Working with other members of the Legal team and business partners on legal issues and matters touching on employee retention, payroll, executive compensation, benefits, performance management, and immigration and visa issues;

• Build and uplevel employment legal processes and infrastructure, moving the function from ad hoc support toward a structured, best-in-class practice.

• Partner directly with senior regional leadership to operationalize their strategic direction.

What We Look For In You

• Attorney licensed to practice law in the US.

• 9+ years of experience at a top-tier law firm and/or in-house legal team working on international employment matters;

• Comfortable working independently in a fast-paced, growth-stage and multi-cultural environment;

• Ability to effectively advise and build trust with business teams;

• Ability to work in a high-functioning legal team and feel comfortable in a collaborative working environment;

• Experience working on cross-jurisdictional matters and a global legal team;

• Ability to translate complex legal concepts into practical and actionable business advice for non-legal audiences;

• Drafting, reviewing and negotiating offer letters, employment agreements, incentive plans and severance agreements.

Perks & Benefits

• Competitive total compensation package

• L&D programs and Education subsidy for employees' growth and development

• Various team building programs and company events

• Wellness and meal allowances

• Comprehensive healthcare schemes for employees and dependants

• More that we love to tell you along the process!

OKX Statement:

OKX is committed to equal employment opportunities regardless of race, color, genetic information, creed, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, lawful alien status, national origin, age, marital status, and non-job related physical or mental disability, or protected veteran status. jobs.title: Production Planner
jobs.description:
ABOUT MARIANA MINERALS

Mariana Minerals is a software-first, vertically integrated minerals company on a mission to supply the critical minerals powering modern energy, AI, and defense technologies. We’re reimagining the minerals supply chain by combining deep industry expertise with advanced software, automation, and data-driven decision-making.

Every Mariana Minerals site runs on a production plan, and this role brings them together. As our first Production Planner, you'll partner with each site to develop its plan, then roll those plans up into one clear view across the company.

You'll build our planning tools in MarianaOS, either with tools our software team develops or by building your own with AI. If you love building systems and learning new ways to work, you'll thrive here.

You'll also own KPIs and drive operational excellence across our sites, tracking productivity, cycle times, and costs, and finding ways to improve them. This role reports to our COO and sits at the intersection of operations, data, and OpEx. You'll build the playbook, and you will help shape the foundation of a central OpEx team.

This role is for someone scrappy, data-driven, and highly collaborative, who's excited to build systems from the ground up.

 


RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Partner with site leads to build, refine, and maintain site-level production plans

 - Consolidate production plans across all locations into a unified, company-wide view

 - Define, track, and report KPIs covering productivity, cycle times, and costs

 - Build planning tools and systems in MarianaOS using AI-assisted development

 - Take over and expand the production planning work currently being handled across the team

 - Drive operational excellence initiatives and identify opportunities to improve how our sites run

 - Work closely with site leadership and technical program managers to keep plans aligned and on track


QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE

 - 5+ years of experience in operations, business operations, or production planning; OpEx or continuous improvement background strongly preferred

 - Bachelor's degree preferred

 - Experience defining and tracking KPIs such as productivity, cycle times, and costs

 - Data-driven system builder who uses metrics to drive decisions and AI to create the tools that track them

 - Highly collaborative, with strong communication skills and the ability to partner with site leaders and program managers across multiple locations

 - Thrives in a fast-paced startup environment with ambiguity and room to build


WORKING ENVIRONMENT & PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

Full-time, salaried. Standard business hours with flexibility as needed to support sites across time zones.

Primarily office-based at one of our operating sites in Utah (La Sal), Texas (Houston or Joaquin), or at our San Francisco office, with periodic travel to other Mariana sites.  Site visits may involve exposure to industrial and mining environments and require appropriate PPE.


OUR CULTURE IS BUILT ON FOUR PRINCIPLES:



Everyone Gets Home Safe. We never put speed or cost ahead of people.

Extreme Ownership. We take full responsibility for outcomes, relentlessly driving toward solutions.

Engineer Out Requirements, then Automate. We simplify, optimize, and then automate for scale.

Share Your Legos. We collaborate openly, share knowledge, and empower each other to build bigger, better solutions.



Join us as we build the future of responsible mineral sourcing and supply!

jobs.description:
You’ll join our New Business Sales team, selling NextRoll’s AdRoll platform to sophisticated advertisers and agencies across CTV, DOOH, and display. As a Senior Account Executive, you will be an individual contributor, owning the full sales cycle for strategic mid-market opportunities from self-generated pipeline through close.

As a Senior Account Executive, you’ll be a senior individual contributor responsible for the full sales cycle - from a self-generated pipeline through negotiation and close. You’ll identify and develop high-value opportunities, engage senior decision-makers, shape the commercial strategies, and position AdRoll to address complex media and advertising needs. This is a commercially driven role for a seller who understands how modern media is bought and can credibly engage sophisticated advertisers, agencies and media leaders. You’ll leverage  strong industry relationships, consultative selling, and deep programmatic expertise to create new opportunities, win net-new logos and grow investment into NextRoll’s fastest-growing channels.

You’ll partner closely with Solutions, Marketing and Customer Success to develop compelling solutions, navigate complex buying processes and deliver meaningful new business revenue for NextRoll.

jobs.title: Mold/Asbestos Analyst - $5K Sign-on Bonus - Eurofins Built Environment Testing, Las Vegas, NV
jobs.description:
Eurofins Built Environment Testing is searching for a Mold/Asbestos Analyst in Las Vegas, NV

The Analyst primarily performs analysis of bulk samples using PLM for asbestos, and analysis of non-culturable surface and air samples for fungi.  Analyst prepares and analyzes environmental samples according to scientific methodology in compliance with company Quality Assurance programs and SOP’s, and must be knowledgeable of both job-specific routine and complex analyses. The analyst validates and reviews data for accuracy, and enters laboratory data into the LIMS that ultimately generates required reports to clients. Schedules sample workload according to due dates and sample hold times, and must be knowledgeable of the job-specific laboratory testing equipment, requiring the exercise of discretion and judgment in its operation.

• Prepare and analyze aerobiological and environmental samples for asbestos and fungi.
• Accurately enters and reports analytical data using the LIMS
• Performs independent data reviews for other analysts’ work
• Performs analysis of reference materials, proficiency samples and other quality control samples as needed
• Maintains client service and provides technical support as needed
• Assists the QA manager in development, implementation and data collection of QA processes for the different analytical tests
• Performs confirmation of lab results as needed by client services personnel
• Performs and completes all analytical testing and Quality Assurance related tasks as needed
• Assists in pursuing, receiving and maintaining necessary laboratory accreditations
• Maintains and updates all necessary Training and QA documents onsite as necessary
• Coordinates and manages projects according to their rush status and due time for timely delivery
• Assists co-workers on analytical questions, as necessary
• Participates in Lean initiatives as needed
• Follows company policies and procedures and ensures that coworkers are doing the same
• An other duties as assigned

Basic Minimum Qualifications:

• 1+ years of experience performing asbestos PLM (Polarized Light Microscopes) and/or mold analysis
• Bachelor’s degree in biology, geology or a closely related science REQUIRED
• Authorization to work in the United States indefinitely without restriction or sponsorship
• Professional working proficiency in English is a requirement, including the ability to read, write and speak in English

The ideal candidate would possess:

• 8 units of Microbiology courses preferred
• General regulatory requirements
• Knowledge of computers, spreadsheets, and databases
• Strong computer, scientific, and organizational skills

Compensation Range: $21 - $26 per hour depending on experience and qualifications.

Position is full-time, Monday - Friday, 8am-5pm shift with overtime and weekends as needed.

$5,000 Sign-on Bonus available for qualified candidates with one year or more of experience performing asbestos PLM (Polarized Light Microscopes) and/or mold analysis.

Eurofins Environment Testing (USA) provides a compensation range for informational purposes, the actual base compensation may vary based upon, but not limited to, relevant experience and skill set, base compensation of internal peers, business sector, and geographic location.

As a Eurofins employee, you will become part of a company that has received national recognition as a great place to work.  We offer excellent full-time benefits including comprehensive medical coverage, life and disability insurance, 401(k) with company match, paid holidays, paid time off, and dental and vision options.

We support your development! Do you feel you don’t match 100% of the requirements? Don’t hesitate to apply anyway! Eurofins companies are committed to supporting your career development.

We embrace diversity! Eurofins network of companies believe in strength and innovation through diversity, being an Equal Opportunity Employer. We prohibit discrimination against employees or applications based on gender identity and/or expression, race, nationality, age, religion, sexual orientation, disability, and everything else that makes employees of Eurofins companies unique.

Sustainability matters to us! At Eurofins, we believe sustainability is at the heart of everything we do. Guided by our vision to be the Global Leader in “Testing for Life,” our mission to contribute to a healthier and safer world, and our core values, we are building a strong foundation for Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives. Eurofins’ commitment to sustainability begins within our own companies through a shared responsibility to people and the planet. With climate change posing an imminent threat, Eurofins and its many companies recognize their duty to proactively reduce or offset the environmental impact of essential operations while also helping our clients do the same—serving as a true ESG Enabler.

Find out more in our career page: https://careers.eurofins.com/

Company description: Eurofins Scientific is an international life sciences company, providing a unique range of analytical testing services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work with the biggest companies in the world to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic and labelling is accurate.

The Eurofins network of companies is the global leader in food, environment, pharmaceutical and cosmetic product testing and in discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and agroscience contract research services. It is one of the market leaders in certain testing and laboratory services for genomics, discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and in the support of clinical studies, as well as having an emerging global presence in Contract Development and Manufacturing Organisations. It also has a rapidly developing presence in highly specialised and molecular clinical diagnostic testing and in-vitro diagnostic products.

In over 35 years, Eurofins has grown from one laboratory in Nantes, France to 61,000 staff across a decentralised and entrepreneurial network of ca. 900 laboratories in 61 countries. Eurofins companies offer a portfolio of over 200,000 analytical methods to evaluate the safety, identity, composition, authenticity, origin, traceability and purity of biological substances and products.

In 2025, Eurofins generated total revenues of EUR 7.296 billion, and has been among the best performing stocks in Europe over the past 20 years.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Global Site Contracts
jobs.description:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.

The Opportunity:

Revolution Medicines is seeking a motivated individual Senior Manager, Global Site Contracts, who will support all processes related to site contracts and budgets. The individual will be responsible for but not limited to drafting, advising, negotiating, and executing clinical site agreements. Ensures final contracts and contract terms are consistent with organizational strategy, delivered by agreed upon timelines, falls within Fair Market Value and in compliance with legal, financial & regulatory requirements. This role is an individual contributor with team leadership responsibilities, reporting to the Director, Clinical Vendor and Outsourcing. Must have strong oncology experience.

Responsibilities:

• Ability to manage a high volume of site contract agreements from start to finish. Support all site contract and budget activities related to clinical trials.

• Ensure consistency of contract terms with company policies and goals and best practices to enhance the contracting process.

• Ensure smooth, timely, and accurate implementation of all contract terms.

• Accountable for the timely preparation and execution of all site contracts and budgets.

• Enter contracts into the contract management system (CMS).

• Demonstrated experience with clinical budget build/development using (FMV), and historical data (Grant Plan). Strong negotiation of MCTA, ICTAs, CTAs, CSAs, CDAs, other site agreements and budgets with investigator sites (directly or with support where language necessitates), using appropriate templates, guidance, and legal/budget playbooks, consulting with ClinOps, Finance and Legal for approval.

• Provide input for ongoing updates of applicable legal contracts and budget playbooks and templates.

• Ensure appropriate tracking of various agreements.

• Effectively escalate/communicate in a timely manner to stakeholders and clinical teams regarding contract issues that could impact project deliverables.

• Lead process improvement projects and continuous improvement in delivery of Global Contract Management responsibilities.

• Demonstrate an elevated level of applicable competencies in contract management, critical thinking, highly competent in negotiation and contracting business standards.

• Ensure the execution of end-to-end process is robust and is established as a way of effectively supporting the needs of key business partners while continuously monitoring and further enhancing service quality, efficiency, effectiveness, and lead or support continuous improvement initiatives.

• Manage contract workflow and collaboration with senior leaders to ensure efficient contract execution and suggest and implement new / more efficient processes as needed.

• Responsible for measuring and reporting metrics and Key Performance Indicators (“KPIs”) for in scope service deliverables

• Participation in team meetings and collaborate with other functional groups within the company to achieve clinical study goals.

• Ensure contracts and budgets are completed on time, within budget and in compliance with Standard Operating procedures (SOPs), FDA regulations, and International Council for Harmonization (ICH)/ GCP guidelines.

• Communicate effectively within cross functional project teams at Revolution Medicines.

Required Skills, Experience and Education:

• B.S., 10+ years equivalent related business/industry experience.

• Experience in pharmaceutical, biotech, academia, CROs (Clinical Research Organizations).

• Strong computer skills: Microsoft office and software to manage contracting.

• Demonstrated leadership, stakeholder influencing without authority and negotiation skills.

• Strong knowledge of a wide variety of clinical-related contract types, including clinical trial site agreements, investigator sponsored trial. agreements, research collaboration agreements, consulting agreements, and confidentiality agreements.

• 5+ years’ experience with clinical budget negotiation.

• Strong analytical and contract administration skills, verbal and written communication skills, and the ability to interact effectively with internal and external business partners.

• High degree of dedication, motivation, and ability to work under pressure with a drive for results and the ability to engage and deliver through others.

• Experience working in a global environment.

• Strong working knowledge of FDA Regulations, ICH Guidelines and GCPs governing the conduct of clinical trials.

• Strong critical thinking skills with sound technically driven decision-making ability.

• An innovative team-player with capacity to be effective in a dynamic and fast-paced company environment.

• Strong Oncology experience necessary.

Preferred Skills:

• Big pharma/CRO experience a plus.

• Grant Plan experience a plus.

jobs.title: Senior HSE Manager – EPC/EPCM Projects
jobs.description:
Remote option is available for this position.

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. No sponsorship is available for this position.

Are you eager to develop your excellence in an inclusive, collaborative, and empowering community? Are you excited about joining a company that strives to make a difference – for its employees, clients, and society? Are you motivated by creating sustainable change that benefits society and nature?

If this sounds like you, or you’re curious to learn more, then this role could be the perfect opportunity. Join our Workplace Management team and work with us to close the gap to a sustainable future.

Your new role

This role provides senior HSE leadership across Ramboll’s EPC/EPCM project portfolio in Ramboll Americas, supporting the safe delivery of complex engineering, procurement, construction management, commissioning, and turnover activities. The role is responsible for establishing consistent HSE governance, aligning contractors and project teams, supporting high-risk work planning, and enabling effective execution across multiple concurrent projects. The successful candidate will bring significant hands-on experience from large-scale EPC/EPCM construction environments and will be able to operate confidently at both strategic and field execution levels.

The ideal candidate will be a credible HSE leader with significant field experience on large-scale construction or EPC/EPCM projects, strong contractor management capability, and the confidence to influence senior project, client, and contractor stakeholders. They will be comfortable working across multiple projects, balancing strategic governance with practical field-based support, and helping project teams create consistent, risk-based HSE execution.

Your key responsibilities will be:

Strategic HSE Leadership

• Lead the development of a portfolio-wide HSE approach that enables consistent standards, scalable processes, and project-specific execution across all EPC/EPCM projects.
• Serve as primary HSE advisor to Project Directors and EPC/EPCM leadership teams.
• Drive adoption of Ramboll’s HSE program and translate its expectations into practical project-level behaviours, controls, and leadership routines.
• Provide strategic HSE guidance during proposals and contract negotiations to align client expectations and establish the conditions needed for effective safety management.
• Provide HSE leadership within an EPC/EPCM delivery model, ensuring clear boundaries, responsibilities, and interfaces between Ramboll, clients, construction contractors, subcontractors, and suppliers.

Safety Program Organization & Implementation

• Define HSE organization structures that are scalable with the ability to support multi-project EPC/EPCM delivery on a nationwide basis.
• Clarify roles, responsibilities, interfaces, and governance models required for integrated EPC/EPCM/ safety programs.
• Establish standardized HSE execution plans across engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning, and turnover.
• Establish construction readiness expectations, including contractor mobilisation, competency assurance, risk review, and field execution controls.

Contractor & Multi-Party Coordination

• Align HSE expectations, execution standards, and performance requirements across contractors, subcontractors, vendors, and third-party stakeholders.
• Lead contractor onboarding, alignment sessions, audits, and recurring performance reviews.
• Ensure HSE requirements are embedded into contracting strategies, procurement packages, bid documents, mobilisation plans, and contractor management processes.
• Support project teams in translating Ramboll and client HSE requirements into practical field execution requirements for contractors and subcontractors.

Risk Management, Governance and Assurance

• Provide governance and assurance over EPC/EPCM risk management processes, including hazard identification, construction risk assessments, high-risk work reviews, and site controls.
• Support project HSE resources and project leadership in establishing consistent risk management expectations, while ensuring accountability remains clear within the project delivery structure.
• Review and challenge the effectiveness of controls for high-risk activities, including lifting, electrical work, confined space entry, work at height, ground disturbance, energisation, commissioning, and simultaneous operations.
• Provide oversight, escalation support, and subject matter input for high-potential or higher-severity incidents, ensuring investigations are completed and lessons learned are embedded across relevant projects.
• Conduct site visits, leadership engagements, and assurance reviews to verify that project HSE controls are effective, understood, and consistently applied by the relevant project teams and contractors.

Safety Culture & Engagement

jobs.title: Learning & Development Lead, Operations
jobs.description:
Learning & Development Lead — Operations

Role Overview

The Learning & Development Lead owns training and readiness for Physical Intelligence's robot operator workforce.

This person is responsible for designing and running the systems that take a new operator from candidate work trial through their first 30–60 days, with the goal of getting people productive quickly while maintaining a high quality bar.

They also own ongoing training as the work changes. When researchers introduce new robot workflows, tasks, tools, or operating procedures, the Learning & Development Lead translates those changes into training that can be rolled out quickly and consistently across the operation.

This is a highly operational training role. We are looking for someone who has built or owned training programs for hourly or frontline employees and knows how to turn complex work into a simple, repeatable learning process.



Responsibilities

Operator Trials & Readiness

 - Own the operator work-trial program and ensure candidates are evaluated consistently.

 - Maintain clear trial standards, evaluator guidance, and scoring criteria.

 - Partner with recruiting and operations to continuously improve what the trial predicts about future operator success.

New-Hire Onboarding

 - Build and run onboarding from day one through the first 30–60 days.

 - Define what an operator should know and be able to do at each stage of ramp.

 - Create training plans, checklists, certification steps, and readiness milestones.

 - Identify struggling operators early and create clear paths for remediation.

 - Continuously improve time-to-productivity for new hires.

New Workflow Training

 - Partner with researchers and operations teams when new robot tasks, systems, or processes are introduced.

 - Learn new workflows quickly and translate them into clear training materials and operating instructions.

 - Design the rollout plan needed to train a large operator population quickly.

 - Track who has been trained and verify that the training actually resulted in correct execution.

 - Maintain consistency as training expands across shifts, teams, and locations.

Training Operations

 - Maintain a clear training calendar and ensure training happens when required.

 - Coordinate trainers, operators, shift leads, and researchers.

 - Keep training materials current as workflows change.

 - Build repeatable processes so training does not depend on tribal knowledge.

 - Track training completion, readiness, and performance metrics.

Continuous Improvement

 - Use operator performance data and feedback to identify gaps in training.

 - Work with operations leaders to understand recurring quality or productivity issues.

 - Determine whether problems are caused by training, instructions, process, tooling, or something else.

 - Continuously simplify and improve how operators learn.

What We're Looking For

 - Experience owning training, onboarding, or workforce development programs for hourly or frontline employees.

 - Demonstrated ability to get new employees productive quickly.

 - Experience building structured ramp programs with clear milestones and standards.

 - Strong operational organization and follow-through.

 - Able to turn ambiguous or technical workflows into simple, teachable processes.

 - Comfortable managing trainers, who are responsible for training large groups of people on new procedures under tight timelines.

 - Strong written and verbal communication.

 - Able to work effectively with both highly technical stakeholders, trainers, and frontline operators.

 - Comfortable in an environment where processes and requirements change frequently.

 - Uses data and observation to improve training rather than relying only on subjective feedback.

Experience in robotics is not required.



Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

jobs.description:
ABOUT SAVVY WEALTH:

Wealth management is a $545 billion industry that still runs on manual work. 75% of advisors offer no digital communication beyond email, and most still build financial plans by hand in Excel. Savvy is reinventing what it looks like to be a financial advisor. Founder Ritik Malhotra saw the fragmentation firsthand after seeking out his own advisor, and started Savvy to give independent advisors a modern, AI-native home.



Savvy is a registered investment advisor (RIA), and we partner with experienced financial advisors who want to grow without running the back office themselves. Advisors bring their book and join Savvy, running under their own brand (or ours), and Savvy earns a percentage of the assets they manage. In return, they get a true business-in-a-box: a proprietary tech platform and client portal, an in-house marketing team that helps them grow, a world-class investment management team, and a dedicated client services team that runs day-to-day operations and support. Advisors at Savvy service up to 50% more households and save 19 hours a week.



AI runs through everything we do. On the product side, Savvy Intelligence (released April 2026) is the only AI built for wealth managers that can see a client's complete financial picture. Internally, everyone at Savvy uses Claude and is encouraged to experiment with it, backed by a dedicated AI enablement team and a RevOps org building agents in-house.



The trajectory is steep and it's still early. We're a Series C company with 170+ people, $200M raised, and $100M ARR in sight this year. Inc. ranked us the No. 1 fastest-growing financial services company in America in 2026. Come build the next stage with us!



Recognition:

We're a Certified Great Place to Work and have been honored for our culture and our growth:

 - Newsweek's America's Greatest Startup Workplaces (2026)

 - Fortune Best Workplaces in New York™ (2026)

 - Great Place to Work Certified™ 
   
   

The Role:
As a Portfolio and Trading Associate, you will play a critical role in enhancing and scaling Savvy’s centralized trading infrastructure. You’ll be responsible for daily trading, portfolio management, and helping drive adoption of Savvy’s SWIM (Savvy Wealth Investment Management) platform.

You’ll also execute advisor-submitted investment tasks in line with daily SLAs, ensuring timely, accurate completion. This is a hands-on role where you will be expected to manage portfolios on behalf of advisors with discretion, adapt to startup-style workflows (limited documentation, figure-it-out mindset), and continuously improve our processes. This is not a traditional trading role—you will use AI-powered internal tools daily and help improve and expand them.

This role offers a unique opportunity to work closely with advisors, ensure operational excellence, and help build scalable processes for one of the fastest-growing RIAs in the country.



Responsibilities: 

 - Conduct daily portfolio management activities, including cash reviews, drift analysis, and tax-loss harvesting

 - Execute cash raises, rebalances, and one-off trades in Eclipse and at custodians

 - Process advisor-submitted investment tasks via the internal dashboard and complete same-day executions (per SLA)

 - Leverage trading software (Orion Eclipse) to support daily operations and manage client portfolios at scale

 - Implement new accounts into SWIM and execute rebalances for advisors

 - Support bulk implementations to accelerate advisor adoption of SWIM

 - Assist with firm-wide model updates and rebalancing of SWIM and Custom Advisor Models

 - Identify and implement improvements to trading, portfolio management, and investment operations procedures to enhance scalability and efficiency

 - Apply knowledge of investment strategies and portfolio construction to support advisor requests and execution



Must Have:

 - 2+ years of relevant experience in wealth management, trading, or investment operations.

 - 2+ years of experience trading client portfolios using portfolio management and trading software.

 - Strong understanding of the wealth management industry and experience collaborating with advisors.

 - Proven ability to take ownership of tasks and execute with efficiency and accuracy.

 - Current Series 65 license or willingness to obtain within 2 months.

Nice to have:
