jobs.title: Senior Numerical Optimization Engineer (Arsenal 2)
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Maritime Digital Production (MDP) is the software and digital systems function within Anduril's Heavy Metal division. We build and deploy the full technology stack that powers Anduril's shipbuilding factories: the data infrastructure that makes every machine and sensor visible in real time, the manufacturing execution system (ArsenalOS) that workers and planners use every shift, the scheduling engine that replans production in minutes instead of days, and the AI systems that eliminate manual toil from both the shop floor and business operations.

MDP operates at the boundary between Operational Technology and Information Technology. Our systems live where factory-floor machines, edge compute, and OT networks meet enterprise platforms and cloud infrastructure. We incubate solutions close to the production line, validate them with real operators building real hardware, harden them for reliability and security, and then scale them across multiple sites. The environment is fast, physical, and consequential. When our systems go down, production stops. The output of our work is not a dashboard: it is a ship.

This is not a support function. It is a strategic investment by Anduril in the premise that digitizing the manufacturing lifecycle end-to-end, from engineering definition through scheduling through execution through field feedback, is how Heavy Metal will out-build, out-adapt, and out-scale the traditional defense industrial base. MDP is scaling from a founding team to 70+ engineers across multiple U.S. sites. You will be joining early, working on hard problems with real operational stakes, and shaping how manufacturing software is built at Anduril from the ground up.

ABOUT THE JOB

As a Senior Numerical Optimization Engineer on this unique initiative, you will own the scheduling optimization core that decides when and how ships get built. This project represents a shipyard's work as a graph of 100,000+ manufacturing operations carrying precedence, spatial, resource, and qualification constraints, then continuously replans as the factory changes. You will formulate that problem, build and benchmark the solvers that attack it, and keep them fast and trustworthy enough that a new plan can reach the floor within minutes of a disruption.

This is a research-grade problem with production consequences. Resource-constrained project scheduling at this scale is NP-hard, there is no ground truth to measure against, and a schedule has to be stable enough that the shop floor is not thrashed every time it changes. You will have the latitude to develop novel approaches and the obligation to ship them.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Formulate shipyard production scheduling as a mathematical optimization problem covering precedence with lag, disjunctive spatial exclusion, multi-resource capacity with qualification matching, calendars and shifts, and material availability.

• Own the solver-agnostic scheduling interface, integrate commercial and open-source solvers behind it, and benchmark them against each other on makespan, stability, resource utilization, and solve time.

• Build the two-tier replan path: fast local repair that returns a feasible schedule in seconds for a bounded affected subgraph, and background global re-solve that runs for minutes and swaps in when it beats the incumbent plan.

• Develop the stability objective that keeps a replan from needlessly moving work the factory has already staged, and the policy that decides when a better plan is worth the churn.

• Establish what "good enough" means when there is no ground truth: LP relaxation lower bounds, best-of-N ensemble upper bounds, quality ratios, and solution-quality regression tests that run on every change.

• Research and evaluate approaches beyond the V1 solver, including decomposition, metaheuristics, rolling-horizon methods, and non-traditional hardware (wafer-scale compute, quantum annealing) where they earn their place.

• Turn disruption events into replans: determine blast radius across the operation graph, scope the re-solve, merge the result into the live schedule, and resolve boundary conflicts.

• Build adaptive planning templates that generate recovery work (E.g. a damaged part that must be removed, replaced, and reinspected) by composing geometric queries with scheduling logic.

• Compose scheduled operations into work orders a manufacturing execution system can dispatch, and recompose them when the plan changes.

• Write production-quality code with comprehensive tests, participate in code review and architectural discussion, and instrument your systems so solution quality is observable, not just uptime.

• Partner with manufacturing engineers, planners, and factory operators to turn how the yard actually works into constraints and objectives.

• Work alongside the computational geometry engineer who derives geometric precedence from CAD, and the data engineers who supply the operation graph and the live factory event stream.

• Leverage AI tooling (coding assistants, automation) in your development workflow and contribute to team engineering practices.

• Join an on-call rotation supporting production scheduling systems.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• 5+ years of experience building production software systems, ideally in a fast-paced environment.

• Deep expertise in numerical optimization, including linear programming, mixed-integer linear programming, constraint programming, combinatorial optimization, or metaheuristics.

• Demonstrated ability to take a real-world problem, formulate it as a mathematical model, and carry that model all the way into a system other people depend on.

• Hands-on experience with optimization solvers and libraries (E.g. Gurobi, CPLEX, OR-Tools, SCIP, PuLP, CVXPY, Pyomo), including the judgment to recognize when a given solver or formulation is the wrong tool.

• Expert proficiency in Python for scientific computing and robust software development, with strong foundations in numerical computing libraries (NumPy, SciPy, Pandas).

• Strong theoretical and practical grounding in graph algorithms, constraint satisfaction, and computational complexity analysis.

• Experience with scheduling or resource allocation at a scale where exact methods stop working, and the judgment to know when to stop optimizing.

• Experience building systems that operate reliably under real operational constraints such as high availability, latency budgets, or degraded inputs.

• Excellent written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain an optimization trade-off to a factory planner who does not care about duality gaps.

• Advanced degree in Operations Research, Applied Mathematics, Computer Science, Industrial Engineering, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent depth built in practice.

• U.S. Person status is required as this position needs to access export controlled data.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Ph.D. in Operations Research, Applied Mathematics, or a closely related field, with publications or production work in scheduling or large-scale optimization.

• Experience with resource-constrained project scheduling (RCPSP), job shop scheduling, or precedence-constrained scheduling in a production setting.

• Experience with dynamic or online rescheduling: replanning under uncertainty, schedule stability, and rolling-horizon methods.

• Experience benchmarking solvers or algorithms where no ground-truth optimum exists, using dual bounds, anytime curves, or ablation across constraint classes.

• Experience with metaheuristics (genetic algorithms, simulated annealing, tabu search, large neighborhood search) and decomposition methods (Benders, column generation, Lagrangian relaxation).

• Experience with performance-critical implementation in C++ or Rust for optimization kernels or hot-path graph traversal.

• Familiarity with graph databases or large in-memory graph representations at 100K+ nodes.

• Experience in manufacturing, industrial, or OT-adjacent domains, and familiarity with BOM structures, manufacturing routing, work centers, and MES, ERP, PLM, or APS systems.

• Exposure to traditional and non-traditional optimization hardware e.g. GPU-accelerated solvers, HPC, or quantum annealing and QUBO formulations.

• Experience in hyper-growth startup-like environments, with demonstrated success balancing speed, ambiguity, and long-term system health.

• Familiarity with frontier AI tooling, AI coding assistants, and AI-enabled software development workflows.

• Experience in shipbuilding, aerospace, or complex discrete manufacturing.

• Eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret security clearance.

US Salary Range

$191,000—$253,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

jobs.title: Engineering Manager Runtime - Storage
jobs.description:
ABOUT BASETEN

Baseten powers mission-critical inference for the world's most dynamic AI companies, like Cursor, Notion, OpenEvidence, Abridge, Clay, Gamma, and Writer. By uniting applied AI research, flexible infrastructure, and seamless developer tooling, we enable companies operating at the frontier of AI to bring cutting-edge models into production. We're growing quickly and recently raised our $1.5B Series F https://www.baseten.co/blog/announcing-our-series-f/, led by Altimeter Capital, Conviction Partners, and Spark Capital. Join us and help build the platform engineers turn to ship AI products.



THE ROLE

Container runtimes were designed for general-purpose software workloads. AI inference is not a general-purpose workload.

Running large models at production scale exposes cracks in every layer of the container stack: runtimes unaware of GPU memory constraints, images that take minutes to pull when a model needs to scale to thousands of replicas, and isolation mechanisms that weren’t designed for the multi-tenant serving environments that production AI requires. The tools the industry has relied on for a decade weren’t built for this, and patching around those limitations at higher layers only goes so far.

Baseten owns the entire pipeline, from the moment a developer pushes a model to the moment a request gets a response. That vertical ownership means we can fix these problems at the root. The Runtime Fabric team is doing exactly that: purpose-building the container runtime and storage layers for AI inference workloads, led by some of the world’s top containerd maintainers.

As Engineering Manager for Storage Products on the Runtime Fabric team, you will lead the engineers who build and run the storage products behind that stack: the Baseten Delivery Network (BDN), which sits in the cold start path of every model on the platform, the snapshotters and filesystems that expose model weights and container images to a running container, and the storage that model deployment and training need next. The team is advancing the next generation of caching for inference workloads, from the origin tier to the GPU host. You will own reliability for the area as a measured outcome, report to the head of Runtime Fabric, and stay close to the code through design and code review. If you’ve managed systems engineers and have hands-on experience with caching, content-addressable storage, or distributed filesystems, we’d love to talk.

EXAMPLE INITIATIVES

 - How the Baseten Delivery Network (BDN) makes cold starts fast https://www.baseten.co/blog/how-the-baseten-delivery-network-bdn-makes-cold-starts-fast/

 - Extending BDN from model weights to container image layers, training checkpoints, and deployment artifacts

 - Lazy-loading snapshotters and block-level delivery (EROFS, FUSE, ublk) so a container can start before the full image or model has arrived

RESPONSIBILITIES

Team Leadership and Culture

 - Hire and grow a team of 5 to 10 systems engineers with storage, caching, and Linux expertise

 - Run the team’s planning and delivery: scope work against the Runtime Fabric roadmap, set priorities, and ship on a predictable cadence

 - Provide regular coaching, feedback, and career development support to your direct reports

 - Own on-call health for the team’s services, including escalation paths and follow-through on incidents

Technical Direction

 - Guide the architecture and evolution of the Baseten Delivery Network: the tiered caching and weight delivery product that makes cold starts 2-3x faster and eliminates thundering herd failures during burst scaling events

 - Shape storage products tailored to Baseten’s workloads: extend BDN from model weights to container images, training checkpoints, and deployment artifacts, and define the interfaces that model deployment, training, and customers use to reach them

 - Oversee the on-host side of delivery: lazy-loading snapshotters, EROFS and overlayfs layouts, and block-level delivery (FUSE, ublk) for multi-gigabyte files

 - Own reliability of the delivery path as a measured outcome: end-to-end instrumentation from snapshotter initialization to first inference request, targets for cold start and cache behavior, tolerance for failing upstream registries and object stores, and safe rollout of changes to a path every customer depends on

 - Make the delivery path work across heterogeneous clusters and cloud providers, each with its own object store and network

 - Review designs and code across the area, and take on hands-on work where it unblocks the team

 - Champion the team’s contributions back to containerd and the snapshotter ecosystem alongside the maintainers on the Runtime Fabric team

Cross-Functional Partnership

 - Act as the point of contact for storage across Baseten, ensuring model deployment, training, and platform teams have the integration support they need

 - Optimize requirements for the underlying storage platforms with the infrastructure team: object storage, local NVMe and block storage, and network bandwidth per cluster, so that capacity and provider decisions account for what the delivery path needs

 - Manage the team’s dependencies in both directions: sequence work that model deployment, training, and infrastructure teams block on, and negotiate interfaces and timelines with the teams and upstream projects the storage path depends on

 - Work with the head of Runtime Fabric and product stakeholders to prioritize storage investments based on customer impact and infrastructure reliability

 - Communicate team progress, technical trade-offs, and incidents clearly to the team and to leadership

REQUIREMENTS

 - Experience managing a team of engineers in a systems, infrastructure, or storage context, including hiring and performance management [TODO: confirm whether a tech lead stepping into management qualifies]

 - Hands-on background in distributed storage systems, content-addressable storage, or large-scale caching infrastructure

 - Strong systems programming background in Go, Rust, and/or C/C++, with the ability to engage credibly in code reviews and architectural discussions

 - Working knowledge of the Linux storage stack: filesystems, the page cache, block devices, and mounts

 - Understanding of how container images are structured, stored, and delivered at scale

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence without authority across teams

NICE TO HAVE

 - Contributions to containerd/containerd, snapshotter projects (stargz, soci, nydus, overlaybd), distribution/distribution, or closely related open-source projects

 - Familiarity with lazy-loading snapshotters or peer-to-peer image distribution

 - Experience with EROFS, FUSE, ublk, or io_uring

 - Experience building or operating CDN, object storage, or large-scale caching infrastructure

 - Experience running storage services on Kubernetes



BENEFITS

 - Competitive compensation, including meaningful equity

 - (U.S. only) 100% coverage of medical, dental, and vision insurance for employee and dependents

 - Flexible PTO policy including company wide Winter Break (our offices are closed from Christmas Eve to New Year's Day!)

 - Paid parental leave

 - Fertility and family-building stipend through Carrot

 - (U.S. only) Company-facilitated 401(k)

 - Exposure to a variety of ML startups, offering unparalleled learning and networking opportunities.

Apply now to embark on a rewarding journey in shaping the future of AI! If you are a motivated individual with a passion for machine learning and a desire to be part of a collaborative and forward-thinking team, we would love to hear from you.

At Baseten, we are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. We provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, genetic information, disability, or veteran status.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and will consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable law (by example, the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, where applicable).

jobs.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI’s Client Platform Engineering team builds and operates the platforms that make employee devices secure, reliable, and easy to use. Our work spans device posture and trust, onboarding, application delivery, operating-system updates, fleet telemetry, and employee-facing remediation. We partner with Security, IT, Research, Applied, and specialized engineering teams to reduce friction while protecting OpenAI’s systems and data.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Client Platform Engineer, You will build and own agentic solutions that automate OAI fleet operations and reduce employee friction, with measurable outcomes and reliability. You will develop first-party software, integrate commercial and open-source tools, and own changes from design and testing through deployment and production operations. Your work will improve security, reliability, and the employee experience.

We’re looking for people who are passionate about automation, endpoint security, and building scalable solutions that improve employee experience. You should have deep experience securing and managing Linux fleets at scale, with strong software engineering skills to automate security controls and fleet operations across environments with different compliance requirements. Your problem-solving mindset and attention to detail will be key to success in this role.

In this role, you will:

Build the platforms that help employees do their best work on devices they can trust.

 - Own the design, development, deployment, and operation of secure Linux endpoint management systems across environments with different compliance requirements.

 - Create magical employee experiences by building agentic workflows with OpenAI products and models that use fleet telemetry to anticipate issues, guide remediation, and design friction out of everyday work.

 - Make new hires productive from day one, using OpenAI products to simplify device setup, software delivery, and onboarding support.

 - Build secure, reliable workflows with scoped access, human review for sensitive changes, traceable actions, and tested recovery.

 - Partner with IT, Security, Research, and Engineering to deliver consistent Linux provisioning, updates, and support alongside macOS and Windows.

 - Develop first-party software and integrate commercial and open-source tools for software packaging, deployment, and application management.

 - Manage fleet configuration as code through GitOps, version control, peer review, and automated validation.

 - Build and operate CI/CD pipelines for fleet infrastructure across Azure, AWS, and GCP, with staged deployments and tested rollback.

 - Use fleet telemetry to proactively improve performance and reliability, detect configuration drift, and verify deployment outcomes.

 - Participate in engineering on-call, own incident resolution, and turn operational lessons into lasting improvements that reduce recurring failures and manual work.


YOU MAY BE A FIT FOR THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE: 

 - Proficiency in Python, Go, or another modern programming language.

 - Deep experience securing and managing Linux fleets with configuration management, MDM, device enrollment, policy enforcement, and cloud identity integration.

 - Demonstrated success with open-source endpoint tools for configuration, device and application management, and telemetry.

 - Experience delivering secure, reliable, scalable systems across different compliance requirements.

 - Deep experience managing infrastructure at scale with IaC and GitOps, using tools such as Terraform, Ansible, and Chef.

 - Experience integrating and operating fleet infrastructure with CI/CD and DevOps workflows.

 - A track record of deploying and operating fleet infrastructure in public cloud environments (Azure, AWS, GCP).

 - Initiative, analytical judgment, and the ability to turn problems into practical improvements.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE:

 - Deep experience with open-source fleet management tools and frameworks.

 - Experience with containerization technologies such as Docker and Kubernetes.

 - Familiarity with compliance frameworks such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP, and NIST.

 - Strong soft skills, including stakeholder communication and cross-functional collaboration.

jobs.title: IT Network Engineer (OT)
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

IT NETWORK ENGINEER (OT)

SpaceX is looking for an Operational Technology (OT) Network Engineer with experience in routing, switching, and wireless in industrial network environments. This employee will be a member of the IT Network Engineering team, which is responsible for maintaining a stable, reliable, and diverse network. This network supports the design, manufacturing, and launching of rockets, spacecraft, satellites, and human spaceflight. This position will design and support industrial and OT networks for production, test, site operations, and live data center build environments. The ideal candidate will be a great communicator, able to document work in a ticketing system, excel at multi-tasking, resolve issues to prevent failures, and enjoy a fast-paced high-tech environment.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Design and implement highly available networks, balancing routing and redundancy for production, test, and site requirements.

• Design and validate resilient, scalable multi-site OT network topologies for critical facilities.

• Evaluate, procure, and deploy network hardware: switches, firewalls, multiplexing, and SD-WAN appliances.

• Develop and contribute to network automation tooling, including configuration analysis and scalable deployment.

• Plan and coordinate network outage windows with stakeholders for software updates, hardware refreshes, and maintenance.

• Troubleshoot and resolve network issues. Publish root-cause analysis and host retrospective reviews.

• Provide networking support during launch and test campaigns, including on-call or real-time support as the networking responsible engineer.

• Tune network monitoring for operational telemetry and issue detection before impact.

• Create and update network documentation: architecture overviews, design drawings, and operational procedures.

• Work with cross-functional teams on network designs, including failure modes and redundancy.

• Perform job walks with customers, vendors, and contractors to gather requirements and create implementation plans.

• Segment industrial networks from campus and corporate networks. Maintain controls-network segmentation.

• Author system and network architecture drawings, IP/VLAN schemes, and data flow diagrams.

• Support on-site deployment, physical network cutovers, and new site commissioning.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, or other STEM discipline and 3+ years of professional network engineering experience; OR 5+ years of professional network engineering experience and high school diploma or equivalency certificate in lieu of a degree.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Industrial, utility, or operational technology network engineering experience.

• Understanding of the OSI model and network standards.

• Cisco, Arista, and Juniper data center-class switches.

• Wave Division Multiplexing (WDM) and fiber optics infrastructure.

• Enterprise and media protocols.

• Switch port security features, network segmentation, QoS, multicast, and redundancy protocols.

• Network monitoring tools and layer-1 testing tools.

• Scripting (Bash, PowerShell, Python) and automation frameworks (Terraform, Ansible).

• Linux and Windows system administration.

• GitOps and infrastructure as code, as a user and as a contributor.

• Layer 2 and Layer 3 design, deployment, and troubleshooting in latency-sensitive or industrial environments.

• Functional experience with multiple network vendors in production or lab environments.

• Hands-on configuration of managed industrial switches and routers.

• Real-time systems, industrial control networks, or OT environments in aerospace, defense, energy, oil and gas, or similar high-reliability industries.

• Industry-standard certifications such as CCNA, CCNP, JNCIS, or JNCIP.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• This role requires you to be onsite. Hybrid or remote work will not be considered.

• Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed.

• Must have a valid driver's license.

• Ability to lift heavy objects up to 35 lbs. unassisted.

• Ability to provide 24x7 on-call support in emergency situations and participate in an after-hours on-call rotation.

• Willingness to occasionally travel to other sites to support new company initiatives.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

jobs.title: Enterprise Security Engineer, Vulnerability Management
jobs.description:
About the Team

Enterprise Security protects the systems, identities, devices, and services that enable OpenAI's employees to work securely and effectively. We partner across IT and Security to understand risk, build practical defenses, and support a rapidly evolving technical environment.

About the Role

We are looking for an Enterprise Security Engineer with a focus on vulnerability management, novel vulnerabilities, and zero-day response. You will investigate vulnerabilities and security weaknesses across networks, endpoints, and SaaS, prioritize them in the context of real exposure, and drive remediation through verified outcomes.

You will also build security capabilities and automation, use AI agents to solve practical problems, and help shape how enterprise security operates as agents become a larger part of everyday work.

This role is open to candidates in San Francisco, CA, and to remote candidates in the United States.

In this role, you will:

 - Discover, investigate, and prioritize vulnerabilities and misconfigurations across enterprise systems, including novel vulnerabilities and zero-days with incomplete information and no established playbook.

 - Translate technical findings into clear attack paths, business impact, and actionable remediation.

 - Develop and validate emergency mitigations when patches are unavailable, coordinate with system owners, vendors, and incident responders, and drive durable fixes through verified closure.

 - Improve asset visibility, ownership, vulnerability data quality, and reporting.

 - Build and operate security tools and integrations using code, APIs, automation, and AI agents.

 - Design controls for agent access, execution, and accountability.

 - Contribute across endpoint, network, identity, and SaaS security, and support incident investigations when needed.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have independently investigated novel or emerging vulnerabilities and driven enterprise remediation from uncertain initial reports through mitigation and verified closure.

 - Bring technical depth in a relevant security domain and working knowledge across networks, endpoints, and SaaS.

 - Can understand and improve code and safely integrate APIs and security systems.

 - Have solved substantive problems using AI agents and can explain how you evaluated and corrected their work.

 - Think clearly about security tradeoffs, ambiguous evidence, and the changing risks of agentic systems.

 - Collaborate effectively, take ownership, and communicate technical risk to varied audiences.

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. jobs.description:
Zscaler (NASDAQ: ZS) accelerates digital transformation so customers can be more agile, efficient, resilient, and secure. We are looking for a Sr. Manager, People Data Infrastructure and Platforms to join our team. • You are a high-trust collaborator who communicates with clarity, candor, and respect, building strong cross-functional partnerships across People, IT, and enterprise data teams.

What Will Make You Stand Out (Preferred Qualifications)

jobs.description:
Voyager is an innovative space, defense, and national security technology company committed to advancing and delivering transformative, mission-critical solutions. We tackle the most complex challenges to unlock new frontiers for human progress, fortify national security, and protect critical assets to lead in the race for technological and operational superiority from ground to space.

Forge the Future: Join Voyager Technologies

The future belongs to those who build it. At Voyager Technologies, we’re building technologies that protect lives, expand frontiers, and prepare us for what’s next. And we’re doing that with people who are wired to solve, build, adapt and lead. These roles are not for the faint of heart.

You’ll help lay the foundation for humanity's future. Join a culture where innovation thrives, curiosity is rewarded, and impact is real. We’re a company of doers, thinkers, and builders, united by purpose and grounded in reality.

If you want to put your skills to work where the stakes are real and the mission is bigger than any one person, forge the future with Voyager.

Job Summary:

The Master Scheduler plays a crucial role within the Program Controls function, collaborating closely with the Program Controls Analyst to support a diverse portfolio of aerospace programs for DoD, NASA, and commercial customers. These programs encompass Firm Fixed Price, Cost-Plus, and pure commercial contracts, some of which necessitate ANSI/EIA-748-compliant Earned Value Management Systems (EVMS). This role involves developing and maintaining Integrated Master Schedules (IMS) using Microsoft Project as the enterprise scheduling tool. The Program Controls Scheduler ensures cost-schedule integration, supports effective program planning and execution, and customizes scheduling strategies to align with each program's unique lifecycle, risk posture, and contractual requirements. This position requires a high degree of collaboration among engineering, business, and operational teams to ensure that programs are delivered on time, within budget, and with full visibility into performance.

Responsibilities:

• Develop, maintain, and control Integrated Master Schedules (IMS) aligned with the WBS, Control Account structure, and contractual deliverables.

• Apply Critical Path Methodology (CPM), perform schedule integrity checks, and maintain logical network relationships.

• Integrate schedules with cost and risk systems to support full cost-schedule integration and, when required, Earned Value Management (EVM).

• Establish and maintain schedule baselines; support baseline change management and Integrated Baseline Reviews (IBRs).

• Perform schedule performance analysis, including variance analysis, float analysis, critical path identification, metrics, Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), and trend assessments.

• Support Estimate to Complete (ETC), Estimate at Completion (EAC), and forecasting processes in partnership with the Program Controls Analyst.

• Tailor scheduling and planning approaches to suit program type—ranging from highly regulated government programs to agile commercial efforts.

• Support proposal activities by developing proposal-level schedules aligned with technical and cost strategies.

• Collaborate daily with Program Managers, CAMs, engineers, contracts, procurement, finance, quality, and other functions to ensure integrated execution.

• Present schedule performance data and recommendations to leadership, customer stakeholders, and functional teams.

• Contribute to process improvement initiatives and support tool integrations across cost, schedule, and risk and change management systems.

Required Qualifications:

• Three (3+) or more years of experience in project scheduling or program planning within aerospace, defense, or other technically complex environments, supporting diverse program types.

• Bachelor’s degree in Program Management, Engineering, Construction Management, Business Administration, Finance, or related field.

• Extensive experience developing and maintaining logic-driven network schedules for complex programs.

• Deep knowledge of Critical Path Methodology (CPM), float analysis, and schedule risk assessment.

• Experience with schedule baseline development and change control processes.

• Familiarity with Earned Value Management (EVM) principles and schedule integration techniques.

• Proficiency in Microsoft Project (enterprise scheduling tool) and Microsoft Office applications.

• Strong written, visual, and verbal communication skills, including experience briefing program leadership.

• Ability to work across multiple programs with varying contract types, lifecycle phases, and reporting requirements.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Experience supporting DoD, NASA, or government aerospace programs with full EVM and IBR participation.

• Experience integrating MS Project with cost and performance tools (e.g., Cobra, wInsight, EVMS for Project, or internal dashboards).

• Experience tailoring scheduling practices for commercial programs and agile development environments.

• Strong organizational skills and ability to manage competing priorities across multiple programs.

• Ability to assess and improve existing planning processes and tools.

jobs.title: Director, Clinical Monitoring Oversight
jobs.description:
Olema Oncology is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company committed to transforming the standard of care and improving outcomes for patients living with breast cancer and beyond. With our transformation into a fully integrated oncology company well underway, it’s an exciting time to be part of Team Olema.

Our lead product candidate, palazestrant, is a novel, orally available complete estrogen receptor antagonist (CERAN) and selective estrogen receptor degrader (SERD) currently in two pivotal Phase 3 clinical trials. We expect top-line data from OPERA-01, our ongoing Phase 3 trial of palazestrant as a monotherapy in patients with second- or third-line ER+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer (MBC), in Q1 2027 which, if positive, could lead to our first potential approval and commercial launch in 2028. OPERA-02, our Phase 3 trial of palazestrant in combination with ribociblib in patients with frontline ER+/HER2- MBC, is enrolling patients. Together with its mechanism of action, pharmacokinetic properties, and the potential to demonstrate activity in both ESR1 wild-type and mutant tumors, palazestrant could transform the metastatic breast cancer treatment paradigm and provide access to a $15 billion global market opportunity.

Our follow-on product candidate, OP-3136, is a potent KAT6 inhibitor with the potential to generate further value and meaningfully impact the metastatic breast cancer treatment landscape – particularly in combination with palazestrant. We recently presented encouraging Phase 1 monotherapy data from this program across multiple solid tumor types, are advancing patient enrollment in the ongoing combination arms in MBC, and expect to initiate a Phase 1 study of OP-3136 in combination with Bayer’s darolutamide in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer by the end of this year.

Aspiring to transform the metastatic treatment paradigm is an ambitious endeavor that requires a resolute approach to developing better therapies and passionate colleagues dedicated to helping the patients we serve feel better, longer. Team Olema possesses a deep commitment to a shared purpose, the sustained pursuit of excellence, cultivating the courage required to advance our programs, the drive to succeed, and a collective capacity for adaptability through learning, growth, and evolution. We are a small group of nimble self-starters who bring consistency in our quest for the extraordinary every single day.

If you’re ready to be part of a tenacious, courageous, agile, and growing team, join us in making a profound impact, together – for our patients, for your career, and for what’s beyond.

About the Role >>> Director, Clinical Monitoring Oversight

As the Director, Clinical Monitoring Oversight reporting to the Vice President, Clinical Operations you will provide strategic and operational leadership for global clinical monitoring oversight across Olema’s clinical programs. This role ensures that clinical monitoring, whether by internal teams, through Functional Service Providers (FSPs), or outsourced to Clinical Research Organizations (CROs), is executed with high standards of quality and consistency while maintaining compliance with GCP regulations. The Director oversees Olema’s Clinical Monitoring Oversight Leads, regional monitoring and oversight teams, clinical service provider/FSP provider, and site performance. This role will develop and implement global monitoring oversight strategies and standards for Olema’s clinical monitoring execution, driving operational excellence, data integrity, and inspection readiness across all trials with an emphasis on risk-based, data driven processes. The role will adapt to evolving organizational structures, monitoring delivery models, and clinical development needs as Olema's portfolio and operational requirements change.

This role is based out of either our San Francisco or Cambridge office and will require 10-20% travel.

Your work will primarily encompass:

• Provide strategic direction and operational oversight of all global monitoring activities across Olema’s clinical programs

• Oversee internal clinical monitoring and/or oversight team and FSP vendor responsible for providing Clinical Oversight Monitors (COMs) and/or Clinical Research Associates, ensuring alignment, consistency, and accountability across global regions

• Adapt clinical monitoring and oversight strategies, organizational structures, resource allocation, and operating models to meet evolving clinical development and business needs

• Oversee clinical monitoring and/or monitoring oversight resource planning, utilization, and related budgets and forecasts, ensuring alignment with study priorities, risk, workload, and portfolio needs

• Establish and maintain effective governance with the FSP partner, including performance management, risk mitigation, and continuous improvement in monitoring quality and efficiency

• In collaboration with assigned Clinical Trial Leads, define and implement Olema’s clinical monitoring and oversight strategy, including risk-based and centralized monitoring approaches in alignment with ICH-GCP and regulatory expectations

• Ensure global harmonization of clinical monitoring and oversight processes, training, and documentation across programs and regions

• Develop and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) and quality metrics to evaluate site performance, FSP delivery, and regional oversight effectiveness

• Collaborate with Clinical Operations, Data Management, Clinical Compliance, Clinical Quality, Pharmacovigilance, Clinical Science, and Clinical Development to ensure monitoring activities are aligned with program objectives and timelines

• Contribute to the development and review of key operational documents, including Monitoring Plans, Oversight Plans, Risk Management Plans, and audit/inspection responses

• Proactively assess monitoring risks and implement mitigation strategies to maintain inspection readiness

• Lead, manage, and mentor internal monitoring and oversight staff, fostering collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement

• Support organizational capability development, succession planning, and evolving staffing needs to ensure effective monitoring and oversight as the clinical portfolio changes

• Serve as the Monitoring Oversight representative on cross-functional and governance teams, presenting program updates, risks, and mitigation strategies to senior management

• Drive innovation and process optimization in monitoring oversight practices, including leveraging technology and data analytics to enhance quality and efficiency

• Establish and implement monitoring oversight reporting processes, tools, and communication pathways to ensure COMLs provide timely, consistent, and actionable updates to Clinical Trial Leads (CTLs), enabling effective collaboration, risk escalation, and CTL accountability for monitoring quality and performance within their assigned trials

• May perform the full scope of Clinical Oversight Monitor Lead (COML) responsibilities, including direct oversight of assigned COMs, sites and CRAs, as needed based on study requirements, resource availability, and/or organizational priorities

Ideal Candidate Profile >>>

A love of challenging, important work. We are a pragmatic team, driven to imagine and develop meaningful therapies for improving lives. All employees within our company play a unique and crucial role in our success, both in accomplishing our mission and building a positive company culture. As such, we are looking for someone with the right combination of knowledge, experience, and attributes for this role.

jobs.title: Software Engineer (Early Career) – C++ & Systems
jobs.description:
About SirenOpt

SirenOpt helps manufacturers make better, safer, and more reliable micro- and nano-materials. These materials are the building blocks of critical sectors of the global economy such as batteries, computer chips, aircraft components, and power systems. But, surging material demand and growing complexity are pushing production to unprecedented scales and speeds, leaving manufacturers effectively flying blind. Small, undetected variations during production lead to wastage, lower performance, higher costs, and safety risks.

SirenOpt is changing this by developing a manufacturing intelligence platform that non-destructively probes materials during production, revealing critical internal information without damaging them. Using a novel combination of cold atmospheric plasma, physics-informed machine learning, and predictive analytics, SirenOpt generates unique, real-time material fingerprints that capture material signals not accessible through conventional measurement techniques. These insights give manufacturers unprecedented visibility into how materials behave as they are made.

We turn hidden data into actionable intelligence to help manufacturers reduce variability and thus increase yield and performance. The technology can be deployed as a standalone tool or integrated directly into factory production lines. SirenOpt is currently deploying early versions of its platform with some of the largest industrial manufacturers in the world across North America, Europe, and Asia.

About the job

Job Title: Software Engineer (Early Career) – C++ & Systems

Location: On-Site (San Leandro, CA)

Job Type: Full-Time

Role Overview

SirenOpt is seeking a Software Engineer to help build and maintain the real-time data pipeline behind our sensing platform: acquiring data from multiple sensors, processing and storing it on Linux-based systems, and delivering it to the applications our customers rely on.

You will work primarily in modern C++ and Python, with mentorship from senior engineers, and you will be hands-on with real hardware in our lab to test and validate what you build. This is a role for someone who wants to grow into a well-rounded systems engineer by shipping production software end to end, from a first design discussion to a feature running at a customer site.

What You'll Do

• Develop and maintain software components in modern C++ (C++17/20) for Linux-based systems, with guidance from senior engineers

• Implement features, fix bugs, and write unit and integration tests across the data pipeline, from sensor acquisition through processing and storage to the services that deliver results to applications

• Write and maintain Python scripts for automation, testing, and data analysis

• Read, and where needed modify, existing code written in other languages across our codebase

• Use AI coding tools (e.g., Claude Code, GitHub Copilot) to accelerate development, and verify their output through testing, profiling, and code review

• Run the system on real hardware in the lab to test and validate your changes, including setting up sensors and collecting data

• Participate in code reviews, both receiving and giving feedback, and follow team conventions for code quality

• Help diagnose and debug issues across software and hardware boundaries, working with firmware and hardware engineers

• Measure and improve performance of existing code under the direction of senior engineers

• Document your work so that others on the team can build on it

What We're Looking For

• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field (recent graduates welcome)

• 0–2 years of professional software development experience; internships, co-ops, research, and substantial personal or open-source projects count

• Solid foundation in C++, including memory management, references and pointers, the standard library, and basic object-oriented and generic programming

• Strong ability to read, understand, and write Python, including working within existing Python codebases used for automation, testing, and data analysis

• Ability to pick up new programming languages quickly; our codebase spans several languages and you will need to read, and occasionally modify, code outside of C++ and Python

• Understanding of core computer science fundamentals: data structures, algorithms, operating systems, and concurrency basics

• Comfortable with the everyday toolchain: Linux command line, build tools (CMake or similar), a debugger, and Git-based workflows (branches, pull requests, code review)

• Hands-on experience using AI coding tools (e.g., Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Cursor) as part of a real development workflow, and the judgment to review and test what they produce

• Comfortable working hands-on with lab and test equipment: setting up sensors, running the system on real hardware, and collecting data for testing and validation (we will train you on our specific equipment)

• Clear written and verbal communication, and the ability to work well with teammates across disciplines

Nice to have:

• Experience with Qt, gRPC, or Protocol Buffers

• Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines and automated testing

• Experience with profiling and debugging tools such as perf, Valgrind, GDB, or sanitizers

• Familiarity with hardware communication interfaces such as Ethernet, USB, or Serial

• Contributions to open-source projects

What You'll Learn

You will work on a real-time sensing platform that is already running at some of the largest manufacturers in the world, on a small team where your code reaches customers quickly.

• How a high-throughput, multi-sensor data pipeline is built end to end, from acquisition through processing and storage, and kept reliable in production

• Modern C++ and Linux systems engineering, with regular code review and mentorship from senior engineers

• How software, firmware, and hardware teams work together to ship a physical product

• How to use AI coding tools effectively and responsibly in a professional engineering workflow

• A clear path to grow into a mid-level engineer with ownership of your own components

Base Pay Range

$120,000—$160,000 USD

Benefits

• Equity and Salary compensation depends on experience

• Health, Dental, Vision plans provided

• 401k matching provided

• Time off: 20 days of PTO per year, plus approximately 15 paid US holidays per year

jobs.title: User Success Manager
jobs.description:
About us

Imbue is a radically different AI company.

We believe that data should belong to you, humans should come before technology, and everyone deserves to own a personal team of AI agents. We believe in a future of open agents that you can modify to do exactly what you want.

We’re building a suite of tools to make tech serve humans, and making it open source.

Some first projects include

• Studio: A custom digital HQ for building personalized software, apps, and tools

• Bouncer: A social media feed filter that removes what you don't want to see and retrains your algorithm

• Sculptor: An interface for programmers to run coding agents in parallel and stay in flow

• mngr: A command-line tool for managing agents

• Vet: A standalone tool that catches AI coding mistakes and reviews full PRs

• Offload: A tool that automatically distributes your tests to run in isolated sandboxes

• Latchkey: A command-line tool to integrate local agents with third-party APIs

• Darwinian Evolver: A near-universal optimizer for code and agents

And we’re just getting started. If you’re excited about building a future with open agents, say hi!

We're supported by investors like Nvidia, Simon Last (co-founder of Notion), and Eric Schmidt (former CEO of Google), with $200M raised at over $1B valuation.

Summary

We’re looking for a technical, people-oriented builder to help people get the most out of Imbue’s products, and help us build better products in return.

You’ll be one of the closest people at Imbue to our users. You’ll help them get started, understand what they’re trying to accomplish, troubleshoot problems alongside them, and discover where our products feel magical or fall short. You’ll bring what you learn directly back to product and engineering, helping shape what we build next.

You’ll also build the community around our products: creating spaces for people to learn from each other, share what they’re building, contribute ideas, and help shape the future of our products alongside us.

This isn’t a traditional community management role. It’s part technical problem-solving, part customer success, part community building, and part product discovery.

What you'll do

Your goal is simple: help people do cool things with our products, and make our products better because of them.

• Work directly with users to get them set up, troubleshoot technical problems, and help them discover what they can do with our products.

• Build deep relationships with our most engaged users and understand their goals, workflows, frustrations, and ideas.

• Become an expert on our products and translate complicated technical concepts into useful, approachable guidance.

• Create onboarding, documentation, examples, workshops, office hours, and other resources that help more people succeed.

• Build and grow our user community, online and in person, and create reasons for people to learn, share, contribute, and come back.

• Develop an unusually tight feedback loop between users and our product and engineering teams. Surface patterns, unexpected use cases, friction, and ideas that should influence what we build.

• Find and tell great stories about what people are building with Imbue.

• Build the systems and processes that allow us to support a much larger community as we grow.

About you

• You’ve worked in technical community, developer relations, technical customer success, solutions engineering, or another technical, user-facing role.

• You’re technical enough to dig into how a product works, reproduce problems, troubleshoot with users, and communicate effectively with engineers.

• You love talking to users and have a knack for getting past what someone asks for to understand what they actually need.

• You can explain complicated technical ideas simply and clearly.

• You’re good at building genuine relationships and communities, not just driving “engagement.”

• You instinctively turn repeated problems into better documentation, tooling, product experiences, or processes.

• You have strong product intuition and can distinguish an interesting anecdote from a pattern worth acting on.

• You’re comfortable with ambiguity and excited to build something before there’s a playbook for how to do it.

Compensation & Benefits

• Lunch provided daily (SF office)
• $250 lifestyle stipend per month
• Generous budget for self-improvement: coaching, courses, conferences, etc.
• Actively co-create and participate in a positive, intentional team culture
• Frequent team events, dinners, off-sites, and hangouts

The base salary range for this role is $140,000–$175,000 per year.

jobs.title: Product Design Intern
jobs.description:
COMPANY OVERVIEW

Each year, 2.5 trillion hours are spent on household chores. At Matic, we’re on a mission to recapture that lost time, and we’re doing it by revolutionizing home robotics.

Our first product, also called Matic, is a Wall-E-esque floor cleaning robot. We've built what amounts to "full self-driving in the home” with real-time 3D mapping, adaptive path-tracking, and a precise semantic understanding of the home. Our breakthroughs in spatial AI allow Matic to work reliably in real homes, using only RGB cameras and neural networks running on-device.




PRIVACY FIRST

What happens in the home, stays in the home. Our robots are private by design, with all data processing performed by the robot itself, not in the cloud.




OUR APPROACH

Before the iPhone, consumers adopted several distinct devices; cell phones, PDAs, and portable music players each served a particular need. We believe in a similar progression for home robotics, starting with single-purpose robots and building iteratively toward more complex capabilities over time.




OUR CULTURE

Matic is a tight-knit and collaborative team, singularly focused on building products our customers will cherish. We're ultra-hardworking people committed to solving tough problems that save precious time and energy.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Help shape how people live with a robot in their home. At Matic, we’re bringing advanced robotics into everyday life, and design plays a central role in making that experience feel natural. We’re looking for a Product Design Intern with curiosity, a strong eye for craft, and a drive to turn ideas into something people can experience. You’ll work closely with design and engineering to explore new possibilities and make the product more intuitive, thoughtful, and delightful to use. Your time will be a mix of exploring concepts, building prototypes, sharing ideas, and refining interactions. You’ll use Figma and AI tools to bring concepts to life, test how they feel, and help the team decide what to build. With room to experiment, you’ll contribute to meaningful product work while developing your own design judgment.

What You Will Do

 - Explore and design experiences that connect people, software, and the physical world.

 - Translate complex problems into clear flows, thoughtful interactions, and polished interfaces.

 - Build interactive prototypes with Figma and AI tools to evaluate concepts and communicate design intent.

 - Present your thinking, explore different directions, and refine your work through experimentation and team critique.

 - Collaborate with engineers to understand possibilities, work through constraints, and bring ideas into the product.

 - Follow designs through implementation, paying attention to the details that shape how an experience feels.

 - Contribute to a consistent visual and interaction language across Matic’s product experience.

What You Bring

 - Curiosity about technology and a habit of asking how an experience could be better.

 - Strong foundations in interaction and visual design, including layout, typography, hierarchy, and composition.

 - A portfolio that shows thoughtful problem-solving, design craft, and your approach to developing ideas. School, personal, and internship projects are welcome.

 - Comfort working in Figma and enthusiasm for exploring AI tools in your design process.

 - The ability to communicate your ideas clearly and explain the decisions behind your work.

 - Openness to feedback and a willingness to experiment, iterate, and learn.

 - Care for the small details and an interest in how they contribute to the whole experience.

Nice to Have

 - Experience building functional prototypes with AI tools or code.

 - Familiarity with motion design or spatial interactions.

 - An understanding of mobile design patterns, accessibility, or design systems.

 - Interest in consumer technology, robotics, and products that connect digital and physical experiences.

Portfolio (Required)

Show us how you think and what you make. We’d like to see the questions you explored, the approaches you tried, and the decisions that shaped your work. Interactive prototypes, experiments, and short demos are welcome alongside finished designs.
If you used AI tools, tell us how they supported your process and where your design judgment guided the outcome.
Please include your portfolio password, if applicable.

With intelligent borrowing, savings, and budgeting capabilities, Oportun empowers members with the confidence to build a better financial future. Since inception, Oportun has provided more than $22.7 billion in responsible and affordable credit, saved its members more than $2.5 billion in interest and fees, and helped its members set aside an average of more than $1,800 annually.

The Opportunity

Oportun is currently seeking qualified candidates with customer service, cashier, sales, or hospitality experience to work Full-Time. At Oportun, we consider our customers to be our members, and the primary focus of our Member Loyalty Representatives is to create and generate a rewarding and unique member service experience.

Our Member Loyalty Representatives are passionate about listening, helping, and connecting with people at all touchpoints, such as in our stores and in the communities around our stores through personal outreach activities. As a key member of our team, you will make the mission of Oportun come to life by educating our members and communities about our inclusive, affordable financial services that empower them to build a better future.

At Oportun, we move fast and we hold each other to a high bar. If you care about doing your best work while actually moving the needle for real people, you'll fit right in.

Conducting outreach efforts at local flea markets, community events, and at our Lending As A Service (LAAS) partner locations to increase awareness, capture leads, and assist with starting applications; Actively engaging with people at and around Oportun’s retail locations, encouraging store visits, and assisting with applications. Who You Are

You're comfortable navigating complexity and don't wait for perfect information to move forward. You communicate clearly, give direct feedback, and expect the same in return.

What You Bring

Required

Compensation

Why Oportun

What's in it for you

Oportun offers a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to support your physical, financial, and professional well-being. Benefits vary by country of employment.

As a Valuable Member of Our Team, You’ll Receive

Our AI Mindset

jobs.title: Head of Strategic Partnerships
jobs.description:
Human Interest is on a mission to ensure that people in all lines of work have access to retirement benefits.

More than half of all working Americans are not saving enough for their future. Too often, it’s because they are employed by a company that doesn’t offer a retirement plan. Human Interest is changing that by making it affordable and accessible for small and medium-sized businesses to offer employees a path to financial independence through retirement savings.

We’re a high-growth fintech company changing the retirement industry. We are backed by a number of investors. This includes funding from Marshall Wace and Baillie Gifford, as well as top investors such as BlackRock, TPG (The Rise Fund), SoftBank, Glynn Capital, NewView Capital, USVP, Wing, Uncork, and more.

About the role

The Head of Strategic Partnerships owns a vital piece of Human Interest's most important growth channel: expanding our ecosystem of partners who put our retirement platform in front of millions of small and medium-sized businesses. Reporting directly to the Chief Revenue Officer, you will lead the team to identify, pursue, and close strategic partnerships across payroll providers, benefits brokers, accountants, financial institutions, PEOs, and embedded fintech distribution.

This is a leadership role focused on building, scaling, and driving the strategic partnership ecosystem. While hands-on, the focus is on organizational strategy, team mentorship, and driving cross-functional success. You will be responsible for signing complex, multi-year agreements with some of Human Interest’s largest and most important partners.

The role is equal parts strategist, dealmaker, and operator. You'll be just as comfortable modeling the economics of a new channel as you are in a room negotiating terms, and just as effective driving a deal across the finish line as you are shaping the partnership thesis with the CRO and the broader leadership team.

The person who thrives here is a natural hunter — energized by the pursuit of net-new relationships, comfortable opening doors cold, and relentless about carrying complex, multi-stakeholder deals through long sales cycles. You bring executive presence and the systems thinking to see how a single partnership fits into a broader distribution strategy. You read a term sheet and a partnership thesis with equal fluency, you make sharp prioritization calls about where to spend your time, and you carry deals with a sense of ownership. Above all, you are a builder: you're drawn to the ambiguity of standing up new channels from scratch, and you bring structure, pace, and judgment to a function that is still writing its own playbook.

About the team

The Partnerships organization is the engine behind Human Interest's reach, with over 95% of our business coming from our partner ecosystem. This team builds the relationships that let us scale access to retirement benefits far faster than we could one employer at a time. They think in systems and incentives: which partners share our mission, how we make those partners successful, and how we design programs that compound over time.

The team works shoulder-to-shoulder with Sales, Product, Marketing, Legal, and Operations to establish and launch partnerships that are commercially sound, operationally clean, and genuinely good for the businesses we ultimately serve. As we continue to scale, we're looking for a leader who can take this function to its next level: bigger partners, deeper integrations, and a measurable line on the revenue plan.

What you get to do every day

• Team Leadership & Mentorship: Coach, mentor, and develop a high-performing team of partnership professionals, fostering a culture of ownership, strategic thinking, and high-quality deal execution.

• Strategic Organizational Scaling: Design and implement scalable partnership processes, playbooks, and systems that allow the team to efficiently manage growth and long-term partner success.

• Market Intelligence: Maintain a sharp view of the retirement, payroll, fintech, and benefits landscape, surfacing competitive and regulatory shifts that should shape the partnership roadmap.

What you bring to the role

• Partnerships & Business Development Expertise: 10+ years in partnerships, business development, or channel sales, with a track record of personally owning and growing a book of strategic partnerships.

• Leadership Experience: 5+ years experience building, coaching, and scaling high-performing teams, with a track record of enabling others to achieve revenue targets.

• Proven Dealmaking: Demonstrated history of sourcing, structuring, and closing complex, high-value partnership and distribution agreements with measurable revenue impact.

• Domain Fluency: Deep experience in fintech, retirement / wealth, payroll, benefits, or an adjacent financial-services ecosystem, with a working understanding of how these distribution channels actually buy and sell.

• Builder's Mindset: Thrives in a fast-paced, scaling environment; brings structure to ambiguity and is energized by standing up new motions from scratch.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, LSP Platform
jobs.location: Brooklyn, NY; Washington, DC; Boston, MA
jobs.description:
Altana is the network for trusted trade. Our AI-powered product network empowers governments and businesses to build a more resilient and secure global economy while keeping trade flowing.

The Opportunity at Altana

About the Team

Logistics Service Providers (LSPs) sit at the center of global trade. Freight forwarders, customs brokers, carriers, and 3PLs touch millions of shipments and connect shippers, suppliers, and governments. The LSP Platform team builds the products that enable keeping up with the rapid pace of government regulation, and modernizing the business processes by engaging in Altana's network. With these tools, LSPs can run a fully agentic, collaborative and cutting edge customs process covering everything needed to screen and clear shipments faster, protect their customers from risk and delays, and offer new trade intelligence services to the shippers they serve.

About the Role

As Senior Product Manager for the LSP Platform, you'll own the roadmap for one of Altana's most strategic product areas. You'll work directly with some of the world's largest logistics companies to understand how goods move, where compliance and risk create friction, and how Altana can remove it. Your job is to embed Altana into the daily workflows of LSPs so it works as a native capability. You'll also turn LSPs into multipliers for the Altana network.

You'll partner with engineering, design, data science, and our go-to-market teams to ship features that make a measurable difference for customers. You'll be accountable for adoption, usage, and customer outcomes.

You Will

• Define the roadmap for Altana's LSP products, balancing near-term customer commitments with long-term platform bets.

• Build a deep understanding of LSP business models, operations, and customer relationships across forwarding, brokerage, and carriage, and turn that into clear product priorities.

• Set success metrics tied to customer impact, such as fewer holds and detentions, faster clearance, lower compliance cost, and new revenue for LSPs. Track progress against them.

• Obsess over the end-user experience of brokers, compliance analysts, and operations teams who work at high volume under time pressure.

• Work with our Enterprise and Public Sector product teams so that what shippers submit, what LSPs process, and what governments receive tells a coherent, trusted story.

• Spend real time with customers through discovery, design partnerships, pilots, and post-launch feedback. Bring that insight back to the team.

• Write clear requirements engineers can build from, and prototype with AI to test ideas before production code is written.

Who you are

You've shipped B2B products that customers rely on. You have 3+ years of product management experience, ideally on data-intensive, API-driven, or workflow products for enterprise customers.

You're relentlessly curious. You don't need to arrive as a logistics expert, but you're eager to become one. You love learning how a complex industry really works: the people, the incentives, the systems, and the workarounds nobody writes down. You ask the next question and the one after that.

You want to be side by side with customers. You'd rather sit next to a broker clearing a shipment than read a summary of the problem. You build trust with customers by showing up, listening closely, and coming back with something that works. You treat them as partners in building the product.

You own and drive outcomes. Shipping a feature is the start, not the finish. You define success by the difference you make for customers, track it, and keep iterating until the product delivers. When something isn't working, you take ownership and fix it.

You're technical enough to own the plumbing. You're comfortable with using AI in your daily workflow for prototyping and even code contributions, and you understand APIs, EDI, ETL/ELT, JSON, and integration architecture, and can go deep with engineers and customer IT teams.

You're obsessed with UX. You hate clunky integrations and high-friction workflows, and believe complex processes can feel simple.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience at an early-stage or high-growth company, where you defined a product area from ambiguity rather than inheriting a mature roadmap.

• A track record of embedded customer work, such as design partnerships, pilots, or on-site discovery, that shaped what you built and led to measurable adoption.

• Experience building platform, API, or integration products where success depended on fitting into customers' existing systems and workflows.

• Comfort working with data-heavy or AI/ML-driven products, including turning complex model outputs into decisions users can act on with confidence.

• Exposure to logistics, freight, customs, trade compliance, or supply chain technology is a plus, but not required. We care more about how quickly you learn than what you already know.

• Experience with products serving multiple stakeholders with competing incentives (e.g., marketplaces, networks, or multi-party workflows) is a strong plus.

This role can be based in Brooklyn, NY, Boston, MA or Washington, D.C., with hybrid work flexibility

US Salary Range and Benefits

185,000-220,000 USD

The salary range, to the extent specified for this role, is a good faith statement of the minimum and maximum levels of the annual based salary for the position. The base salary offered to a successful candidate will depend on a wide range of compensation factors, including, but not limited to, work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Altana's total compensation package. Altana also offers either a discretionary bonus or a variable compensation plan depending on the role. Additionally, Altana offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

• Flexible Time Off: Altana operates with a Flexible Time Off (FTO) policy that gives you agency over your own time off so you can maximize your work-life balance.

• Parental Leave: We offer industry leading Paid Parental Leave (PPL), providing 14 weeks of leave for non-birthing, adoptive, and foster parents and up to 26 weeks of leave for birthing parents, all paid at 100% of your base salary.

• Health Benefits: We have a full suite of medical, vision, and dental benefits with generous employer contributions, designed to give you flexibility and choice for your individual health situation. Our high deductible health plan is 100% employer paid for employees and supplemented with an employer contribution to your Health Savings Account (HSA). There is also a Flexible Spending Account (FSA) option.

• Supplemental Benefits: Altana provides life, short- and long-term disability, and AD&D insurance coverage, all at no cost to you, so you know that you and your loved ones are covered in case of an emergency.

• 401(k) Savings: Save for and invest in your future using our Guideline 401(k) retirement savings program.

• Commuter Benefits: Save money on your commute by setting aside pre-tax funds for public transit or parking!

• Wellness: Because we value mental and emotional health, every Altana employee has access to a free premium subscription to Calm, the #1 app for meditation, sleep, and mindfulness.

• Pet Insurance: Pets are family too! Keep them healthy with Wishbone insurance and/or our Total Pet vet service and telehealth discount plan.

• Employee Assistance Program: Free access to confidential personal support.

• Dependent Care FSA: You will have access to a Dependent Care FSA, which allows you to set aside pre-tax funds for childcare expenses.

The recruiter assigned to this role can share more information about the specific compensation and benefit details associated with this role during the hiring process.

Our Values

Our values are the core beliefs that shape who we are, what we stand for, and how we behave.They form the foundation of Altana’s culture and integrity and guide how we hire, design, build, and connect with each other and our customers.

• Trust: Our customers and partners entrust us with missions of the highest importance. We honor that by keeping our word, meeting commitments, and ensuring every action we take reinforces confidence in us. We rely on each other to deliver, to speak openly, and to hold ourselves accountable.

• Resilience: In a world of uncertainty and complexity, our work must withstand challenges, evolve with conditions, and ensure reliability over time. Resilience is both how we operate and what we deliver. It’s how we respond when things don’t go to plan –– we adapt, we support each other, and we keep moving forward.

• Stewardship: We are stewards of every mission we touch. Because our work impacts lives and futures, we hold ourselves accountable to delivering mission impact and never compromising. Our responsibility extends beyond individual projects to the broader system of global trade. We believe that stewardship starts from within so that we can bring focus, creativity, and excellence to our work. Each of us is personally responsible for fostering a workplace where people can thrive. And we are stewards of the greater good of the company. By holding ourselves and each other accountable, we build a culture of innovation and collective success that reflects the scale of our mission.

• Courage: Courage is what unlocks the seemingly impossible for our customers. It’s the core value that drives us make bold moves and take on big, complicated network problems—the ones others avoid. We know success isn't guaranteed, but we have the audacious vision to believe a solution is possible and to build it. Courage fuels our growth mindset. It means embracing challenges that make us stronger, and it’s demonstrated by how we approach hard conversations and complex projects.

At Altana, we believe that a diverse workforce enables greater creativity, performance, and adaptability. We’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer and welcome you to join us as you are. Our employment opportunities and decisions are based on business needs and individual qualifications, without regard to race, color, religious creed, national origin, ancestry, age, physical or mental disability, medical condition, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, genetic information, family care or medical leave status, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by the laws or regulations in the areas in which we operate. We prohibit discrimination and harassment of any type, in any situation.

Offers related to employment at Altana will come from an Altana.ai email address. We will never ask for payment as part of the interview or onboarding process.

Who We Are

Oportun (Nasdaq: OPRT) is a mission-driven financial services company that puts its members' financial goals within reach. With intelligent borrowing, savings, and budgeting capabilities, Oportun empowers members with the confidence to build a better financial future. Since inception, Oportun has provided more than $22.7 billion in responsible and affordable credit, saved its members more than $2.5 billion in interest and fees, and helped its members set aside an average of more than $1,800 annually.

The Opportunity

Oportun is currently seeking qualified candidates with customer service, cashier, sales, or hospitality experience to work Full-Time. At Oportun, we consider our customers to be our members, and the primary focus of our Member Loyalty Representatives is to create and generate a rewarding and unique member service experience.

Our Member Loyalty Representatives are passionate about listening, helping, and connecting with people at all touchpoints, such as in our stores and in the communities around our stores through personal outreach activities. As a key member of our team, you will make the mission of Oportun come to life by educating our members and communities about our inclusive, affordable financial services that empower them to build a better future.

At Oportun, we move fast and we hold each other to a high bar. If you care about doing your best work while actually moving the needle for real people, you'll fit right in.

What You'll Do

Your day-to-day

• Welcome members with a warm greeting and provide quality member service.

• Seamlessly process all transactions, while following company policies & procedures and protecting our members’ information.

• Work as a team or independently, including time alone in the store without direct supervision or with coworkers, while exceeding daily goals in our lending and servicing activities.
